children.title: Fixed Variable Elimination
children.top_down_role: Removal of variables whose lower and upper bounds coincide.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed Variable Elimination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact elimination of variables fixed by equal bounds or prior presolve deductions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the linear program 
\[\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\;\ell\le x\le u\}.\]
Partition the indices as \(F\cup R\), where every \(j\in F\) is fixed at \(x_j=v_j\). First verify \(\ell_F\le v_F\le u_F\). Replace the equality system by \(A_Rx_R=b-A_Fv_F\), retain the bounds \(\ell_R\le x_R\le u_R\), and replace the objective by \(c_R^{\mathsf T}x_R+c_F^{\mathsf T}v_F\). Solve the reduced problem and recover \(x_F=v_F\). If a fixed value violates its bounds, or the reduced equality system is inconsistent, report infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Substitute every fixed value into the constraints and objective, solve for the remaining variables, then restore the fixed coordinates.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n},\ b\in\mathbb R^m,\ c,\ell,u\in\mathbb R^n\)
\(F\cap R=\varnothing\) and \(F\cup R=\{1,\ldots,n\}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_R\mapsto (v_F,x_R)\) preserves feasibility and objective values up to the constant \(c_F^{\mathsf T}v_F\).

notation.meaning: Fixed and retained variable index sets.

children.title: Forced Variable Identification
children.top_down_role: Detection of variable values implied by rows, bounds, or feasibility structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Forced Variable Identification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact predicates that force one coordinate to a unique feasible value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A variable \(x_j\) is forced to \(v_j\) if the current constraints imply \(x_j=v_j\). Two directly verifiable cases are: \(\ell_j=u_j=v_j\); or an equality row has \(a_{ij}\ne0\), \(a_{ik}=0\) for every \(k\ne j\), and hence \(v_j=b_i/a_{ij}\). In the singleton-row case, feasibility additionally requires \(\ell_j\le v_j\le u_j\). More generally, any sound implied bounds \(L_j,U_j\) force the variable when \(L_j=U_j=v_j\). A contradiction occurs when \(L_j>U_j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A variable is forced when valid implied lower and upper bounds coincide; equal bounds and singleton equality rows provide directly checkable cases.
assumptions_latex: \(Ax=b\) and \(\ell\le x\le u\) describe the current presolved feasible set
\(L_j\le x_j\le U_j\) are valid implied bounds
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_j=U_j=v_j\Rightarrow x_j=v_j\) for every feasible \(x\).

notation.meaning: Valid implied bounds for variable j.
Row i of the equality matrix.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Implied bounds for one variable obtained from a bounded equality row.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For an equality row \(\sum_k a_{ik}x_k=b_i\), define \(q^-_{ij}=\sum_{k
e j}\min\{a_{ik}\ell_k,a_{ik}u_k\}\) and \(q^+_{ij}=\sum_{k
e j}\max\{a_{ik}\ell_k,a_{ik}u_k\}\). If \(a_{ij}
e0\), division of \([b_i-q^+_{ij},b_i-q^-_{ij}]\) by \(a_{ij}\), with endpoints reordered when necessary, gives a valid interval \(I_{ij}\) for \(x_j\). Intersect \(I_{ij}\) with \([\ell_j,u_j]\): a singleton forces \(x_j\), while an empty intersection certifies infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bound the activity of the other row terms and divide the residual interval by the target coefficient; a singleton intersection forces the variable and an empty one proves infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(\ell_k,u_k\in\mathbb R\) for every \(k\ne j\) with \(a_{ik}\ne0\)
\(\ell_k\le x_k\le u_k\) are valid bounds
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_j\in I_{ij}\cap[\ell_j,u_j]\).

notation.meaning: Minimum and maximum activity of row i excluding variable j.

knowledge_statements.title: Equality-Row Activity Bounds for Forcing

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between logical implication and tolerance-based numerical fixing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Valid implied bounds \(L_j\le x_j\le U_j\) force a value from those bounds alone only when \(L_j=U_j\). If \(L_j<U_j\), an arbitrarily small width \(U_j-L_j\) is not an exact equality certificate. Fixing from \(U_j-L_j\le\varepsilon\) is therefore an inexact reduction unless a declared perturbation model or an independent exact equality certificate justifies it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nearly coincident bounds do not exactly fix a variable without an additional certificate or an explicit perturbation model.
assumptions_latex: \(L_j\le x_j\le U_j\) are valid implied bounds
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \([L_j,U_j]\) is not a singleton and does not by itself imply \(x_j=v\).
knowledge_statements.title: Near-Equality Is Not Exact Forcing

children.title: Variable-Recovery Records
children.top_down_role: Presolve records needed to restore eliminated variable values.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Recovery Records
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine reconstruction data retained when presolve removes variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A variable-recovery record for eliminated coordinates \(F\) is an affine map
\[x_F=Tx_R+d,\]
together with the index ordering used by \(F\) and \(R\). For simple fixing, \(T=0\) and \(d=v_F\); for substitution, the appropriate row of \(T\) and entry of \(d\) store the substitution coefficients. Records are applied in reverse elimination order. If each reduction was exact, composing the records gives a map \(\mathcal R\) such that every reduced feasible solution \(z\) reconstructs an original feasible solution \(x=\mathcal R(z)\) with the recorded objective offset restored.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Store each eliminated variable as an affine function of retained variables, then apply records backward to reconstruct an original solution.
assumptions_latex: Each recorded elimination is an exact affine substitution
Index sets and objective offsets are retained without permutation ambiguity
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z\in P_{\mathrm{red}}\Rightarrow \mathcal R(z)\in P\), with the original objective obtained by restoring recorded constants.

notation.meaning: Composition of recovery records in reverse order.

children.title: Barrier Geometry After Variable Removal
children.top_down_role: Interior-geometry effects caused by fixed-variable or forced-variable reductions.

knowledge_statements.title: Barrier Geometry After Variable Removal
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relative-interior barrier induced after exact variable fixing and removal of constraints constant on the reduced affine hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b,\;Gx\le h,\;x_F=v_F\}\) be nonempty, let \(R=\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus F\), and write \(x_R=z\). Its reduced affine hull is \(H=\{z:A_Rz=b-A_Fv_F\}\), and the restricted slack of inequality \(q\) is \(s_q(z)=h_q-g_{qF}^{\mathsf T}v_F-g_{qR}^{\mathsf T}z\). Inequalities with \(s_q\equiv0\) on \(H\) are active throughout the reduced set and are omitted from its relative-interior barrier. Inequalities with positive constant slack contribute only additive constants and may also be omitted. If \(J\) indexes the remaining inequalities, then the reduced logarithmic barrier is \[\widehat\phi(z)=-\sum_{q\in J}\log s_q(z)\] on \(\{z\in H:s_q(z)>0\text{ for every }q\in J\}\). Barrier terms for fixed bound coordinates are removed rather than evaluated at zero slack.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After fixed coordinates are removed, construct the barrier on the reduced set's relative interior: omit inequalities active everywhere, discard positive constant terms up to an additive constant, and retain logarithms of the remaining positive slacks.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\ne\varnothing\)
Every inequality retained in \(J\) has positive slack at some point of the reduced relative interior
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat\phi\) is the logarithmic barrier on the relative interior of the reduced feasible set, up to omitted additive constants.

notation.meaning: Affine hull determined by the reduced equalities.
Slack of inequality q after fixed-variable substitution.
Indices of inequalities having nonconstant restricted slack.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gradient and Hessian geometry of the relative-interior barrier in intrinsic coordinates after variable removal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After fixed-variable removal, barrier gradients and Hessians pull back to the reduced affine hull; fixed coordinates and constant slacks contribute no intrinsic curvature.
assumptions_latex: \(z=z_0+Ny\) parameterizes the reduced affine hull
\(N\) has full column rank
\(s_q(z)>0\) for every \(q\in J\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nabla^2\psi=N^{\mathsf T}\nabla^2\widehat\phi N\), with intrinsic curvature contributed only by nonconstant retained slacks.

notation.meaning: Basis matrix for directions in the reduced affine hull.

children.title: Singleton Row Reductions
children.top_down_role: Presolve treatment of constraints containing a single active variable.

knowledge_statements.title: Singleton Row Reductions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Presolve of an equality row containing exactly one nonzero coefficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For an equality row \(i\) with \(a_{ij}
e0\) and \(a_{ik}=0\) for all \(k
e j\), compute \(v_j=b_i/a_{ij}\). If \(v_j
otin[\ell_j,u_j]\), declare the linear program infeasible. Otherwise fix \(x_j=v_j\), delete row \(i\), substitute \(v_j\) into every remaining row containing column \(j\), add \(c_jv_j\) to the objective constant, and delete column \(j\). Store \(x_j=v_j\) as a recovery record. The reduction preserves the feasible solutions projected onto the remaining coordinates and preserves objective values after adding the constant offset.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A singleton equality row fixes its sole variable; an out-of-bounds value proves infeasibility, otherwise the row and variable are eliminated.
assumptions_latex: \(\operatorname{supp}(a_{i\cdot})=\{j\}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_j=b_i/a_{ij}\), followed either by an infeasibility report or exact elimination.

notation.meaning: Indices of nonzeros in row i.
Value forced by the singleton row.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conversion of a one-variable inequality or ranged row into variable-bound tightening.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a row has the form \(L_i\le a_{ij}x_j\le U_i\), where \(a_{ij}\ne0\) and either endpoint may be infinite. Dividing by \(a_{ij}\), with endpoint order reversed when \(a_{ij}<0\), yields an implied interval \([\widehat\ell_j,\widehat u_j]\). Replace the current bounds by \(\ell'_j=\max\{\ell_j,\widehat\ell_j\}\) and \(u'_j=\min\{u_j,\widehat u_j\}\). If \(\ell'_j>u'_j\), the model is infeasible; otherwise delete the singleton row because its restriction is exactly represented by the tightened bounds. The case \(L_i=U_i\) is the forced-value variant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A singleton inequality or ranged row becomes a bound on its sole variable; intersect it with the existing interval, report infeasibility if empty, and otherwise delete the row.
assumptions_latex: \(a_{ik}=0\) for every \(k\ne j\)
\(L_i\le U_i\) in the extended real line
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \([\ell'_j,u'_j]=[\ell_j,u_j]\cap[\widehat\ell_j,\widehat u_j]\); emptiness proves infeasibility, while a nonempty intersection permits exact row deletion after bound tightening.

notation.meaning: Lower and upper activity bounds of the singleton row.
Variable bounds implied by the singleton row.

knowledge_statements.title: Singleton Inequality and Ranged-Row Reduction

children.title: Singleton Column Reductions
children.top_down_role: Presolve treatment of variables appearing in a single active constraint.

knowledge_statements.title: Singleton Column Reductions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact elimination through a free variable appearing in one equality row.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose column \(j\) occurs only in equality row \(i\), with \(a_{ij}\ne0\), and \(x_j\) is free. Solve that row as
\[x_j=\frac{b_i-\sum_{k\ne j}a_{ik}x_k}{a_{ij}}.\]
Delete row \(i\) and column \(j\). Replace each remaining objective coefficient by \(c'_k=c_k-c_ja_{ik}/a_{ij}\), and add \(c_jb_i/a_{ij}\) to the objective constant. Other equality rows are unchanged because their column-\(j\) entries vanish. Store the displayed affine formula for recovery. With finite bounds on \(x_j\), this reduction is invalid unless the substituted bounds are retained as equivalent constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A free variable appearing in one equality can satisfy that row and be eliminated, with objective coefficients adjusted and an affine recovery formula stored.
assumptions_latex: \(a_{ij}\ne0\) and \(a_{hj}=0\) for every \(h\ne i\)
\(\ell_j=-\infty\) and \(u_j=+\infty\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reduced problem is equivalent under the displayed recovery substitution and objective constant shift.

notation.meaning: Singleton row position and singleton column index.
Objective coefficient after eliminating the singleton column.

children.title: Variable Substitution
children.top_down_role: Elimination through recoverable variable replacement.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable Substitution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-pivot substitution producing an equivalent reduced linear program and an affine recovery rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose an equality row \(i\) and pivot variable \(x_j\) with \(a_{ij}
e0\), and solve the row as \[x_j= rac{b_i}{a_{ij}}-\sum_{k
e j} rac{a_{ik}}{a_{ij}}x_k.\] For every other equality row \(h
e i\), set \(a'_{hk}=a_{hk}-a_{hj}a_{ik}/a_{ij}\) and \(b'_h=b_h-a_{hj}b_i/a_{ij}\). Set \(c'_k=c_k-c_ja_{ik}/a_{ij}\) and add \(c_jb_i/a_{ij}\) to the objective constant. Delete row \(i\) and column \(j\), retain as equivalent constraints every bound on \(x_j\) after applying the displayed substitution, and store that formula as the recovery record.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pivot on a nonzero equality coefficient, substitute the solved variable throughout the model and objective, retain all induced bound constraints, and store its affine reconstruction formula.
assumptions_latex: Every finite bound on \(x_j\) is converted into its equivalent constraint after substitution
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The retained substitution formula defines a bijection between the original feasible solutions and the reduced feasible solutions and preserves objective values after restoration of the recorded constant.

children.title: Substitution Fill Control
children.top_down_role: Sparsity costs that limit otherwise valid substitutions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation of algebraic validity from implementation-specific sparsity acceptance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be any prescribed fill metric computed from the predicted post-substitution matrix, such as added nonzeros, maximum row density, or a weighted combination, and let \(B\) be its implementation-selected limit. An exact substitution may be accepted when \(M\le B\) and skipped when \(M>B\). This decision affects the size and sparsity of the presolved model but not the algebraic validity of the substitution: accepting it remains equivalent when all induced constraints and recovery data are retained, while rejecting it simply leaves the original row and variable in the model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fill thresholds decide whether an exact substitution is computationally desirable, not whether it is mathematically valid.
assumptions_latex: The proposed substitution is algebraically valid
\(M\) and \(B\) are fixed by the implementation policy
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The predicate \(M\le B\) is an efficiency safeguard; it is not an equivalence or feasibility condition.
knowledge_statements.title: Policy Separation for Fill-Limited Substitution

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sparse family in which one algebraically valid substitution creates a dense row-by-column block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let pivot row \(i\) contain the pivot coefficient \(a_{ij}\ne0\) and \(p\) additional nonzeros in columns \(T\). Let the pivot column \(j\) occur in \(q\) other rows, each having no coefficient in \(T\). If coefficients are chosen so that no post-substitution cancellation occurs, eliminating \(x_j\) introduces all \(p\) columns of \(T\) into each of those \(q\) rows, producing \(pq\) new nonzeros relative to deleting the pivot row and column alone. Thus a sparse pivot row and column can generate a dense \(q\)-by-\(p\) block.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pivot row with p other variables and a pivot column present in q other rows can create pq new nonzeros.
assumptions_latex: The pivot column occurs in exactly \(q\) other rows
Affected rows initially have no entries in \(T\)
No substitution cancellation occurs
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Delta N=pq\) for this family.

notation.meaning: Nonpivot columns present in the pivot row.
Pivot-row width excluding j and number of other rows containing j.

knowledge_statements.title: Bipartite Fill Growth Under Substitution

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coefficient-level and support-level accounting of fill caused by an equality-pivot substitution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a pivot \((i,j)\) with \(a_{ij}
e0\), every affected row \(h
e i\) has post-substitution coefficients \(a'_{hk}=a_{hk}-a_{hj}a_{ik}/a_{ij}\) for \(k
e j\). If \(S_h=\operatorname{supp}(a_{h\cdot})\), then \(\operatorname{supp}(a'_{h\cdot})\subseteq(S_h\setminus\{j\})\cup(S_i\setminus\{j\})\), with strict inclusion possible through cancellation. Relative to merely deleting row \(i\) and column \(j\), the exact matrix fill change is \[\Delta N=\sum_{h
e i}\left(|\operatorname{supp}(a'_{h\cdot})|-|S_h\setminus\{j\}|ight),\] where unaffected rows contribute zero. Symbolic estimates that ignore cancellations are upper estimates rather than exact fill counts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Substitution can introduce every pivot-row variable into each row containing the pivot column; exact fill uses the updated coefficients, while support unions give cancellation-blind upper estimates.
assumptions_latex: Supports are computed over the active equality matrix
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{supp}(a'_{h\cdot})\subseteq(S_h\setminus\{j\})\cup(S_i\setminus\{j\})\), and \(\Delta N\) gives the exact nonzero-count change after substitution.

notation.meaning: Support of equality row h before substitution.
Exact change in matrix nonzeros relative to row-and-column deletion alone.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Substitution Fill Accounting
Substitution Fill Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A policy-dependent sparsity safeguard for accepting an otherwise exact substitution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a proposed pivot \((i,j)\), form the symbolic post-substitution supports \(S'_h\) using \[S'_h\subseteq\bigl(S_h\setminus\{j\}\bigr)\cup\bigl(S_i\setminus\{j\}\bigr)\qquad\text{for every }h\ne i\text{ with }j\in S_h,\] accounting for numerical cancellations when coefficient values are available. Let \(N_0\) be the nonzero count after merely deleting row \(i\) and column \(j\), and let \(N_1\) be the predicted nonzero count after substitution. Given a fill budget \(B\ge0\) and row-density limit \(D\ge0\), accept the substitution only if \(N_1-N_0\le B\) and \(\max_{h\ne i}|S'_h|\le D\). These predicates control sparsity costs but are not required for mathematical equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accept a proposed substitution only when its predicted added nonzeros and maximum resulting row density satisfy the prescribed implementation limits.
assumptions_latex: \(B\ge0\) and \(D\ge0\) are prescribed sparsity limits
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_1-N_0\le B\) and \(\max_{h\ne i}|S'_h|\le D\) are the selected acceptance predicates.

notation.meaning: Row supports before and after the proposed substitution.
Baseline and predicted post-substitution nonzero counts.

children.title: Redundant Constraint Removal
children.top_down_role: Removal of constraints that add no effective restriction to the presolved model.

knowledge_statements.title: Redundant Constraint Removal
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact removal of an equality implied by retained equality rows, with an inconsistency branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the equality system \(Ax=b\), suppose row \(i\) satisfies \[a_{i\cdot}=\sum_{k\in K}\alpha_k a_{k\cdot},\] where \(K\subseteq\{1,ldots,m\}\setminus\{i\}\). Compute \(r_i=b_i-\sum_{k\in K}\alpha_kb_k\). If \(r_i=0\), delete row \(i\), since it is implied by rows \(K\). If \(r_i\ne0\), report infeasibility. Retain the coefficients \((\alpha_k)_{k\in K}\) whenever dual multipliers or infeasibility certificates must later be reconstructed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Express the candidate row through retained rows, compare the corresponding right-hand sides, remove the row if they match, and report infeasibility otherwise.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\setminus\{i\}\)
\(a_{i\cdot}=\sum_{k\in K}\alpha_k a_{k\cdot}\) is an exact dependence
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_i=0\) permits exact row removal without changing the feasible set, whereas \(r_i\ne0\) implies \(\{x:Ax=b\}=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: Dependence coefficients for the candidate row.
Right-hand-side residual under the row dependence.

children.title: Linear Dependency Detection
children.top_down_role: Identification of dependent row or column structures before barrier linear algebra.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear Dependency Detection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Null-space certificates for dependent or inconsistent equality rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), a nonzero vector \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^m\) satisfying \(A^{\mathsf T}\lambda=0\) certifies a linear dependence among the rows of \(A\). Applied to \(Ax=b\), if additionally \(\lambda^{\mathsf T}b\ne0\), no feasible \(x\) exists because every feasible point would satisfy \(0=\lambda^{\mathsf T}Ax=\lambda^{\mathsf T}b\). If \(\lambda^{\mathsf T}b=0\), the certificate establishes dependency but not inconsistency; a row with a nonzero component of \(\lambda\) can be expressed through the others and considered for exact removal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonzero left-null vector detects dependent rows; a nonzero product with the right-hand side is an infeasibility certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\)
\(\lambda\ne0\) and \(A^{\mathsf T}\lambda=0\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda^{\mathsf T}b\ne0\Rightarrow\{x:Ax=b\}=\varnothing\); otherwise \(\lambda\) certifies row dependence.

source_refs.locator: Rank of the Matrix \( A \) p. 31

source_witnesses.locator: Rank of the Matrix \( A \) p. 31

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent algebraic characterizations and exact-factorization detection of dependent equality rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), the following are equivalent: \(\operatorname{rank}(A)<m\); the rows of \(A\) are linearly dependent; \(\ker(A^{\mathsf T})\ne\{0\}\); and \(AA^{\mathsf T}\) is singular. If an exact rank factorization \(A=UV\), with \(U\in\mathbb R^{m\times r}\) full column rank and \(V\in\mathbb R^{r\times n}\) full row rank, has \(r<m\), then \(\ker(U^{\mathsf T})=\ker(A^{\mathsf T})\). Moreover, \(Ax=b\) is consistent if and only if \(b\in\operatorname{range}(A)\), equivalently \(\lambda^{\mathsf T}b=0\) for every \(\lambda\in\ker(A^{\mathsf T})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Row dependence is equivalently rank loss, a nontrivial left null space, or singularity of the row Gram matrix; a left-null basis gives every compatibility condition on the right-hand side.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\)
Any asserted factorization and rank are exact
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}(A)<m\iff\ker(A^{\mathsf T})\ne\{0\}\iff AA^{\mathsf T}\text{ is singular}\), and \(Ax=b\) is consistent iff \(b\perp\ker(A^{\mathsf T})\).

notation.meaning: Left null space containing all row-dependence coefficient vectors.

knowledge_statements.title: Equivalent Exact Row-Dependence Tests

children.title: Rank-Revealing Reduction Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Numerical limits on declaring structural dependence.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Revealing Reduction Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numerical rank decisions become tolerance-dependent near singularity and do not alone certify exact redundancy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Exact row removal requires an exact dependence, whereas floating-point rank revelation uses a threshold. For \[A_\varepsilon=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&\varepsilon\end{pmatrix},\qquad 0<\varepsilon<\tau\le1,\] the exact rank is two, while a rule declaring singular values strictly below \(\tau\) negligible reports numerical rank one. Removing the second row on this basis can enlarge the feasible set or conceal inconsistency in its right-hand side. Thus threshold-based rank revelation alone does not certify exact redundancy; uncertain rows require residual tests with scaling-aware tolerances, preservation as constraints, or an independently verifiable dependence certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matrix can be exactly full rank while a tolerance-based test reports a deficient numerical rank, so thresholding alone cannot justify exact row removal.
assumptions_latex: \(0<\varepsilon<\tau\le1\)
Numerical rank counts singular values that are not strictly below \(\tau\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}(A_\varepsilon)=2\) while the specified threshold rule reports numerical rank one.

notation.meaning: A diagonal matrix family approaching rank deficiency.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Scale Dependence of Absolute Rank Thresholds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of absolute singular-value thresholds to remain invariant under rescaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an absolute threshold \(\tau>0\), replacing \(A\) by \(\alpha A\) replaces every singular value by \(|\alpha|\sigma_k(A)\); hence the reported numerical rank can change although exact rank does not. A scale-aware rule may instead compare \(\sigma_k(A)\) with \(\tau_{\mathrm{abs}}+\tau_{\mathrm{rel}}\|A\|_2\), but even such a relative rule defines numerical rather than exact rank and cannot by itself certify exact row redundancy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Absolute rank thresholds are not invariant under rescaling; relative thresholds improve scale behavior but still do not certify exact dependence.
assumptions_latex: \(\alpha\ne0\)
Numerical rank is determined by thresholding singular values
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}(\alpha A)=\operatorname{rank}(A)\), while an absolute-threshold numerical rank may change with \(|\alpha|\).

notation.meaning: Absolute and relative components of a scale-aware threshold.

knowledge_statements.title: Scale Dependence of Absolute Rank Thresholds

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Singular-value separation required for a threshold rank decision to be invariant under bounded perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\widetilde A=A+E\) with \(\|E\|_2\le\eta\). Weyl's singular-value bound gives \(|\sigma_k(\widetilde A)-\sigma_k(A)|\le\eta\) for every defined singular value. Thus an observed rank-\(r\) split at threshold \(\tau\) is certified for every admissible \(A\) when \(\sigma_r(\widetilde A)>\tau+\eta\) and, when \(r<\min\{m,n\}\), \(\sigma_{r+1}(\widetilde A)<\tau-\eta\). A singular value in \([\tau-\eta,\tau+\eta]\) cannot support a perturbation-robust side-of-threshold declaration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A threshold numerical-rank decision is perturbation-stable only when the relevant singular values are separated from the threshold by the perturbation bound.
assumptions_latex: \(\widetilde A=A+E\)
\(\tau>\eta\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|\sigma_k(\widetilde A)-\sigma_k(A)|\le\eta\), and values within distance \(\eta\) of \(\tau\) are threshold-ambiguous.

notation.meaning: The kth singular value in nonincreasing order.

knowledge_statements.title: Perturbation-Stable Numerical Rank Boundary

children.title: Certificate Preservation Under Row Removal
children.top_down_role: Traceability requirements for certificates after redundant-row elimination.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Preservation Under Row Removal
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transformation of dual and infeasibility certificates after removing a dependent equality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:A_Kx=b_K,\;a_{i\cdot}x=b_i,\;x\ge0\}\), where \(a_{i\cdot}=\alpha^{\mathsf T}A_K\) and \(b_i=\alpha^{\mathsf T}b_K\). Any reduced dual certificate \((\bar y_K,s)\) satisfying \(A_K^{\mathsf T}\bar y_K+s=c\) lifts by setting \(y_i=0\). Conversely, an original dual certificate \((y_K,y_i,s)\) projects to \(\bar y_K=y_K+\alpha y_i\); then \(A_K^{\mathsf T}\bar y_K+s=c\) and \(b_K^{\mathsf T}\bar y_K=b_K^{\mathsf T}y_K+b_i y_i\). The same linear transformation maps left-null infeasibility certificates, so validity and certificate objective values are preserved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Store the removed row's dependence coefficients; they transform dual multipliers and left-null certificates without changing their validity or values.
assumptions_latex: \(a_{i\cdot}=\alpha^{\mathsf T}A_K\)
\(b_i=\alpha^{\mathsf T}b_K\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar y_K=y_K+\alpha y_i\) preserves dual feasibility and the dual objective, while \(y_i=0\) lifts reduced certificates.

notation.meaning: Dependence coefficients for the removed row.
Nonnegative dual slack for x greater than or equal to zero.

source_refs.locator: Rank of the Matrix \( A \) p. 31

source_witnesses.locator: Rank of the Matrix \( A \) p. 31

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block transformation of dual and left-null certificates when several dependent equalities are removed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition equality rows into retained rows \(K\) and removed rows \(D\), and suppose \(A_D=TA_K\) and \(b_D=Tb_K\). For any original multipliers \((y_K,y_D)\), define \(\bar y_K=y_K+T^{\mathsf T}y_D\). Then \(A_K^{\mathsf T}\bar y_K=A_K^{\mathsf T}y_K+A_D^{\mathsf T}y_D\) and \(b_K^{\mathsf T}\bar y_K=b_K^{\mathsf T}y_K+b_D^{\mathsf T}y_D\). Conversely, every reduced multiplier lifts by setting \(y_D=0\). Hence dual stationarity, dual objective values, and left-null infeasibility-certificate pairings are preserved under simultaneous exact row removal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Store the block dependence matrix for all removed rows; its transpose projects their multipliers onto retained rows without changing certificate values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar y_K=y_K+T^{\mathsf T}y_D\) preserves both coefficient combinations and right-hand-side pairings, while zero extension lifts reduced multipliers.

notation.meaning: retained and removed equality-row index sets
block dependence matrix expressing removed rows through retained rows

children.title: Bound Tightening
children.top_down_role: Strengthening explicit variable bounds before the barrier solve.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bound tightening from a finite ranged linear row.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(L\le a^{\mathsf T}x\le U\) and \(\ell\le x\le u\), fix \(j\) with \(a_j
e0\) and define \(m_{-j}=\sum_{i
e j}\min\{a_i\ell_i,a_i u_i\}\) and \(M_{-j}=\sum_{i
e j}\max\{a_i\ell_i,a_i u_i\}\). Every feasible point satisfies \(L-M_{-j}\le a_jx_j\le U-m_{-j}\). Dividing by \(a_j\), reversing the inequalities when \(a_j<0\), and intersecting with \([\ell_j,u_j]\) gives valid tightened bounds. An empty intersection certifies infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A ranged row tightens a variable from both endpoints using the minimum and maximum possible activity of all other variables.
assumptions_latex: \(L,U,m_{-j},M_{-j}\) are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Intersecting \([\ell_j,u_j]\) with the interval implied by \(L-M_{-j}\le a_jx_j\le U-m_{-j}\) preserves every feasible point.

notation.meaning: minimum and maximum activity of all variables except coordinate j

knowledge_statements.title: Two-Sided Row Bound Propagation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: When a row endpoint cannot produce a finite propagated bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A row endpoint yields a finite propagated bound on \(x_j\) only when the required extremal activity of the other variables is finite. If that residual activity is \(-\infty\) for an upper-row implication or \(+\infty\) for a lower-row implication, the corresponding calculation supplies no finite bound on \(x_j\); it does not certify infeasibility. Undefined expressions involving infinite bounds must be resolved by explicit extended-real activity rules rather than floating-point subtraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An infinite residual activity means that the row endpoint gives no finite bound in that direction, not that the model is infeasible.
assumptions_latex: Variable bounds may be infinite.
Row activities are evaluated using consistent extended-real conventions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Only finite residual activity justifies a finite propagated endpoint; absence of such an endpoint is an inconclusive propagation result.
knowledge_statements.title: Infinite Residual-Activity Boundary
Bound Tightening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-row interval propagation for a bounded linear inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given bounds \(\ell_i\le x_i\le u_i\) and a row \(a^\top x\le b\), process each index \(j\) with \(a_j\ne0\). Compute \(m_{-j}=\sum_{i\ne j}\min\{a_i\ell_i,a_i u_i\}\). Every row-feasible point satisfies \(a_jx_j\le b-m_{-j}\). If \(a_j>0\), replace \(u_j\) by \(\min\{u_j,(b-m_{-j})/a_j\}\); if \(a_j<0\), replace \(\ell_j\) by \(\max\{\ell_j,(b-m_{-j})/a_j\}\). Repeat over rows until no bound changes or a chosen tolerance is reached. Output the tightened box, or declare infeasibility if some \(\ell_j>u_j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Propagate each inequality through current variable bounds, intersect the resulting implied bounds with the box, and repeat until stable or infeasibility is exposed.
assumptions_latex: \(a^\top x\le b\) is imposed together with the current bounds.
All terms used in \(m_{-j}\) are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x: a^\top x\le b,\ \ell\le x\le u\}\) is unchanged by every accepted tightening.

notation.meaning: minimum contribution of variables other than j

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm and its invariance claim are mathematically coherent and fit Bound Tightening, but no inspectable source supports the propagation rule or infeasibility test.

children.title: Implied Bound Detection
children.top_down_role: Bounds inferred from constraint activity ranges.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear-combination certificates for coordinate bounds inferred from a polyhedral system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x:Gx\le h\}\ne\varnothing\). If \(\lambda\ge0\) satisfies \(G^{\mathsf T}\lambda=e_j\), then every \(x\in P\) satisfies \(x_j\le h^{\mathsf T}\lambda\). If \(\mu\ge0\) satisfies \(G^{\mathsf T}\mu=-e_j\), then every \(x\in P\) satisfies \(x_j\ge-h^{\mathsf T}\mu\). Whenever the corresponding coordinate-optimization LP has a finite optimum, linear-programming strong duality gives a multiplier attaining the tightest implied endpoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative combination of model inequalities certifies an implied coordinate bound; an optimal dual combination certifies the tightest finite endpoint.
assumptions_latex: \(P=\{x:Gx\le h\}\ne\varnothing\).
The relevant coordinate-optimization LP has a finite optimum when attainment of a tight endpoint is asserted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G^{\mathsf T}\lambda=e_j\Rightarrow x_j\le h^{\mathsf T}\lambda\) and \(G^{\mathsf T}\mu=-e_j\Rightarrow x_j\ge-h^{\mathsf T}\mu\) for every \(x\in P\).

notation.meaning: nonnegative multipliers certifying upper and lower coordinate bounds

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Certificates for Implied Bounds
Implied Bound Detection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact implied bounds obtained from auxiliary linear programs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b,\ \ell\le x\le u\}\) be nonempty. For each coordinate \(j\), define \(\underline\beta_j=\inf\{x_j:x\in P\}\) and \(\overline\beta_j=\sup\{x_j:x\in P\}\). Then every feasible point satisfies \(\underline\beta_j\le x_j\le\overline\beta_j\), and no strictly stronger valid coordinate bound exists. A finite optimum of the auxiliary minimization or maximization LP supplies the corresponding bound; an unbounded auxiliary LP supplies no finite bound. If \(\underline\beta_j=\overline\beta_j\), the variable is fixed throughout \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coordinate minimization and maximization over the feasible polyhedron produce the strongest possible implied lower and upper bounds.
assumptions_latex: \(P\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\subseteq\prod_{j=1}^n[\underline\beta_j,\overline\beta_j]\), with coordinatewise-tight endpoints.

notation.meaning: tightest implied bounds on coordinate j

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The auxiliary-LP characterization of coordinatewise-tight implied bounds is precise, but the nontrivial optimality and unboundedness claims have no citation.

children.title: Constraint Activity Screening
children.top_down_role: Classification of rows through attainable activity intervals.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact box-relative classification of a two-sided linear row.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\lambda\le a^{\mathsf T}x\le\upsilon\) over a box \(B\), let \(L(a)=\min_{x\in B}a^{\mathsf T}x\) and \(U(a)=\max_{x\in B}a^{\mathsf T}x\). The row is box-infeasible if and only if \(U(a)<\lambda\) or \(L(a)>\upsilon\); it is box-redundant if and only if \(\lambda\le L(a)\) and \(U(a)\le\upsilon\); and it is uniformly inactive relative to both finite endpoints if and only if \(\lambda<L(a)\le U(a)<\upsilon\). All remaining cases are unresolved relative to the box.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compare a ranged row's attainable activity interval with its permitted interval to classify infeasibility, redundancy, strict inactivity, or an unresolved case.
assumptions_latex: The row has two finite endpoints.
The activity endpoints \(L(a)\) and \(U(a)\) are well defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The relative positions of \([L(a),U(a)]\) and \([\lambda,\upsilon]\) give the stated exact box-relative classification.

notation.meaning: attainable activity interval over the box

knowledge_statements.title: Ranged-Row Activity Screening

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Activity screening when the current box has infinite endpoints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a box with possibly infinite endpoints, each row term has an extended-real minimum and maximum determined by the sign of its coefficient. Summing these terms gives \(L(a)\in\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty\}\) and \(U(a)\in\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) whenever no undefined arithmetic is introduced. The same interval comparisons used for finite activities remain valid; an infinite endpoint commonly leaves the corresponding redundancy or infeasibility test unresolved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Activity screening extends to infinite variable bounds using extended-real row minima and maxima; infinite activity usually makes one screening direction inconclusive.
assumptions_latex: Zero coefficients are omitted before combining coefficients with infinite variable bounds.
The activity sums contain no undefined combination of opposite infinities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Well-defined extended-real activity endpoints support the usual box-relative screening implications, while an unavailable finite comparison is inconclusive.
knowledge_statements.title: Extended-Real Activity Screening
Constraint Activity Screening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interval classification of one inequality over a current bound box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a row \(a^\top x\le b\) and box \(B=[\ell,u]\), define \(L(a)=\sum_i\min\{a_i\ell_i,a_i u_i\}\) and \(U(a)=\sum_i\max\{a_i\ell_i,a_i u_i\}\). The row is box-infeasible when \(L(a)>b\), box-redundant when \(U(a)\le b\), and unresolved when \(L(a)\le b<U(a)\). It is uniformly inactive when \(U(a)<b\). These classifications are exact relative to the box; unresolved does not assert that the row is active on the feasible set defined by the other constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimum and maximum row activity over the bound box screen an inequality as infeasible, redundant, uniformly inactive, or unresolved.
assumptions_latex: Every product defining \(L(a)\) and \(U(a)\) has a well-defined finite value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a^\top x\in[L(a),U(a)]\) for every \(x\in B\), yielding the stated screening cases.

notation.meaning: minimum row activity over the box
maximum row activity over the box

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The interval classification is mathematically consistent and appropriately scoped to the bound box, but it lacks an inspectable source.

children.title: Inactive Constraint Removal
children.top_down_role: Removal of constraints proven unable to become binding.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimization-based criterion for deleting one inequality relative to all remaining constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\ne\varnothing\) be the feasible set defined by all constraints except \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\), and set \(\rho=\sup\{a^{\mathsf T}x:x\in Q\}\). The row is redundant relative to \(Q\) if and only if \(\rho\le b\). It is uniformly strictly inactive if and only if \(\rho<b\). If \(\rho>b\), including \(\rho=+\infty\), deletion enlarges the feasible set. Thus a finite auxiliary maximization value at most \(b\) is an exact deletion certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximize the candidate row over the model without it: a value at most the right-hand side exactly certifies redundancy, and a strict inequality certifies uniform inactivity.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Q\subseteq\{x:a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\}\iff\sup_{x\in Q}a^{\mathsf T}x\le b.

notation.meaning: feasible set after omitting the candidate row

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Redundancy and Uniform-Inactivity Criterion
Inactive Constraint Removal
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe deletion of an inequality dominated by current valid bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\subseteq B=[\ell,u]\) be the feasible set defined by all constraints except \(a^\top x\le b\). If \(U(a)=\max_{x\in B}a^\top x\le b\), then \(a^\top x\le b\) holds for every \(x\in Q\). Consequently, deleting this row leaves the feasible set and every objective value unchanged. If \(U(a)<b\), the deleted row has positive slack at every point of \(Q\) and therefore cannot be active at any feasible solution. Equality \(U(a)=b\) proves redundancy but not uniform inactivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A row whose maximum activity over valid bounds does not exceed its right-hand side may be deleted without changing the LP.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\subseteq[\ell,u]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q=Q\cap\{x:a^\top x\le b\}\); if \(U(a)<b\), the row is strictly inactive on \(Q\).

notation.meaning: feasible set excluding the screened row
maximum row activity over the valid box

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The sufficient condition for safe row deletion and the distinction between redundancy and strict inactivity are correct in form, but no source is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-versus-Dual Form Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic criterion for choosing a barrier system before sparse factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the standard-form pair \(\min\{c^\top x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\) and \(\max\{b^\top y:A^\top y+s=c,\ s\ge0\}\), a strictly positive primal-dual iterate yields \(D=XS^{-1}\). Eliminating primal and slack directions gives the normal equation \((ADA^\top)\Delta y=r\), of order equal to the number of rows of \(A\); retaining coupled directions gives an augmented system involving both row and column variables. Form selection should preserve primal-dual equivalence and choose the representation whose scaled coefficient matrix is expected to produce the smaller, better-conditioned sparse factorization, rather than using dimension alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose an equivalent primal, dual, normal-equation, or augmented formulation by comparing scaled conditioning and predicted sparse-factorization cost.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reduced dual-direction matrix is \(ADA^\top\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\), while equivalent augmented formulations have different sparsity and conditioning.

notation.meaning: diagonal matrices formed from primal variables and dual slacks

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited primal-dual framework can support the normal-equation construction, but the supplied locator does not clearly support the broader formulation-selection principle involving conditioning, sparse fill, and predicted factorization cost.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Barrier noncoercivity caused by the redundant common-shift direction in a split free-variable lift.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed projected value \(x_j^+-x_j^-=\bar x\), every \(t>0\) gives the positive lift \((x_j^+,x_j^-)=(\max\{\bar x,0\}+t,\max\{-\bar x,0\}+t)\). If the transformed model depends on the pair only through its difference, this ray leaves all projected constraints and the linear objective unchanged, whereas \(-\mu\log x_j^+-\mu\log x_j^-\to-\infty\). Thus projection equivalence does not make the naive split-variable primal barrier well posed; the redundant direction must be removed or controlled, or the free variable handled natively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A split free variable has a common-shift ray, making a naive logarithmic barrier on both split variables unbounded below despite projection equivalence.
assumptions_latex: The transformed model depends on \((x_j^+,x_j^-)\) only through \(x_j^+-x_j^-\).
Both split variables receive ordinary positive-orthant logarithmic terms.
No additional constraint bounds the common-shift direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf_{x_j^+-x_j^-=\bar x,\;x_j^+,x_j^->0}-\mu(\log x_j^++\log x_j^-)=-\infty.

notation.meaning: nonnegative variables representing the free coordinate
fixed projected value of the original free variable

knowledge_statements.title: Split-Variable Barrier Noncoercivity
Free-Variable Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Split-variable representation of an unrestricted LP variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An unrestricted variable \(x_j\in\mathbb R\) may be replaced by \(x_j=x_j^+-x_j^-\) with \(x_j^+,x_j^-\ge0\). In every constraint and in the objective, replace the column \(a_j\) by the two columns \(a_j\) and \(-a_j\), and replace the cost \(c_j\) by \(c_j\) and \(-c_j\). Projection by \(x_j=x_j^+-x_j^-\) maps the transformed feasible set onto the original feasible set and preserves objective values. Conversely, every original value has a representative, for example \(x_j^+=\max\{x_j,0\}\) and \(x_j^-=\max\{-x_j,0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Represent a free variable as the difference of two nonnegative variables; projection recovers exactly the original feasible points and objective values.
assumptions_latex: The original model depends linearly on \(x_j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_j=x_j^+-x_j^-\) gives an objective-preserving projection from the split formulation to the original LP.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The split-variable representation and projection equivalence are standard and precise, but no inspectable citation is provided.

children.title: Bounded-Variable Formulations
children.top_down_role: Barrier representations for variables with finite lower or upper limits.

knowledge_statements.title: Bounded-Variable Formulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct logarithmic-barrier treatment of finite variable-bound endpoints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an LP with bounds \(\ell_i\le x_i\le u_i\), each finite lower endpoint contributes \(-\mu\log(x_i-\ell_i)\), and each finite upper endpoint contributes \(-\mu\log(u_i-x_i)\). When both endpoints are finite, the resulting gradient component is \(-\mu/(x_i-\ell_i)+\mu/(u_i-x_i)\), and the diagonal Hessian component is \(\mu/(x_i-\ell_i)^2+\mu/(u_i-x_i)^2\). A missing endpoint contributes no corresponding logarithm. Thus simple bounds can remain explicit without adding equality rows or slack variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each finite variable-bound endpoint can be handled directly by a logarithmic term, producing diagonal gradient and Hessian contributions without new equality rows or slack variables.
assumptions_latex: Every barrier iterate lies strictly inside each retained finite bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The bound-barrier Hessian is diagonal and positive in every coordinate having at least one finite retained endpoint.

source_refs.source_title: Interior Point Methods for Linear Optimization
source_refs.locator: 5.3 The primal logarithmic barrier function p. 90

source_witnesses.source_title: Interior Point Methods for Linear Optimization
source_witnesses.locator: 5.3 The primal logarithmic barrier function p. 90

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degenerate finite bounds in a direct logarithmic-bound formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\ell_i=u_i\), the constraint \(\ell_i\le x_i\le u_i\) fixes \(x_i\), but no point satisfies both \(x_i>\ell_i\) and \(x_i<u_i\). Hence \(-\mu\log(x_i-\ell_i)-\mu\log(u_i-x_i)\) has empty domain. The fixed coordinate must be eliminated or handled through a relative-interior formulation rather than treated as an ordinary box.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equal finite endpoints fix the variable and leave no strict box interior, so the ordinary two-endpoint logarithmic barrier is undefined.
assumptions_latex: \(\ell_i,u_i\in\mathbb R\).
The formulation retains logarithms for both finite endpoints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \ell_i=u_i\Longrightarrow\{x_i:\ell_i<x_i<u_i\}=\varnothing.

notation.meaning: finite lower and upper endpoints of coordinate \(i\)

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Bound Barrier Boundary

children.title: Ranged-Constraint Formulations
children.top_down_role: Barrier representations for rows with both lower and upper limits.

knowledge_statements.title: Ranged-Constraint Formulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct barrier representation of two-sided linear rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A ranged row has the form \(r_i\le a_i^\top x\le u_i\), where \(r_i<u_i\). On its strict interior, direct logarithmic-barrier treatment adds \(-\mu\log(a_i^\top x-r_i)-\mu\log(u_i-a_i^\top x)\) to the objective. Its Hessian contribution is \(\mu\big((a_i^\top x-r_i)^{-2}+(u_i-a_i^\top x)^{-2}\big)a_i a_i^\top\). If one endpoint is infinite, omit its inequality and logarithm. The formulation preserves the original variable space while recording both margins of the ranged row.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A two-sided linear row contributes one logarithmic term per finite endpoint and a rank-one weighted Hessian contribution.
assumptions_latex: \(r_i<a_i^\top x<u_i\) at the barrier iterate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The direct ranged-row barrier has the displayed gradient domain and positive-semidefinite Hessian contribution.

notation.meaning: coefficient vector of the ranged row

source_refs.source_title: Interior Point Methods for Linear Optimization
source_refs.locator: 5.3 The primal logarithmic barrier function p. 90

source_witnesses.source_title: Interior Point Methods for Linear Optimization
source_witnesses.locator: 5.3 The primal logarithmic barrier function p. 90

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Endpoint-width boundary for an ordinary direct ranged-row barrier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A finite ranged row requires \(r_i<u_i\) to possess a strict row interior. If \(r_i>u_i\), the closed ranged constraint is infeasible. If \(r_i=u_i\), it is the equality \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x=r_i\), which may be feasible but has no point satisfying \(r_i<a_i^{\mathsf T}x<u_i\). Consequently, its two-logarithm ranged barrier has empty domain and the row must be represented as an equality or handled on the feasible set's relative interior.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A negative-width range is infeasible, while a zero-width range is an equality with no ordinary strict ranged-barrier domain.
assumptions_latex: \(r_i,u_i\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r_i>u_i\Longrightarrow\{x:r_i\le a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le u_i\}=\varnothing,\qquad r_i=u_i\Longrightarrow\{x:r_i<a_i^{\mathsf T}x<u_i\}=\varnothing.

notation.meaning: lower and upper limits of ranged row \(i\)

knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate Ranged-Row Boundary

children.title: Slack-Based Range Conversion
children.top_down_role: Structural consequences of representing ranged rows through slack variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Slack-Based Range Conversion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-plus-bounded-slack conversion of a finite ranged row.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For finite \(r<u\), the ranged constraint \(r\le a^\top x\le u\) is equivalent to introducing \(s\) and imposing \(a^\top x-s=r\) together with \(0\le s\le u-r\). The correspondence is bijective over feasible points: from an original point set \(s=a^\top x-r\), and from a transformed point discard \(s\). If the original row has no separate objective term, assign zero cost to \(s\). Strict range feasibility \(r<a^\top x<u\) is equivalent to \(0<s<u-r\), so the bounded-slack barrier represents the same interior.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convert a finite ranged row into one equality and a bounded slack whose value uniquely records position within the range.
assumptions_latex: \(r,u\in\mathbb R\) and \(r<u\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r\le a^\top x\le u\iff\exists s:\ a^\top x-s=r,\ 0\le s\le u-r\), with unique \(s\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The equality-plus-bounded-slack conversion is precise and bijective, but no source supports the equivalence and strict-interior correspondence.

children.title: Barrier-System Effects of Reformulation
children.top_down_role: Dimension, sparsity, and recovery impacts of bounded or ranged formulations.

knowledge_statements.title: Barrier-System Effects of Reformulation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: KKT-size and sparsity consequences of direct versus slack range modeling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(r<Ax<u\), direct barrier treatment contributes \(A^\top W A\) to the primal Newton matrix, where \(W=\mu\operatorname{Diag}((Ax-r)^{-2}+(u-Ax)^{-2})\). Converting the range to \(Ax-s=r\) with \(0<s<u-r\) instead adds one bounded variable and one equality per ranged row; the slack-bound curvature is diagonal, but the augmented KKT matrix contains the incidence block linking \(x\) and \(s\). The two models have identical projected feasible interiors and objective values, yet their Newton systems can differ in dimension, conditioning, nonzero pattern, and factorization fill.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equivalent direct and slack range models preserve solutions but generate Newton systems with different dimensions, curvature placement, sparsity, and conditioning.
assumptions_latex: All finite range margins are strictly positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Reformulation preserves the projected LP but need not preserve the barrier KKT matrix or its factorization cost.

bounded slack vector in the converted formulation
