knowledge_statements.title: Sparsity-Oriented Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection-equivalent extended formulations chosen to reduce sparse factorization cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the original feasible set be \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\). An extended formulation \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+p}\) with variables \((x,z)\) is admissible when \(P=\{x:\exists z,\ (x,z)\in Q\}\), the transformed objective equals \(c^\top x\), and a feasible lift or recovery rule is recorded. A sparsity-oriented reformulation may duplicate variables, split rows, or introduce linking equations only under this projection equivalence. Its computational merit is determined by the nonzero pattern and fill of the resulting scaled KKT or normal-equation factorization; fewer coefficients or smaller nominal dimension alone does not guarantee lower cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use extended formulations only when projection preserves the LP and the resulting KKT sparsity is expected to reduce factorization work.
assumptions_latex: The reformulation has an explicit projection onto the original variables.
Objective values are preserved under projection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)=P\), while the reformulated barrier system may have a different sparsity graph and fill pattern.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The projection-equivalence requirement is precise and the structure-dependent cost warning fits the principle container, but neither the extended-formulation criterion nor the sparse-factorization claim has a citation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary for generic solution reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Reverse maps generally do not commute. Omitting a substitution, permutation, scaling, fixed value, or objective offset, or applying correct records in forward rather than reverse order, need not preserve original feasibility or objective value. A reconstructed vector must therefore be rejected whenever direct original-model residual, bound, or objective-identity checks fail.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Missing records or the wrong application order can invalidate an otherwise valid reduced solution.
assumptions_latex: At least two transformations are composed or a transformation changes indices, scale, variables, or objective offset
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A valid reduced solution does not guarantee a valid reconstruction from an incomplete or misordered log.
knowledge_statements.title: Incomplete or Misordered Postsolve Logs

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic metadata sufficient to reconstruct original primal or primal-dual solution components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For presolve transformations \(T_1,\ldots,T_k\), a solution-reconstruction log stores each reverse map \(R_i\), index permutations, eliminated constants and substitutions, variable or row scaling factors, and the cumulative objective offset \(\delta\). Starting from a reduced solution, apply \(R_k,\ldots,R_1\) in reverse transformation order. The log is sufficient when the reconstructed point satisfies the original constraints and bounds and \(c^{\mathsf T}x^{(0)}=\widehat c^{\mathsf T}x^{(k)}+\delta\). If dual components are claimed, their inverse scaling and multiplier updates must also be stored and validated in the original model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply a complete transformation log backward, restore indices, scalings, substitutions, and objective offsets, then validate the reconstructed original solution.
assumptions_latex: Every applied presolve step has the required reverse map
Transformation order, permutations, scalings, and objective offsets are retained
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A reduced feasible point reconstructs to an original feasible point with the recorded objective identity; claimed dual components additionally satisfy the original dual equations and signs.

notation.meaning: Reverse solution map for presolve transformation i.

knowledge_statements.title: Reverse Solution-Transformation Log
Solution-Reconstruction Metadata
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metadata representation sufficient for reversing a presolve transformation sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose presolve applies transformations \(T_1,\ldots,T_k\), producing reduced variables \(x^{(k)}\). Solution-reconstruction metadata are sufficient when, for every step \(i\), they encode a reverse map \(R_i\) and any eliminated constants, substitutions, permutations, scaling factors, and objective offset needed to compute \(x^{(i-1)}=R_i(x^{(i)})\). Reconstruction applies \(R_k,\ldots,R_1\) in reverse transformation order. Sufficiency requires every reduced feasible point to map to an original feasible point and the recorded cumulative offset \(\delta\) to satisfy \(c^\top x^{(0)}=\widehat c^\top x^{(k)}+\delta\). Under these conditions, an optimal reduced point reconstructs an optimal original point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reverse-transformation log reconstructs original solutions by applying stored recovery maps backward while restoring feasibility and the recorded objective offset.
assumptions_latex: Each presolve step has a recorded reverse map on reduced feasible points.
The cumulative objective offset is recorded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{(0)}=(R_1\circ\cdots\circ R_k)(x^{(k)})\) is feasible, and reduced optimality transfers through the objective identity.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Solution Metadata Need Not Preserve Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between point postsolve data and homogeneous certificate lifting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A reverse map sufficient to reconstruct feasible points need not reconstruct row multipliers, homogeneous directions, or objective slopes. If the transformation log omits a row combination, scaling, bound change, or eliminated-coordinate rule needed by the claimed certificate, a valid reduced certificate may lift to an object that fails the original sign, null-space, residual, or strict objective-slope condition. Such an object must be rejected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Point-recovery data alone may lose the multiplier or ray information needed for an original-model certificate.
assumptions_latex: A reduced certificate is valid
At least one certificate-specific reverse action required by a presolve transformation is absent or inconsistent
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Reduced certificate validity does not imply validity of the incompletely reconstructed original-space object.
knowledge_statements.title: Solution Metadata Need Not Preserve Certificates

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metadata sufficient to lift reduced infeasibility or improving-ray evidence through presolve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an ordered presolve history \(T_1,\ldots,T_k\), certificate-reconstruction metadata store, for every transformation, the certificate-specific reverse action on the affected rows, columns, bounds, scalings, and affine substitutions. Given a reduced certificate \(w^{(k)}\), apply these actions in reverse order to obtain \(w^{(0)}\) in the original dimensions. The result is accepted only after it satisfies the defining original-model predicate for the claimed certificate class; reduced-model validity alone is insufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Store certificate-specific inverse actions for every presolve step, apply them backward, and validate the lifted object against the original model.
assumptions_latex: Every presolve transformation affecting the certificate has a recorded reverse action
Transformation order, dimensions, signs, and scaling factors are retained
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A lifted object is a certificate only if its reconstructed original-space form satisfies the claimed certificate predicate.

notation.meaning: Reduced and reconstructed original-space certificate objects.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate-Specific Reverse Transformation Log

assumptions_latex: The original linear program and every presolve transformation are represented in exact arithmetic or with declared numerical tolerances.
Each transformation has a specified inverse action on primal-dual objects.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The record permits a reduced infeasibility or unboundedness certificate to be lifted and checked against the original linear program.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metadata required to lift reduced-model certificates through an ordered presolve history.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Certificate-reconstruction metadata for transformations \(T_1,\ldots,T_k\) consists of their order, eliminated rows and columns, substitution formulas, scaling factors, bound changes, and certificate-specific inverse rules. Given a reduced certificate \(w^{(k)}\), reconstruction applies these rules in reverse order, producing \(w^{(i-1)}=T_i^{\dagger}(w^{(i)})\) for \(i=k,\ldots,1\). The record is complete when \(w^{(0)}\) has the original dimensions and satisfies the defining sign, orthogonality, and residual conditions of the claimed primal-infeasibility, dual-infeasibility, or improving-ray certificate, under the declared tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The metadata records enough transformation history to lift a reduced infeasibility or unboundedness certificate and validate it in the original model.
knowledge_statements.title: Certificate-Reconstruction Metadata

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the certificate-reconstruction metadata leaf and is internally coherent, but no inspectable source is cited for the required metadata, inverse rules, or original-model certificate validation conditions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: A Reconstructed Point Does Not Determine a Basis
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonuniqueness and singularity boundary for basis reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Successful reconstruction of an original feasible point does not by itself reconstruct a basis. At a degenerate point, several nonsingular bases may induce the same point, and a set of columns chosen only from reconstructed zero or positive values may be singular. Missing or inconsistent status and dependency metadata therefore yields at most a basis candidate requiring rank and feasibility validation or repair pivots.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Point recovery alone neither selects a unique basis nor guarantees that selected columns are independent.
assumptions_latex: An original feasible point has been reconstructed
No independently validated original basic-index set is supplied
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\) feasible does not imply that a value-derived candidate \(B\) is unique or that \(A_B\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.title: A Reconstructed Point Does Not Determine a Basis

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Basis Reconstruction Record and Acceptance Test
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basis-specific postsolve data and the validation required after applying it.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A basis-reconstruction record stores the reverse updates to row and column statuses, the placement of fixed or eliminated variables, dependencies for restored rows or columns, and any pivots required when reversing presolve. Applying the records in reverse order produces a candidate original basic-index set \(B\). It is accepted as an original-model basis only when \(A_B\) is square and nonsingular and the induced basic solution and nonbasic bound assignments satisfy the original constraints. Optimal-basis status additionally requires original-model multipliers and reduced costs with the required signs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reverse the stored row, column, and status updates to obtain a candidate basis, then accept it only after original-matrix rank, primal-status, and, when claimed, dual reduced-cost checks.
assumptions_latex: The original model is represented in equality form with bounds
The reduced status description and all basis-specific reverse updates are available
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B\) is accepted only if \(A_B\) is nonsingular and the claimed original primal and dual status predicates hold.

notation.meaning: Original constraint-matrix columns indexed by B.

knowledge_statements.title: Basis Reconstruction Record and Acceptance Test

assumptions_latex: The original linear program is represented in equality form with bounds.
The reduced solution has been reconstructed to the original variables before basis reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The metadata defines a candidate original-model basis whose nonsingularity and primal-dual status can be independently checked.

notation.meaning: basis matrix formed from basic columns

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metadata for constructing and validating an original-model basis after reduced-model solution recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Basis-reconstruction metadata consists of the reduced basic-status vector, the status assigned to every eliminated or fixed variable and removed row, dependencies used to restore deleted rows or columns, and any pivot priorities or repair instructions. It determines a candidate index set \(B\) for which \(A_B\) is square. Reconstruction succeeds only if \(A_B\) is nonsingular and the associated basic solution, nonbasic bound assignments, reduced costs, and row multipliers satisfy the original primal and dual feasibility tolerances. Otherwise the metadata yields only a basis candidate requiring rank-revealing repair or additional pivots.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The record restores variable and row statuses, then requires the resulting original basis to pass rank, feasibility, and reduced-cost checks.
knowledge_statements.title: Basis-Reconstruction Metadata

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition has the correct role and local scope, but the detailed claims about restoring statuses, dependencies, and a valid original-model basis have no cited source.

assumptions_latex: The original feasible region is \(P=\{x:Ax=b,\ x>0\}\).
Presolve uses a reconstruction map \(x=Rz+r\) from a reduced feasible set \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Strict feasibility is preserved exactly when \(Rz+r>0\) holds for every reduced point designated strictly feasible.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact condition for an affine reduction to preserve the original coordinatewise strict interior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q^{\circ}\) denote the reduced points satisfying every retained inequality strictly. The reduction preserves strict interior under reconstruction if and only if \(Rz+r>0\) componentwise for every \(z\in Q^{\circ}\). It reflects strict interior if and only if every \(x\in P\) has some \(z\in Q^{\circ}\) with \(x=Rz+r\). Fixing an original variable at zero, or reconstructing it as an expression that can vanish on \(Q^{\circ}\), violates preservation even when feasibility and optimal value are preserved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reduced strict-interior point remains strict only when every reconstructed original slack is positive; fixing a variable at zero destroys this property.
knowledge_statements.title: Strict-Interior Changes Under Reduction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition matches the strict-interior boundary leaf and its affine-map formulation is precise, but no source supports the preservation and reflection criteria or the stated failure examples.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit curvature mismatch under a positive-coordinate aggregation reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the reconstruction \(x=z_1+z_2\), the pullback of the one-coordinate barrier is \(F_R(z)=-\log(z_1+z_2)\), whose Hessian is \((z_1+z_2)^{-2}\mathbf 1\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}\) and has rank one. The native positive-orthant barrier \(G(z)=-\log z_1-\log z_2\) has Hessian \(\operatorname{Diag}(z_1^{-2},z_2^{-2})\) and rank two. Thus the reconstruction preserves the positive projected coordinate but not the barrier curvature or local norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Aggregating two positive coordinates into one preserves the projected coordinate but changes the logarithmic-barrier Hessian from full rank to rank one.
assumptions_latex: The original positive coordinate is reconstructed as \(x=z_1+z_2\).

notation.meaning: original positive coordinate reconstructed from reduced variables
positive coordinates in the alternative representation

knowledge_statements.title: Aggregation Curvature Counterexample

assumptions_latex: The original barrier is the logarithmic barrier on positive primal slacks or variables.
The reduction is represented by an affine reconstruction \(x=Rz+r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Unless reconstructed slacks are merely positive scalar multiples of reduced coordinates, the reduced logarithmic barrier generally differs from the pullback of the original barrier.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison of the original barrier pulled back through reconstruction with a native reduced-model barrier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On the domain \(Rz+r>0\), the pullback satisfies \(F_R(z)=-\sum_{j=1}^n\log((Rz+r)_j)\), with gradient \(R^{\mathsf T}\nabla F(Rz+r)\) and Hessian \(R^{\mathsf T}\nabla^2F(Rz+r)R\). A reduced barrier \(G(z)=-\sum_i\log z_i\) has the same central-path geometry only under a structure preserving the logarithmic terms up to an additive constant, such as coordinate deletion and positive diagonal rescaling. General substitutions or aggregation change curvature, local norms, and central-path neighborhoods despite preserving the feasible projection or optimal value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: General presolve substitutions preserve feasibility but alter logarithmic-barrier curvature and central paths; simple positive coordinate rescalings are the exceptional invariant case.
knowledge_statements.title: Barrier-Geometry Distortion

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property belongs in the barrier-geometry distortion leaf, and the pullback derivative formulas are coherent. The stronger comparison with native reduced barriers and central-path geometry requires a direct source.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Original-Space Validation After Numerically Sensitive Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A posteriori acceptance test for a primal-dual point reconstructed after presolve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x=Rz+r\) be the stored reconstruction for \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\). At prescribed absolute tolerances \((\tau_p,\tau_d,\tau_g)\), the reconstructed point \((x,y,s)\) passes the original-space acceptance test when \(\|Ax-b\|\le\tau_p\), \(x\ge-\tau_p\mathbf 1\), \(\|A^{\mathsf T}y+s-c\|\le\tau_d\), \(s\ge-\tau_d\mathbf 1\), and \(|c^{\mathsf T}x-b^{\mathsf T}y|\le\tau_g\). Reduced-space residual tests alone do not imply these inequalities when reconstruction amplifies perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recompute primal feasibility, dual feasibility, bound violations, and the duality gap in the original model before accepting a reconstructed solution.
assumptions_latex: \(x=Rz+r\) is the stored postsolve reconstruction.
Original data \((A,b,c)\), a specified norm, and acceptance tolerances are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Satisfaction of the displayed inequalities establishes that the reconstructed point passes the stated original-space tolerance test.

notation.meaning: absolute primal, dual, and gap acceptance tolerances

knowledge_statements.title: Original-Space Validation After Numerically Sensitive Reduction

assumptions_latex: A presolve transformation replaces the original linear system by an algebraically equivalent reduced system.
Floating-point arithmetic with unit roundoff \(u\) is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A reduction is numerically adverse when its reconstruction or reduced linear systems amplify perturbations enough to invalidate the intended feasibility or optimality tolerances.

notation.meaning: condition number of an operator or matrix

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numerical failure boundary for algebraically valid presolve transformations used before a barrier solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A reduction is numerically adverse when it introduces divisions by small pivots, subtraction of nearly equal quantities, extreme row or column scaling, or an ill-conditioned reconstruction operator. In particular, if a reduced perturbation \(\delta z\) reconstructs as \(\delta x=R\delta z\), then \(\|\delta x\|\leq\|R\|\,\|\delta z\|\); large \(\|R\|\) magnifies solve errors. Likewise, reduced Newton systems with large \(\kappa\) may have relative errors of order \(u\kappa\). When these amplified errors exceed the original-model tolerances, algebraic equivalence does not ensure numerically reliable recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Small pivots, cancellation, extreme scaling, or ill-conditioned reconstruction can amplify reduced-solve errors beyond original-model tolerances.
knowledge_statements.title: Numerically Adverse Reductions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary classification fits the leaf, but the numerical-error discussion, including the conditioning and tolerance claims, is uncited and needs authoritative support with a specific locator.

assumptions_latex: A barrier method returns an interior primal-dual point for a presolved model.
Crossover seeks a basic primal-dual solution of the original model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Presolve is crossover-complete only when its retained metadata identifies enough original active-set and dependency information to reconstruct and validate an original basis.

notation.meaning: original active constraints at a limiting solution

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information that presolve must retain for reliable crossover to an original-model basic solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Crossover information is lost when multiple original rows, columns, bounds, or active sets map to the same reduced representation and the transformation record omits the distinctions needed to select among them. The loss is operationally material if no retained data determine a set \(B\) such that \(A_B\) is nonsingular and the reconstructed basic solution satisfies original primal-dual tolerances. Aggregation, duplicate-row deletion, fixed-variable elimination, and substitution can cause this failure unless dependencies, statuses, and tie-breaking or repair data are retained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reduced interior solution may not determine an original basis when presolve discards active-set, dependency, or status information needed by crossover.
knowledge_statements.title: Crossover Information Loss

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement correctly targets loss of basis-reconstruction information during crossover, but no source supports the asserted failure modes or the sufficiency of the listed retained metadata.

assumptions_latex: The primal-dual pair is \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\geq0\}\) and \(\max\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\ s\geq0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A strictly feasible start interface accepts exactly points satisfying both affine systems and strict componentwise positivity.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard-form primal-dual interface when a strictly feasible starting triple is supplied.

source_refs.locator: 4.2 The case where strictly feasible solutions are known p. 72
source_refs.source_title: Interior Point Methods for Linear Optimization

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The interface accepts \((x^0,y^0,s^0)\) as a strictly feasible primal-dual start precisely when \(Ax^0=b\), \(A^{\mathsf T}y^0+s^0=c\), \(x^0>0\), and \(s^0>0\). It initializes the complementarity parameter by \(\mu_0=(x^0)^{\mathsf T}s^0/n>0\). If a neighborhood condition is required by the selected path-following method, the interface must additionally test its stated residual or componentwise complementarity inequalities; strict feasibility alone does not imply membership in every central-path neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strict-start interface verifies primal and dual equations, positive primal variables and dual slacks, and any neighborhood condition required by the algorithm.
knowledge_statements.title: Strictly Feasible Start Interfaces

source_witnesses.locator: 4.2 The case where strictly feasible solutions are known p. 72
source_witnesses.source_title: Interior Point Methods for Linear Optimization

assumptions_latex: The primal-dual pair is in standard form and trial vectors of compatible dimensions are available.
The algorithm permits nonzero primal and dual residuals at initialization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The construction returns a positive but generally infeasible starting triple together with explicit initial residuals.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive initialization for infeasible primal-dual interior-point algorithms in standard form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given trial vectors \((\bar x,\bar y,\bar s)\) and a floor \(\delta>0\), set \(x^0_i=\max\{\bar x_i,\delta\}\), \(y^0=\bar y\), and \(s^0_i=\max\{\bar s_i,\delta\}\). Compute \(r_p^0=b-Ax^0\), \(r_d^0=c-A^{\mathsf T}y^0-s^0\), and \(\mu_0=(x^0)^{\mathsf T}s^0/n\). Supply the positive triple and residuals to an infeasible-start method, which stops only when the prescribed primal, dual, and complementarity tolerances are met; positivity does not assert initial feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Floor trial primal variables and dual slacks at a positive value, compute residuals, and pass all quantities to an infeasible-start method.
knowledge_statements.title: Infeasible-Start Construction

assumptions_latex: A homogeneous self-dual embedding of the primal-dual linear program has been specified.
Its initial point lies in the strict interior of the embedding cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The embedding initialization provides one interior trajectory whose terminal scaling distinguishes recoverable solutions from infeasibility certificates.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic homogeneous self-dual initialization; exact embedding equations depend on the chosen convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(x^0>0\), \(s^0>0\), \(\tau^0>0\), and \(\kappa^0>0\), together with \(y^0\), and define the embedding's constant residual or displacement so that \(H(x^0,y^0,s^0,\tau^0,\kappa^0)=0\). Apply a primal-dual path-following method to the embedded feasibility system while preserving positivity. At termination, output the scaled primal-dual solution when \(\tau>0\) and the normalized residuals satisfy the original tolerances; when \(\tau\) tends to zero while \(\kappa>0\), interpret the normalized terminal vector using the embedding's stated infeasibility-certificate rules.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Initialize a homogeneous self-dual embedding at a known positive point, follow its central path, then decode either a scaled solution or a certificate.
knowledge_statements.title: Embedding-Based Initialization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithmic role fits, but homogeneous self-dual embeddings use convention-dependent equations and decoding rules. Without a cited, explicit embedding convention, the initialization and terminal certificate interpretation cannot be reliably reviewed.

assumptions_latex: A prior strictly interior triple solves or approximately solves a nearby standard-form linear program.
The new problem has the same variable and constraint dimensions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The prior point is reusable exactly when positivity is retained and its new residuals satisfy the receiving algorithm's admissibility thresholds after any correction.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reuse test and repair rule for an interior point from a nearby linear program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \((\hat x,\hat y,\hat s)\), compute \(r_p'=b'-A'\hat x\) and \(r_d'=c'-A'^{\mathsf T}\hat y-\hat s\), and test \(\hat x>0\) and \(\hat s>0\). If positivity fails, apply a componentwise positive shift, or damp toward an available reference interior point, until \(x^0\geq\delta e\) and \(s^0\geq\delta e\). Optionally apply affine correction equations to reduce \(r_p'\) and \(r_d'\), choosing a step length that preserves these bounds. Accept the corrected triple as a strict-feasible start only when both residuals satisfy the required feasibility tolerances; otherwise pass it, with its residuals, to an infeasible-start method.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recompute residuals under the new model, repair positivity by shifting or damping when an interior reference is available, and classify the result as feasible-start or infeasible-start input.
knowledge_statements.title: Prior Interior-Solution Reuse

assumptions_latex: A nonsingular basis \(B\) and associated primal-dual basic solution are available for the new or a nearby model.
A positive centering parameter \(\mu_0\) and positivity floor \(\delta\u003e0\) are chosen.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Perturbing complementary zero components by positive amounts yields an interior candidate, but feasibility must be restored or carried as residual data.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Construction of a positive primal-dual candidate from complementary basic and nonbasic statuses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Start from the basic solution and replace every zero or nonpositive primal component by at least \(\delta\), producing \(x^0>0\). Replace every zero or nonpositive dual slack similarly, producing \(s^0>0\); a complementarity-scaled choice may set repaired components near \(\mu_0/s_i^0\) or \(\mu_0/x_i^0\) when the denominator is positive. Choose or update \(y^0\), then compute \(r_p^0=b-Ax^0\) and \(r_d^0=c-A^{\mathsf T}y^0-s^0\). Apply a positivity-preserving feasibility correction, or initialize an infeasible-start method with these residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Perturb the basis solution away from zero, compute the resulting feasibility residuals, and correct them or use an infeasible-start barrier method.
knowledge_statements.title: Prior-Basis-to-Interior Start

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the basis-to-interior start leaf and distinguishes positivity from feasibility, but the proposed perturbation and complementarity-scaled repair rules lack a direct source.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: A Basis Solution Is Not a Strict Barrier Start
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the direct-reuse boundary separating simplex bases from interior barrier starts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a complementary basic primal-dual solution, each index satisfies \(x_i s_i=0\). Consequently the pair cannot satisfy \(x>0\) and \(s>0\) simultaneously and cannot be passed unchanged to a logarithmic primal-dual barrier iteration requiring strict positivity. A basis-derived start must first be shifted or otherwise mapped into the positive domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A complementary basis solution lies on the barrier-domain boundary and cannot be reused unchanged as a strictly positive primal-dual start.
assumptions_latex: The barrier method requires \(x>0\) and \(s>0\).
The basis-derived pair satisfies \(x_i s_i=0\) for every index.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \neg(x>0\ \wedge\ s>0).
knowledge_statements.title: A Basis Solution Is Not a Strict Barrier Start

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conditional Transfer of a Path-Following Iteration Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States when a warm point inherits the underlying neighborhood-based accuracy bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a path-following method initialized in its required neighborhood with complementarity \(\mu_0\) reaches \(\mu\le\varepsilon\) in at most \(C\sqrt\nu\log(\mu_0/\varepsilon)\) iterations, where \(\nu\) is its barrier parameter. A warm start satisfying the same hypotheses inherits that bound with its own \(\mu_0\). Euclidean proximity without those hypotheses gives no such bound or guaranteed advantage over cold initialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A warm start inherits the usual iteration estimate only through valid neighborhood membership and favorable initial complementarity; proximity alone guarantees no speedup.
assumptions_latex: The underlying method has the stated neighborhood-based bound.
The warm point satisfies every initialization hypothesis of that theorem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{warm}}\le C\sqrt\nu\log(\mu_0/\varepsilon).

notation.meaning: barrier parameter of the underlying path-following method

review_flags: conditional on the underlying method's complexity theorem
knowledge_statements.title: Conditional Transfer of a Path-Following Iteration Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a declared gate for direct reuse of a prior interior primal-dual point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a changed standard-form model, let \(\mu_0=(x^0)^{\mathsf T}s^0/n\). knowledge_statements.title: KKT Block Organization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Newton linearization for a standard-form primal-dual linear program at a strictly positive iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the primal-dual pair \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\geq0\}\) and \(\max\{b^Ty:A^Ty+s=c,\ s\geq0\}\), let \(e\in\mathbb R^n\) be the all-ones vector and define \(X=\operatorname{Diag}(x)\), \(S=\operatorname{Diag}(s)\), \(r_p=b-Ax\), \(r_d=c-A^Ty-s\), and \(r_c=\sigma\mu e-XSe\). The primal-dual Newton direction is organized as
\[
\begin{bmatrix}0&A^T&I\\A&0&0\\S&0&X\end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix}\Delta x\\\Delta y\\\Delta s\end{bmatrix}
=
\begin{bmatrix}r_d\\r_p\\r_c\end{bmatrix}.
\]
The three block rows encode dual feasibility, primal feasibility, and linearized complementarity, respectively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The full Newton system groups the dual-feasibility, primal-feasibility, and complementarity equations into three block rows acting on the primal, multiplier, and slack directions.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b,y\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c,x,s\in\mathbb R^n\).
\(x,s\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\), \(\mu=x^Ts/n\), and \(\sigma\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K(\Delta x,\Delta y,\Delta s)^T=(r_d,r_p,r_c)^T\) with the displayed KKT block matrix \(K\).

notation.meaning: Diagonal matrices of primal variables and dual slacks.
All-ones vector in the primal-variable space.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a strictly positive iterate, the unreduced three-block KKT Newton matrix is nonsingular exactly when the equality matrix has full row rank.
assumptions_latex: \(x,s\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\).
\(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K\text{ is nonsingular}\iff\operatorname{rank}(A)=m.\)

knowledge_statements.title: Nonsingularity of the Full KKT Newton Matrix
Complementarity-Block Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagonal scaling that converts the complementarity row into an eliminable symmetric coefficient block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X=\operatorname{Diag}(x)\), \(S=\operatorname{Diag}(s)\), and \(\Theta=XS^{-1}\), where \(x,s\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\). Multiplying
\[
S\Delta x+X\Delta s=r_c
\]
by \(X^{-1}\) gives
\[
\Theta^{-1}\Delta x+\Delta s=X^{-1}r_c,
\qquad
\Delta s=X^{-1}r_c-\Theta^{-1}\Delta x.
\]
Here \(\Theta\) and \(\Theta^{-1}\) are symmetric positive definite. Substitution into \(A^T\Delta y+\Delta s=r_d\), together with \(A\Delta x=r_p\), gives the symmetric augmented system
\[
\begin{bmatrix}-\Theta^{-1}&A^T\\A&0\end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix}\Delta x\\\Delta y\end{bmatrix}
=
\begin{bmatrix}r_d-X^{-1}r_c\\r_p\end{bmatrix}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive diagonal complementarity scaling expresses the slack direction from the primal direction and yields a symmetric augmented system when combined with the primal and dual block rows.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(x,s,\Delta x,\Delta s,r_c,r_d\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(\Delta y,r_p\in\mathbb R^m\).
\(x,s\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\).
\(S\Delta x+X\Delta s=r_c\), \(A^T\Delta y+\Delta s=r_d\), and \(A\Delta x=r_p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Delta s=X^{-1}r_c-\Theta^{-1}\Delta x\) with \(\Theta=XS^{-1}\succ0\), and the resulting two-block coefficient matrix is symmetric.

notation.meaning: Positive diagonal primal and slack matrices.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact domain of the inverse-based diagonal elimination used by complementarity scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\operatorname{Diag}(x)\), \(S=\operatorname{Diag}(s)\), and \(\Theta=XS^{-1}\). The elimination \(\Delta s=X^{-1}r_c-\Theta^{-1}\Delta x\) is well defined with \(\Theta\succ0\) when \(x_i>0\) and \(s_i>0\) for every \(i\). If some \(x_i=0\), then \(X^{-1}\) and \(\Theta^{-1}\) are undefined; if some \(s_i=0\), then \(S^{-1}\), and hence \(\Theta\), is undefined. Thus this scaling cannot be evaluated literally at a boundary point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complementarity scaling and its inverse-based slack elimination require strictly positive primal and slack components and break down literally at the boundary.
assumptions_latex: \(X=\operatorname{Diag}(x)\) and \(S=\operatorname{Diag}(s)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x,s\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\Rightarrow\Theta\succ0\); if \(x_i s_i=0\) for some \(i\), at least one required inverse is undefined.
knowledge_statements.title: Boundary Breakdown of Complementarity Scaling
Symmetric-Indefinite Augmented Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symmetric two-block reduction obtained after eliminating the dual-slack direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), let \(\Theta\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be positive diagonal, and let \(q\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(r_p\in\mathbb R^m\). The slack-eliminated Newton equations have the augmented form
\[
\begin{bmatrix}-\Theta^{-1}&A^T\\A&0\end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix}\Delta x\\\Delta y\end{bmatrix}
=
\begin{bmatrix}q\\r_p\end{bmatrix}.
\]
If \(A\) has full row rank, the coefficient matrix is nonsingular and symmetric indefinite, with inertia \((m,n,0)\) when inertia is ordered as positive, negative, and zero eigenvalue counts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Slack elimination gives a nonsingular symmetric-indefinite augmented system in the primal and multiplier directions when the constraint matrix has full row rank.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has rank \(m\).
\(\Theta\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is diagonal and positive definite.
\(q,\Delta x\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(r_p,\Delta y\in\mathbb R^m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{inertia}\!\left(\begin{bmatrix}-\Theta^{-1}&A^T\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\right)=(m,n,0)\).

notation.meaning: Numbers of positive, negative, and zero eigenvalues of a symmetric matrix.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Semidefinite Blocks Do Not Guarantee Quasidefinite Nonsingularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp loss of the rank-independent conclusion when a signed diagonal block is not definite.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Replacing either definite diagonal block in \(K_q\) by a merely positive-semidefinite block removes the unconditional nonsingularity guarantee. For example, if \(R_d=0\) and there exists \(0\ne y\in\ker(A^{\mathsf T})\), then \(K_q(0,y)=(0,0)\). Dually, if \(H\) is singular and there exists \(0\ne x\in\ker(H)\cap\ker(A)\), then \(K_q(x,0)=(0,0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With only semidefinite regularization, null spaces of the diagonal blocks and the constraint matrix can leave the augmented system singular.
assumptions_latex: The corresponding diagonal block is allowed to be singular
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Semidefiniteness alone does not imply rank-independent nonsingularity or fixed inertia.
knowledge_statements.title: Semidefinite Blocks Do Not Guarantee Quasidefinite Nonsingularity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which primal-only, dual-only, and two-sided shifts remove singularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Writing \(H=\Theta^{-1}+R_p\), primal regularization changes the negative definite block and the inverse used in the constraint-space Schur complement. A positive-definite dual block \(R_d\) makes \(R_d+AH^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\) positive definite for arbitrary \(A\), giving the rank-independent two-sided quasidefinite case. If \(R_d=0\), nonsingularity instead requires \(A\) to have full row rank; if \(H\) is not positive definite, further null-space conditions are required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive dual block removes left-null-space singularity; without it, full row rank is required, while loss of primal definiteness requires additional null-space control.
assumptions_latex: \(H\succ0\) for the stated Schur-complement alternatives
\(R_d\succeq0\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_d\succ0\) gives rank-independent nonsingularity, whereas \(R_d=0\) requires \(\operatorname{rank}(A)=m\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definite signed diagonal blocks in a regularized augmented Newton matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) and \(R_d\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) be symmetric positive definite. For every \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), the symmetric quasidefinite matrix \[K_q=\begin{bmatrix}-H&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&R_d\end{bmatrix}\] is nonsingular and has inertia \((m,n,0)\), where the entries count positive, negative, and zero eigenvalues. No rank assumption on \(A\) is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Oppositely signed definite diagonal blocks make the augmented matrix nonsingular with fixed inertia, even when the constraint matrix is rank deficient.

\(R_d\succ0\)
\(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\)

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetric Quasidefinite Nonsingularity and Inertia
Quasidefinite Augmented Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regularized augmented Newton matrix with definite diagonal blocks and fixed inertia.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H=\Theta^{-1}+R_p\succ0\) and \(R_d\succ0\). The regularized augmented matrix
\[
K_q=\begin{bmatrix}-H&A^T\\A&R_d\end{bmatrix}
\]
is symmetric quasidefinite. For every \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), the Schur complement of \(-H\) is \(R_d+AH^{-1}A^T\succ0\). Consequently \(K_q\) is nonsingular and has inertia \((m,n,0)\). This conclusion does not require \(A\) to have full row rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive primal and dual regularization makes the augmented matrix symmetric quasidefinite, nonsingular, and of fixed inertia even for rank-deficient constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(\Theta\succ0\), \(R_p\succeq0\), and \(H=\Theta^{-1}+R_p\succ0\).
\(R_d\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) is symmetric positive definite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K_q\) is nonsingular and \(\operatorname{inertia}(K_q)=(m,n,0)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Factorization Fill Is Not Determined by Assembled Nonzeros
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limit of an assembled-nonzero count as a sparse-solve complexity predictor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The count \(\operatorname{nnz}_{\mathrm{struct}}(K_a)\) describes only the assembled matrix. The storage and arithmetic of a sparse symmetric factorization depend on the elimination ordering, pivoting, and fill graph; matrices with the same dimensions and assembled nonzero count can therefore have different factor nonzero counts and factorization costs. Numerical cancellation does not remove a structural entry, while additional diagonal regularization changes the structural count when a previously structural-zero diagonal position is inserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sparse factorization cost depends on ordering, pivoting, and fill, not on the assembled nonzero count alone.
assumptions_latex: A sparse symmetric factorization of the augmented matrix is used
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{nnz}_{\mathrm{struct}}(K_a)\) alone does not determine factor storage or arithmetic complexity.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Structural Pattern of the Augmented Matrix
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Assembled structural sparsity before numerical factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K_a=\begin{bmatrix}-D&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\), where \(D\) is structurally full diagonal of order \(n\), the off-diagonal structural pattern is exactly the bipartite incidence pattern of \(A\). Thus \(\operatorname{nnz}_{\mathrm{struct}}(K_a)=n+2\operatorname{nnz}_{\mathrm{struct}}(A)\). Assembling \(K_a\) forms no products between distinct rows or columns of \(A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The assembled augmented matrix preserves the bipartite incidences of the constraint matrix and adds only the primal diagonal.

\(D\) is diagonal and all its diagonal positions are structural nonzeros
Structural symmetric entries are counted separately

knowledge_statements.title: Structural Pattern of the Augmented Matrix
Augmented-System Sparsity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural sparsity of the symmetric augmented matrix before numerical factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For
\[
K_a=\begin{bmatrix}-\Theta^{-1}&A^T\\A&0\end{bmatrix},
\]
where \(\Theta^{-1}\) is diagonal, the off-diagonal nonzero pattern consists exactly of the bipartite incidences \((i,j)\) for which \(A_{ij}\neq0\). Hence \(K_a\) has \(n+2\operatorname{nnz}(A)\) structural nonzeros when all diagonal entries of \(\Theta^{-1}\) are counted and the zero block remains unfilled. Numerical symmetric factorization may add fill according to the chosen permutation, but forming \(K_a\) introduces no products between distinct rows or columns of \(A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The uneliminated augmented matrix preserves the bipartite sparsity of the constraint matrix; additional nonzeros arise only during ordered factorization.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\).
\(\Theta\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is positive diagonal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{nnz}_{\mathrm{struct}}(K_a)=n+2\operatorname{nnz}(A)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Definite Normal-Equation Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive definiteness of the multiplier normal equations under full row rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, let \(\Theta\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be diagonal and positive definite, and define \(N=A\Theta A^T\). Then \(N\) is symmetric positive definite. Consequently, for every \(q\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(r_p\in\mathbb R^m\), the normal equation
\[
N\Delta y=r_p+A\Theta q
\]
has a unique solution \(\Delta y\in\mathbb R^m\). The associated primal direction is
\[
\Delta x=\Theta(A^T\Delta y-q).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With positive diagonal scaling and independent equality constraints, the multiplier normal-equation matrix is symmetric positive definite and uniquely solvable, after which the primal direction is recovered by substitution.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has rank \(m\).
\(\Theta\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is diagonal and positive definite.
\(q\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(r_p\in\mathbb R^m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A\Theta A^T\succ0\), so the displayed normal equation has a unique \(\Delta y\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sharp Rank Characterization of the Positive-Definite Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient rank condition and null-space boundary for weighted normal equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and let \(\Theta\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be symmetric positive definite. Then
\[
\ker(A\Theta A^T)=\ker(A^T).
\]
Consequently,
\[
A\Theta A^T\succ0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \operatorname{rank}(A)=m.
\]
If \(A\) is row-rank deficient, \(A\Theta A^T\) is positive semidefinite and singular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With positive weighting, the normal matrix is positive definite exactly when the constraint matrix has full row rank; otherwise its null space is the null space of the transposed constraint matrix.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\).
\(\Theta\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is symmetric positive definite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A\Theta A^T\succ0\iff\operatorname{rank}(A)=m\), and \(\ker(A\Theta A^T)=\ker(A^T)\).

notation.meaning: Null space of the linear map represented by \(M\).

knowledge_statements.title: Sharp Rank Characterization of the Positive-Definite Regime
Normal-Equation Conditioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral conditioning bound for diagonally weighted normal equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank and \(\Theta=\operatorname{Diag}(\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_n)\), where \(0<\theta_{\min}\leq\theta_i\leq\theta_{\max}\). Then
\[
\theta_{\min}\sigma_{\min}(A)^2\leq\lambda_{\min}(A\Theta A^T)
\leq\lambda_{\max}(A\Theta A^T)
\leq\theta_{\max}\sigma_{\max}(A)^2,
\]
and consequently
\[
\kappa_2(A\Theta A^T)\leq\kappa_2(A)^2\,\frac{\theta_{\max}}{\theta_{\min}},
\qquad
\kappa_2(A)=\frac{\sigma_{\max}(A)}{\sigma_{\min}(A)}.
\]
Thus both the row-space conditioning of \(A\) and the spread of the barrier scaling can degrade the normal equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The normal-equation condition number is bounded by the squared row-space condition number of the full-row-rank constraint matrix times the spread of the positive diagonal scaling.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has rank \(m\).
\(\Theta=\operatorname{Diag}(\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_n)\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\kappa_2(A\Theta A^T)\leq\kappa_2(A)^2\kappa_2(\Theta)\).

notation.meaning: Smallest positive and largest singular values of the full-row-rank matrix.
Spectral condition number; for the full-row-rank rectangular matrix A, the ratio of its largest to smallest positive singular value.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symbolic sparsity and ordering-dependent factor fill of weighted normal equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N=A\Theta A^T\), where \(\Theta\) is positive diagonal. In the symbolic structural pattern, distinct row vertices \(i\) and \(k\) are adjacent in \(N\) exactly when rows \(i\) and \(k\) of \(A\) share a structurally nonzero column. Thus \(\mathcal G(N)\) is the row-intersection graph of \(A\). For a fixed symmetric elimination ordering, symbolic Cholesky elimination connects the remaining neighbors of each eliminated vertex, so the factor pattern depends on the ordering and can be substantially denser than the pattern of \(A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted normal equations project the constraint matrix's bipartite sparsity onto its row-intersection graph, after which the elimination ordering determines additional Cholesky fill.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) is interpreted by its symbolic structural pattern.
\(\Theta\) is positive diagonal.
Numerical cancellation is excluded from the symbolic pattern.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal G(A\Theta A^T)\) is the row-intersection graph of \(A\), and symbolic Cholesky fill is ordering dependent.

knowledge_statements.title: Row-Intersection Structure and Cholesky Fill
Normal-Equation Fill
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural graph and factorization fill of the weighted normal-equation matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N=A\Theta A^T\) with positive diagonal \(\Theta\). For distinct row indices \(i,k\), the entry \(N_{ik}\) can be structurally nonzero exactly when rows \(i\) and \(k\) of \(A\) share a column containing structural nonzeros. Thus the structural graph of \(N\) is the row-intersection graph of \(A\). Under a symmetric elimination ordering, Cholesky fill connects the uneliminated neighbors of each eliminated vertex; hence fill depends on that ordering and may be much denser than \(A\), even though \(\Theta\) is diagonal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normal equations project bipartite constraint sparsity onto the row-intersection graph, after which the elimination ordering determines additional Cholesky fill.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) is treated by structural nonzero pattern.
\(\Theta\) is positive diagonal and generic numerical cancellation is ignored.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal G(A\Theta A^T)\) is the row-intersection graph of \(A\), with subsequent fill determined by the elimination ordering.

notation.meaning: Undirected structural graph of a symmetric matrix.

knowledge_statements.title: Block-Elimination Routes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent solution routes for the full primal-dual Newton equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), positive diagonal matrices \(X,S\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), and residuals \(r_p\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(r_d,r_c\in\mathbb R^n\). Set \(\Theta=XS^{-1}\) and \(q=r_d-X^{-1}r_c\). Route A solves
\[
\begin{bmatrix}-\Theta^{-1}&A^T\\A&0\end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix}\Delta x\\\Delta y\end{bmatrix}
=
\begin{bmatrix}q\\r_p\end{bmatrix}.
\]
Route B solves
\[
(A\Theta A^T)\Delta y=r_p+A\Theta q
\]
and sets \(\Delta x=\Theta(A^T\Delta y-q)\). Either route then sets
\[
\Delta s=X^{-1}r_c-\Theta^{-1}\Delta x.
\]
Check the residuals of all three original block equations against the prescribed linear-solve tolerance and output \((\Delta x,\Delta y,\Delta s)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve either the augmented system or its normal equations, recover the eliminated components, and validate the direction against the original three Newton equations.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has rank \(m\).
\(X,S\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) are positive diagonal matrices.
\(r_p\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(r_d,r_c\in\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: In exact arithmetic, both routes return the same unique solution \((\Delta x,\Delta y,\Delta s)\) of the full Newton system.

knowledge_statements.title: Eliminated Step-Component Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Back-substitution formulas recovering primal and slack components from a multiplier step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), positive diagonal matrices \(X,S\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), residuals \(r_p\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(r_d,r_c\in\mathbb R^n\), and a multiplier direction \(\Delta y\in\mathbb R^m\) satisfying
\[
A\Theta A^T\Delta y=r_p+A\Theta q,
\qquad
\Theta=XS^{-1},
\qquad
q=r_d-X^{-1}r_c.
\]
Compute
\[
\Delta x=\Theta(A^T\Delta y-q),
\qquad
\Delta s=X^{-1}r_c-\Theta^{-1}\Delta x.
\]
Check \(A\Delta x=r_p\), \(A^T\Delta y+\Delta s=r_d\), and \(S\Delta x+X\Delta s=r_c\) against the selected tolerance, then return \((\Delta x,\Delta y,\Delta s)\). In exact arithmetic, all three identities hold when the normal equation is solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After solving for the multiplier direction, two diagonal back-substitutions recover the primal and slack directions; the recovered direction is then checked against the original system.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(X,S\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), and \(X,S\succ0\) are diagonal.
\(r_p,\Delta y\in\mathbb R^m\), \(r_d,r_c\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(\Theta=XS^{-1}\).
\(\Delta y\) satisfies the displayed normal equation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: In exact arithmetic, the recovered \((\Delta x,\Delta y,\Delta s)\) satisfies all three full Newton block equations.

knowledge_statements.title: Step-Direction Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear decomposition of predictor, centering, and correction Newton directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}\) be a fixed nonsingular Newton matrix. For right-hand sides \(r^{\mathrm{aff}},r^{\mathrm{cen}},r^{\mathrm{cor}}\in\mathbb R^d\), set
\[
r=r^{\mathrm{aff}}+r^{\mathrm{cen}}+r^{\mathrm{cor}},
\qquad
K\Delta^j=r^j,
\quad
j\in\{\mathrm{aff},\mathrm{cen},\mathrm{cor}\}.
\]
Then the assembled direction is
\[
\Delta=\Delta^{\mathrm{aff}}+\Delta^{\mathrm{cen}}+\Delta^{\mathrm{cor}},
\qquad
K\Delta=r.
\]
Under the usual primal-dual residual convention, the affine component uses zero centering, the complementarity block of the centering right-hand side is \(\sigma\mu e\), and the complementarity block of the correction right-hand side is the selected second-order term. All component solves use the same coefficient matrix \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linearity permits the total Newton direction to be assembled from affine, centering, and correction solves that share one fixed coefficient matrix.
assumptions_latex: \(K\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}\) is fixed and nonsingular.
\(r^{\mathrm{aff}},r^{\mathrm{cen}},r^{\mathrm{cor}}\in\mathbb R^d\) and \(r=r^{\mathrm{aff}}+r^{\mathrm{cen}}+r^{\mathrm{cor}}\).
\(\sigma\geq0\), \(\mu>0\), and \(e\in\mathbb R^n\) is the all-ones vector for the complementarity block.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K(\Delta^{\mathrm{aff}}+\Delta^{\mathrm{cen}}+\Delta^{\mathrm{cor}})=r\).

knowledge_statements.title: Bounded-Variable Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-dual barrier equations for variables having finite lower and upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For
\[
\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ \ell\leq x\leq u\},
\]
define \(z=x-\ell\), \(w=u-x\), \(Z=\operatorname{Diag}(z)\), \(W=\operatorname{Diag}(w)\), \(S_L=\operatorname{Diag}(s_L)\), and \(S_U=\operatorname{Diag}(s_U)\). At a strictly interior barrier point, the KKT equations are
\[
Ax=b,
\qquad
A^Ty+s_L-s_U=c,
\qquad
Zs_L=\mu e,
\qquad
Ws_U=\mu e.
\]
With residuals \(r_p=b-Ax\), \(r_d=c-A^Ty-s_L+s_U\), \(r_L=\mu e-Zs_L\), and \(r_U=\mu e-Ws_U\), their Newton linearization is
\[
A\Delta x=r_p,
\qquad
A^T\Delta y+\Delta s_L-\Delta s_U=r_d,
\]
\[
S_L\Delta x+Z\Delta s_L=r_L,
\qquad
-S_U\Delta x+W\Delta s_U=r_U.
\]
The associated distance directions satisfy \(\Delta z=\Delta x\) and \(\Delta w=-\Delta x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite lower and upper bounds introduce two positive distance vectors and two bound-multiplier vectors; their complementarity linearizations contain opposite signs on the primal direction.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b,y\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c,\ell,u,x\in\mathbb R^n\).
\(\ell<x<u\) componentwise, \(s_L,s_U\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\), and \(\mu>0\).
\(e\in\mathbb R^n\) is the all-ones vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed equations give the bounded-variable barrier KKT system and its Newton block linearization.

notation.meaning: Distances from the lower and upper bounds.
Diagonal matrices of the bound distances.
Diagonal matrices of the lower-bound and upper-bound multipliers.
Primal, stationarity, lower-complementarity, and upper-complementarity Newton residuals.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Endpoint conditions determining which bounded-variable barrier blocks exist.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For coordinate \(i\), a two-sided logarithmic-barrier block requires \(\ell_i<u_i\) and \(\ell_i<x_i<u_i\). If \(\ell_i=u_i\), the coordinate is fixed and has no strict interior, so it must be eliminated or imposed as an equality. If exactly one endpoint is infinite, only the finite endpoint contributes a distance, multiplier, complementarity equation, and diagonal curvature term; if both endpoints are infinite, neither endpoint contributes such a block.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed coordinate has no two-sided barrier interior, while infinite endpoints remove their corresponding bound blocks.
assumptions_latex: \(\ell_i,u_i\in\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty,+\infty\}\) are valid endpoints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ell_i=u_i\Rightarrow\{x_i:\ell_i<x_i<u_i\}=\varnothing.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Strict-Interior and Endpoint Boundary Cases

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier-eliminated symmetric system induced by finite lower and upper variable bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the seed notation and Newton equations for \(\ell<x<u\), define \[D=Z^{-1}S_L+W^{-1}S_U\succ0.\] Eliminating \(\Delta s_L\) and \(\Delta s_U\) gives \[\begin{bmatrix}-D&A^T\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}\Delta x\\\Delta y\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}r_d-Z^{-1}r_L+W^{-1}r_U\\r_p\end{bmatrix},\] followed by \(\Delta s_L=Z^{-1}(r_L-S_L\Delta x)\) and \(\Delta s_U=W^{-1}(r_U+S_U\Delta x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminating the two bound-multiplier directions adds their positive diagonal curvature contributions and yields an equivalent symmetric primal-multiplier system.
assumptions_latex: The bounded-variable Newton equations in the immutable seed hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D=Z^{-1}S_L+W^{-1}S_U\succ0\), and the displayed reduced system is equivalent to the full Newton equations.

notation.meaning: Sum of lower- and upper-bound diagonal curvature scalings.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced Bounded-Variable Newton System
Free-Variable Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Split-variable representation of unrestricted primal variables in a logarithmic-barrier system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an unrestricted vector \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), introduce \(u,v\in\mathbb{R}_{++}^n\) and impose \(x=u-v\). Then every \(x\) has such a lift, and replacing \(x\) by \(u-v\) transforms \(Ax=b\) and \(c^Tx\) into \(A(u-v)=b\) and \(c^T(u-v)\), respectively. The split formulation has barrier objective \[c^T(u-v)-\mu\sum_{j=1}^n(\log u_j+\log v_j),\qquad \mu>0.\] Its projection onto the original variable space preserves the LP feasible set and linear objective, although the lifted representation is nonunique and doubles the variable block.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unrestricted variable can be split into two positive variables. This preserves the projected LP but doubles the variable block and introduces a nonunique lift.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x=u-v\) gives an exact projected representation with \((u,v)\in\mathbb{R}_{++}^{2n}\).

notation.meaning: positive parts used to represent an unrestricted variable

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Noncoercivity of the Naive Split-Variable Barrier
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure caused by applying independent logarithmic barriers to a redundant positive-parts lift.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(x=u-v\) with \(u,v>0\) and \[\phi_\mu(u,v)=c^T(u-v)-\mu\sum_j(\log u_j+\log v_j),\qquad \mu>0.\] For any feasible \((u,v)\) and \(t>0\), the pair \((u+te,v+te)\) has the same projection, constraints, and linear objective, while \(\phi_\mu(u+te,v+te)\to-\infty\) as \(t\to\infty\). Thus the naive split-variable logarithmic barrier has no minimizer unless the common-shift redundancy is removed or normalized.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Increasing both positive parts together leaves the original variable unchanged and makes the naive split-variable logarithmic barrier unbounded below.
assumptions_latex: \(u,v\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\), \(x=u-v\), and \(\mu>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{t>0}\phi_\mu(u+te,v+te)=-\infty.\)

notation.meaning: Naive barrier objective on the split lift.

knowledge_statements.title: Noncoercivity of the Naive Split-Variable Barrier

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-dual treatment of an unrestricted coordinate without artificial positive parts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a primal coordinate \(x_j\) is unrestricted, it has no bound slack and no complementarity equation. Its dual stationarity condition is \((A^Ty)_j=c_j\), and its Newton row is \((A^T\Delta y)_j=r_{d,j}\). Native free-variable columns contribute to \(A\Delta x=r_p\) but contribute neither a bound-derived positive diagonal scaling nor bound-barrier curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A native free variable remains in primal feasibility, imposes equality in dual stationarity, and has no complementarity or bound-curvature block.
assumptions_latex: \(x_j\in\mathbb R\) has no finite lower or upper bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((A^Ty)_j=c_j\), and no bound-complementarity equation is attached to \(x_j\).
knowledge_statements.title: Native Free-Variable KKT Block

knowledge_statements.title: Ranged-Row System Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct and slack representations of rows having finite lower and upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R\in\mathbb{R}^{q\times n}\) and \(\ell,u\in\mathbb{R}^q\) satisfy \(\ell_i<u_i\). The strict ranged constraints \(\ell<Rx<u\) are equivalent to introducing \(s^L,s^U\in\mathbb{R}_{++}^q\) with \[Rx-s^L=\ell,\qquad Rx+s^U=u.\] Eliminating the slacks gives the direct logarithmic-barrier term \[-\mu\sum_{i=1}^q\bigl(\log((Rx-\ell)_i)+\log((u-Rx)_i)\bigr).\] Thus every ranged row contributes two positive residuals and two diagonal scaling terms to a primal-dual Newton linearization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A ranged row has lower and upper positive residuals. It may be represented by two slacks or by two logarithmic barrier terms.
assumptions_latex: \(R\in\mathbb{R}^{q\times n}\) and \(\ell,u\in\mathbb{R}^q\).
\(\ell_i<u_i\) for every \(i\), and \(\mu>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ell<Rx<u\iff s^L=Rx-\ell>0\) and \(s^U=u-Rx>0\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Endpoint cases in which the two-sided row-barrier representation reduces or loses its strict interior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For row \(i\), a genuine ranged barrier requires finite endpoints with \(\ell_i<u_i\). If \(\ell_i=u_i\), no value satisfies \(\ell_i<r_i^Tx<u_i\); the row must be represented as an equality rather than by two logarithmic terms. If one endpoint is infinite, its logarithmic term and residual block are omitted, reducing the row to a one-sided inequality. As either finite residual approaches zero from above, its barrier value and curvature weight diverge to \(+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equal endpoints produce an equality with no strict ranged interior, while an infinite endpoint reduces the row to a one-sided constraint.
assumptions_latex: \(\ell_i,u_i\in\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty,+\infty\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ell_i=u_i\Rightarrow\{x:\ell_i<r_i^Tx<u_i\}=\varnothing.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate and Infinite Ranged-Row Endpoints

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gradient and Hessian contributions from the two finite sides of each ranged row.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s^L=Rx-\ell>0\), \(s^U=u-Rx>0\), and \[B(x)=-\mu\sum_{i=1}^q(\log s_i^L+\log s_i^U).\] Then \[\nabla B(x)=\mu R^T\bigl((s^U)^{-1}-(s^L)^{-1}\bigr),\] \[\nabla^2B(x)=\mu R^T\operatorname{Diag}\bigl((s^L)^{-2}+(s^U)^{-2}\bigr)R\succeq0.\] Each ranged row contributes one rank-one matrix whose positive weight is the sum of its lower- and upper-side curvature weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The two sides of a ranged row contribute opposite gradient terms but additive positive curvature on the same row vector.
assumptions_latex: \(s^L=Rx-\ell\in\mathbb R_{++}^q\).
\(s^U=u-Rx\in\mathbb R_{++}^q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nabla^2B(x)=\mu R^T\operatorname{Diag}((s^L)^{-2}+(s^U)^{-2})R\succeq0.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Direct-Barrier Curvature of Ranged Rows

children.title: Inequality-Row System Variants

knowledge_statements.title: Inequality-Row System Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Slack and direct-barrier forms of one-sided linear inequality rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(G\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times n}\), the strict inequalities \(Gx<h\) are equivalent to \[Gx+s=h,\qquad s\in\mathbb{R}_{++}^p.\] Eliminating \(s\) yields the direct barrier \[-\mu\sum_{i=1}^p\log(h_i-g_i^Tx),\] where \(g_i^T\) is row \(i\) of \(G\). Reversing a row converts \(g_i^Tx>h_i\) to \((-g_i)^Tx<-h_i\). Consequently, all one-sided rows can use one positive residual per row, with explicit-slack and direct-residual formulations having the same feasible projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each one-sided inequality corresponds to one positive slack or residual. Reversing signs handles lower inequalities, and eliminating slacks gives the direct logarithmic barrier.
assumptions_latex: \(G\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times n}\), \(h\in\mathbb{R}^p\), and \(\mu>0\).
The barrier is evaluated only where \(h-Gx>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Gx<h\iff s=h-Gx\in\mathbb{R}_{++}^p\).

notation.meaning: row i of the inequality matrix

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strict-Feasibility Boundary for One-Sided Row Barriers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Domain and limiting behavior of a one-sided logarithmic row term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The term \(-\mu\log(h_i-g_i^Tx)\) is finite and twice differentiable exactly when \(h_i-g_i^Tx>0\). As this residual decreases to zero from above, the term and its curvature weight \(\mu(h_i-g_i^Tx)^{-2}\) diverge to \(+\infty\). If no point satisfies all row residuals strictly, the direct logarithmic barrier has empty domain even when the closed inequality system is feasible only on its boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One-sided logarithmic row barriers require strict feasibility; their value and curvature diverge at a finite row boundary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_i\downarrow0\Rightarrow-\mu\log s_i\to+\infty\) and \(\mu s_i^{-2}\to+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.title: Strict-Feasibility Boundary for One-Sided Row Barriers

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gradient, Hessian, and equality-constrained Newton coefficient for direct one-sided row barriers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(s=h-Gx>0\), let \[B(x)=-\mu\sum_{i=1}^p\log s_i.\] Then \[
abla B(x)=\mu G^Ts^{-1},\qquad 
abla^2B(x)=\mu G^T\operatorname{Diag}(s^{-2})G\succeq0,\] where powers are componentwise. With equality constraints \(Ex=d\), the Newton coefficient has saddle form \[ egin{bmatrix}
abla^2B(x)&E^T\E&0\end{bmatrix}.\] Each one-sided row contributes the positive rank-one term \(\mu s_i^{-2}g_i g_i^T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A one-sided row contributes one positive weighted rank-one term to the direct barrier Hessian and enters an equality-constrained saddle-point Newton system.
assumptions_latex: \(s=h-Gx\in\mathbb R_{++}^p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nabla^2B(x)=\mu G^T\operatorname{Diag}(s^{-2})G\succeq0.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Direct-Barrier Curvature of One-Sided Rows

children.title: Slack Representation Effects
children.top_down_role: Dimension, sparsity, and recovery effects associated with explicit slack representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Slack Representation Effects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of eliminating explicit inequality slacks from a barrier Newton system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(Gx+s=h\) with \(s>0\) and barrier term \(-\mu\sum_i\log s_i\). Substitution of \(s=h-Gx\) gives \[\nabla^2\phi(x)=\mu G^TS^{-2}G,\qquad S=\operatorname{Diag}(s).\] The same coefficient is obtained by block elimination of slack directions from the equality-constrained Newton equations. Hence explicit-slack and direct-residual formulations produce algebraically equivalent reduced primal steps when formed at the same strictly feasible point. They nevertheless have different unreduced dimensions and sparsity patterns, so their factorization fill and numerical behavior need not coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminating positive slacks recovers the direct barrier Hessian and the same reduced primal step, but changes the unreduced system’s dimension and sparsity.
assumptions_latex: \(Gx+s=h\), \(s\in\mathbb{R}_{++}^p\), and \(\mu>0\).
Block elimination is performed exactly at the same strictly feasible iterate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H_{\mathrm{red}}=\mu G^TS^{-2}G\), while unreduced system structure depends on whether \(s\) is explicit.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times n}\), \(G\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times n}\), and \(R\in\mathbb{R}^{q\times n}\), with \(d\in\mathbb{R}^r\), \(h\in\mathbb{R}^p\), and \(\ell,u\in\mathbb{R}^q\). Consider \(Ex=d\), \(Gx<h\), and \(\ell<Rx<u\). At a strictly feasible point \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), define \(s=h-Gx\), \(s^L=Rx-\ell\), and \(s^U=u-Rx\). The primal barrier Hessian is \[H=\mu G^T\operatorname{Diag}(s^{-2})G+\mu R^T\operatorname{Diag}((s^L)^{-2}+(s^U)^{-2})R.\] Equality-constrained Newton directions satisfy a saddle-point system with coefficient \[\begin{pmatrix}H&E^T\\E&0\end{pmatrix}.\] Thus inequality and ranged rows contribute positive-semidefinite weighted Gram terms, whereas equality rows remain explicit constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For equality, one-sided, and ranged rows of compatible stated dimensions, the mixed Newton system combines weighted barrier curvature from the inequality and ranged rows with an explicit equality block.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonsingularity Criterion for the Mixed-Row Newton Matrix
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact regularity condition for the seed's equality-constrained weighted-Gram Newton coefficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[H=G^TD_GG+R^TD_RR,\] where \(D_G\succ0\) and \(D_R\succ0\) are the diagonal barrier weights induced by strictly feasible one-sided and ranged rows. Then \[K=\begin{bmatrix}H&E^T\\E&0\end{bmatrix}\] is nonsingular if and only if \(E\) has full row rank and \(H\) is positive definite on \(\ker(E)\). Equivalently, \[\operatorname{rank}(E)=r\quad\text{and}\quad\ker(E)\cap\ker(G)\cap\ker(R)=\{0\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The mixed-row saddle matrix is nonsingular exactly when equality rows are independent and row-barrier curvature controls every nonzero equality-feasible direction.
assumptions_latex: \(D_G\succ0\) and \(D_R\succ0\).
\(E,G,R\) have the compatible dimensions stated in the immutable seed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K\text{ is nonsingular}\iff\operatorname{rank}(E)=r\text{ and }\ker(E)\cap\ker(G)\cap\ker(R)=\{0\}.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Nonsingularity Criterion for the Mixed-Row Newton Matrix

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimensions of augmented, Schur-complement, and null-space Newton systems.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be positive definite and let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) have full row rank. The primal-dual Newton coefficient \[K=\begin{pmatrix}H&A^T\\A&0\end{pmatrix}\] has order \(n+m\). Eliminating the \(n\)-vector primal direction gives the positive-definite dual Schur complement \(AH^{-1}A^T\) of order \(m\). If \(Z\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times(n-m)}\) has full column rank and satisfies \(AZ=0\), null-space elimination gives \(Z^THZ\) of order \(n-m\). These systems recover the same exact Newton direction when their eliminations are valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The augmented system is (n+m)-by-(n+m), the dual Schur complement is m-by-m, and the null-space reduced system is (n-m)-by-(n-m); valid exact eliminations recover the same Newton direction.

knowledge_statements.title: Tall Constraint-Matrix Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: System-form selection when a weighted inequality matrix has many more rows than columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) with \(m\gg n\), and let \(W\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times m}\) be positive diagonal. If \(A\) has full column rank, then \(A^TWA\) is positive definite and has order \(n\). knowledge_statements.scope_note: Low-rank decomposition obtained by separating dense rows in a primal Gram system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition the rows as \(A=\begin{bmatrix}A_s\\U^{\mathsf T}\end{bmatrix}\) and \(W=\operatorname{Diag}(W_s,W_U)\), where \(U^{\mathsf T}\) contains \(k\) rows treated as dense. Then \(A^{\mathsf T}WA=A_s^{\mathsf T}W_sA_s+UW_UU^{\mathsf T}\), and the dense-row contribution has rank at most \(k\). If \(H=A_s^{\mathsf T}W_sA_s\) is nonsingular, the Sherman-Morrison-Woodbury formula represents the full solve using solves with \(H\) and a \(k\times k\) correction system. This avoids storing the dense-row cliques in the base Gram matrix, but the inverse formula fails for a singular base or correction system and may be unattractive when either is ill-conditioned.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dense rows can be isolated as a low-rank update to the Gram matrix, potentially preserving a sparse base factorization while introducing a small correction system.

Dense Row Effects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clique and rank-one effects induced by a structurally dense constraint row.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let row \(i\) of \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) have structural support \(S_i=\{j:a_{ij}\ne0\}\), and let \(w_i>0\). Its contribution to the primal Gram matrix is \(w_i a_i a_i^T\). Structurally, this contribution makes every distinct pair of variables in \(S_i\) adjacent, creating a clique of size \(|S_i|\) in the graph of \(A^TWA\). Hence one dense row can create up to \(|S_i|(|S_i|-1)/2\) off-diagonal structural positions, even though its numerical contribution has rank one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dense row contributes only rank one numerically but creates a clique among all columns in its support, potentially causing substantial factor fill.

Dense Column Effects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural graph densification induced by a dense column in primal normal equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), let \(D=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_n)\succ0\), and form \(N=ADA^{\mathsf T}\). For column \(a_j=A_{:j}\), define \(S_j=\{i:(a_j)_i\ne0\}\). When structural nonzeros are determined without numerical cancellation, the contribution \(d_j a_j a_j^{\mathsf T}\) is structurally nonzero at every pair in \(S_j\times S_j\). Hence the structural graph of \(N\) contains a clique on \(S_j\), with exactly \(\binom{|S_j|}{2}\) off-diagonal adjacency pairs induced by that support. A column supported on many rows can therefore densify the normal-equation graph and increase the storage and work of a subsequent sparse factorization.
