knowledge_statements.statement_title: Near Loss of Full Row Rank
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimension-correct relative condition for equality-constraint matrices that remain algebraically full row rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), where \(m\le n\), \(A\ne0\), and let \(\tau\in(0,1)\). Define \(\rho_{\mathrm{row}}(A)=\sigma_m(A)/\sigma_1(A)\). The matrix is nearly row-rank deficient at tolerance \(\tau\) when \(0<\rho_{\mathrm{row}}(A)\le\tau\). Equivalently, \[0<\min_{\|y\|_2=1}\frac{\|A^{\mathsf T}y\|_2}{\|A\|_2}\le\tau.\] Thus a minimizing left singular vector is a unit left near-null witness. If \(m>n\), full row rank is impossible, so the matrix is exactly row-rank deficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full-row-rank equality matrix is nearly row-rank deficient when its smallest row-space singular value is positive but small relative to its spectral norm; equivalently, it has a unit left near-null vector.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(m\le n\), and \(A\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0<\sigma_m(A)/\sigma_1(A)\le\tau\iff 0<\min_{\|y\|_2=1}\|A^{\mathsf T}y\|_2/\|A\|_2\le\tau\).
knowledge_statements.title: Near Loss of Full Row Rank

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation of algebraic row-rank loss from tolerance-based near rank loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(m\le n\), \(\sigma_m(A)=0\) is equivalent to exact row-rank deficiency, whereas \(0<\sigma_m(A)\le\tau\sigma_1(A)\) describes a full-row-rank matrix classified as nearly deficient. The ratio \(\sigma_m(A)/\sigma_1(A)\) is invariant under nonzero scalar multiplication of the entire matrix but generally changes under unequal row or column scaling. The tolerance and scaling convention are therefore part of the numerical diagnosis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero smallest row-space singular value means exact dependence; a positive but threshold-small value means near dependence, whose diagnosis depends on tolerance and scaling.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) with \(m\le n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sigma_m(A)=0\iff\operatorname{rank}(A)<m\), while \(0<\sigma_m(A)\le\tau\sigma_1(A)\) does not imply exact dependence.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact-versus-Near Row-Rank Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral-norm perturbation interpretation of the smallest relevant singular value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(m\le n\), has full row rank, then \[\operatorname{dist}_2\!\left(A,\{B\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}:\operatorname{rank}(B)<m\}\right)=\sigma_m(A).\] Consequently, \(\rho_{\mathrm{row}}(A)\le\tau\) exactly when some perturbation \(E\) with \(\|E\|_2\le\tau\|A\|_2\) makes \(A+E\) row-rank deficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The smallest row-space singular value is the spectral-norm distance to exact row-rank deficiency.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(m\le n\).
\(\operatorname{rank}(A)=m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}_2(A,\{B:\operatorname{rank}(B)<m\})=\sigma_m(A)\).

notation.meaning: Distance induced by the matrix spectral norm.

knowledge_statements.title: Distance to Exact Row-Rank Deficiency
Near Rank Deficiency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tolerance-relative characterization of an almost rank-deficient constraint matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have singular values \(\sigma_1(A)\ge\cdots\ge\sigma_p(A)\), where \(p=\min\{m,n\}\). Relative to a prescribed threshold \(\tau\in(0,1)\), call \(A\) nearly rank deficient when
\[0<\sigma_p(A)\le\tau\sigma_1(A).\]
Equivalently, there is a unit vector \(v\) in the appropriate right-singular space with \(\|Av\|_2\le\tau\|A\|_2\). For full-rank square \(A\), this condition is \(\kappa_2(A)\ge\tau^{-1}\). The designation is therefore relative to the selected tolerance and data scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matrix is nearly rank deficient at tolerance 	6τ when its smallest singular value is positive but no larger than 	6τ times its largest.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0<\sigma_p(A)/\sigma_1(A)\le\tau\) identifies near rank deficiency at relative threshold \(\tau\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The tolerance convention needs a source. The plain statement contains a corrupted tau token, and the asserted singular-vector equivalence should explicitly identify a right singular vector associated with the smallest listed singular value.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Practical row-rank estimate for a wide equality-constraint matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) with \(m\le n\), compute a column-pivoted QR factorization of \(A^{\mathsf T}\): \[A^{\mathsf T}P=QR.\] Given a stated threshold \(t\), the leading diagonal block of \(R\) whose pivots exceed \(t\) supplies a rank estimate and the permutation identifies a candidate independent row subset. Unless a strong rank-revealing guarantee or subsequent SVD verification is supplied, thresholded QR pivots are rank estimates rather than singular-value-equivalent certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pivoted QR of the transpose estimates row rank and proposes independent rows, but ordinary QR pivot thresholds are not automatically equivalent to singular-value thresholding.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) with \(m\le n\).
The pivoting rule, pivot ordering, and threshold convention are stated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted leading pivots of \(R\) define a rank-revealing estimate and a candidate independent row subset, not an unconditional singular-value rank identity.

notation.meaning: Permutation selecting columns of \(A^{\mathsf T}\), equivalently rows of A.

knowledge_statements.title: Column-Pivoted QR Rank-Revealing Variant

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numerical rank and complete thresholded null spaces from a full SVD.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A=U\Sigma V^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) be a full SVD, let \(p=\min\{m,n\}\), and choose \(\tau_a,\tau_r\ge0\). Set \[t=\max\{\tau_a,\tau_r\sigma_1(A)\},\qquad r_t=\#\{i\le p:\sigma_i(A)>t\}.\] With singular vectors ordered consistently, \(\operatorname{span}\{u_{r_t+1},\ldots,u_m\}\) is the complete thresholded left-null subspace and \(\operatorname{span}\{v_{r_t+1},\ldots,v_n\}\) is the complete thresholded right-null subspace. Unpaired vectors occurring in rectangular matrices must be retained when complete bases are requested; a thin SVD does not explicitly return every such direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Threshold a full SVD using an explicit absolute-relative convention and retain all trailing singular vectors, including unpaired rectangular directions, when complete approximate null-space bases are required.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\).
\(\tau_a,\tau_r\ge0\), and the strict comparison \(\sigma_i>t\) is reported.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_t=\#\{i\le\min(m,n):\sigma_i(A)>\max(\tau_a,\tau_r\sigma_1(A))\}\), with thresholded left- and right-null dimensions \(m-r_t\) and \(n-r_t\).

notation.meaning: Factors of a full singular value decomposition.

knowledge_statements.title: Dimension-Complete Thresholded-SVD Detection

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correct interpretation of vectors discarded by a numerical-rank test.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\|y\|_2=1\) and \(\|A^{\mathsf T}y\|_2\le t\), then \(y\) is an approximate row-dependency witness with residual \(\|A^{\mathsf T}y\|_2\). If \(\|v\|_2=1\) and \(\|Av\|_2\le t\), then \(v\) is an approximate right-null witness. The rank-one perturbations \[E=-y(y^{\mathsf T}A),\qquad F=-(Av)v^{\mathsf T}\] satisfy \((A+E)^{\mathsf T}y=0\), \((A+F)v=0\), \(\|E\|_2=\|A^{\mathsf T}y\|_2\), and \(\|F\|_2=\|Av\|_2\). These are backward-error certificates, not exact dependencies of the original matrix unless the corresponding residual is zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate null vectors must carry residuals; they certify proximity to a matrix having the asserted dependency, not exact dependence of the original matrix.
assumptions_latex: The candidate vectors have unit Euclidean norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A null residual at most \(t\) certifies a spectral-norm perturbation at most \(t\) that makes the candidate vector exactly null.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Qualified Approximate Null Certificates

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dense SVD–QR Cost and Output Tradeoff
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Principal dense costs for numerical-rank detection of a wide constraint matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For dense \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) with \(m\le n\), a thin SVD and column-pivoted QR of \(A^{\mathsf T}\) require \(O(nm^2)\) arithmetic and \(O(nm)\) base storage in classical dense implementations. Pivoted QR usually has smaller constants and directly proposes independent rows; the SVD directly supplies singular values and residual-optimal singular directions. Explicitly accumulating a full \(n\times n\) right singular-vector matrix requires \(O(n^2)\) storage and may require more work than thin rank detection. Materializing a complete right thresholded-null basis itself requires \(O(n(n-r_t))\) output storage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Thin dense SVD and pivoted QR share the usual order-n-m-squared rank-detection cost, while explicitly producing a full rectangular null-space basis can dominate storage and additional work.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is dense and \(m\le n\).
Classical dense factorizations are used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Thin rank detection costs \(O(nm^2)\) arithmetic and \(O(nm)\) base storage; explicit right-null output requires \(O(n(n-r_t))\) storage.
review_flags: leading constants, workspace, and full-vector accumulation costs depend on implementation
knowledge_statements.title: Dense SVD–QR Cost and Output Tradeoff

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational limits of finite-precision numerical-rank decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Numerical rank is a property of \((A,t)\), not of \(A\) alone. Singular values close to \(t\) can cross the threshold under perturbations of comparable size. Absolute thresholds change under scalar rescaling, while relative singular-value thresholds are invariant under scalar rescaling but generally change under unequal row or column scaling. For \(A=\operatorname{Diag}(1,\delta)\) with \(\delta>0\), a threshold exceeding \(\delta\) reports numerical rank one although \(A\) has exact rank two. Consequently, a thresholded deficient rank cannot alone justify exact row deletion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Numerical rank depends on threshold and scaling, is ambiguous without separation from the threshold, and cannot alone certify exact redundancy.
assumptions_latex: \(t\ge0\) is the reported numerical threshold.
Data or factorization errors may perturb the computed singular values or pivots.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Values near \(t\) make the detected rank unstable, and a reported numerical rank can be smaller than the exact algebraic rank.
knowledge_statements.title: Threshold, Scaling, and Spectral-Gap Boundary
Numerical Rank Detection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Singular-value rank decision under an explicit absolute-relative threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), absolute tolerance \(\tau_a\ge0\), and relative tolerance \(\tau_r\ge0\), compute singular values \(\sigma_1\ge\cdots\ge\sigma_p\ge0\), where \(p=\min\{m,n\}\). Set
\[t=\max\{\tau_a,\tau_r\sigma_1\},\qquad r_{\mathrm{num}}=\#\{i:\sigma_i>t\}.\]
Return \(r_{\mathrm{num}}\), the right singular vectors with \(\sigma_i\le t\) as an approximate null-space basis, and the left singular vectors with \(\sigma_i\le t\) as approximate row-dependency certificates. The strict comparison convention must accompany the reported rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute an SVD, count singular values above an explicit absolute-relative threshold, and return discarded singular vectors as approximate dependency certificates.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\).
\(\tau_a,	6\tau_r\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_{\mathrm{num}}=\#\{i:\sigma_i(A)>\max(\tau_a,\tau_r\sigma_1(A))\}\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: thresholded SVD is the canonical numerical-rank test

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Thresholded SVD is an appropriate algorithmic role, but the exact absolute-relative convention and returned certificates need a source; an assumption also contains a corrupted tau token.

knowledge_statements.title: Central-Path Scale Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic barrier scaling under convergence to a strictly complementary solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((x(\mu),y(\mu),s(\mu))\) lie on the primal-dual central path, so \(x_i(\mu)s_i(\mu)=\mu\) for every \(i\), and suppose it converges as \(\mu\downarrow0\) to a strictly complementary solution. Define \(B=\{i:x_i^*>0\}\) and \(N=\{i:s_i^*>0\}\). Then
\[i\in B:\ x_i(\mu)=\Theta(1),\ s_i(\mu)=\Theta(\mu),\qquad i\in N:\ x_i(\mu)=\Theta(\mu),\ s_i(\mu)=\Theta(1).\]
Consequently, the diagonal scaling \(W(\mu)=X(\mu)S(\mu)^{-1}\) has entries of order \(\mu^{-1}\) on \(B\) and \(\mu\) on \(N\), producing order \(\mu^{-2}\) separation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a strictly complementary limit, central-path primal-dual ratios grow like 1/mu on primal-positive indices and shrink like mu on dual-positive indices.
assumptions_latex: The central path exists for \(\mu>0\) and converges as \(\mu\downarrow0\).
The limiting solution is strictly complementary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W_{ii}(\mu)=\Theta(\mu^{-1})\) on \(B\) and \(W_{ii}(\mu)=\Theta(\mu)\) on \(N\).

notation.meaning: Strictly complementary primal-positive and dual-positive index sets.

assumptions_latex: \((x(\mu),s(\mu))\) lies on the exact central path.
The limit is strictly complementary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mu A W(\mu)A^{\mathsf T}\to A_B\operatorname{diag}((x_B^*)^2)A_B^{\mathsf T}.

notation.meaning: Columns of the constraint matrix indexed by the strictly complementary partition.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normal-equation decomposition induced by strict-complementarity scale separation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the strictly complementary partition \(B=\{i:x_i^*>0\}\), \(N=\{i:s_i^*>0\}\) and exact complementarity \(x_i(\mu)s_i(\mu)=\mu\), \[W_B(\mu)=\mu^{-1}\operatorname{diag}(x_B(\mu)^2),\qquad W_N(\mu)=\mu\operatorname{diag}(s_N(\mu)^{-2}).\] Writing \(A=[A_B\ A_N]\), \[AW A^{\mathsf T}=\mu^{-1}A_B\operatorname{diag}(x_B^2)A_B^{\mathsf T}+\mu A_N\operatorname{diag}(s_N^{-2})A_N^{\mathsf T},\] and therefore \[\mu AWA^{\mathsf T}\longrightarrow A_B\operatorname{diag}((x_B^*)^2)A_B^{\mathsf T}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict complementarity splits the barrier normal matrix into a primal-positive term of order one over mu and a dual-positive term of order mu.
knowledge_statements.title: Asymptotic Normal-Matrix Decomposition

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive complementarity family showing both free degenerate ratio rates and resulting normal-equation ill-conditioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(0<a<\tfrac12\) and define \[x(\mu)=\begin{bmatrix}\mu^a\\\mu^{1-a}\end{bmatrix},\qquad s(\mu)=\begin{bmatrix}\mu^{1-a}\\\mu^a\end{bmatrix}.\] Both complementary pairs satisfy \(x_i(\mu)s_i(\mu)=\mu\) and converge to \((0,0)\), while \[W(\mu)=\operatorname{diag}\!\left(\mu^{2a-1},\mu^{1-2a}\right).\] For \(A=I_2\), \(H(\mu)=AW(\mu)A^{\mathsf T}=W(\mu)\) and \[\kappa_2(H(\mu))=\mu^{4a-2}\to\infty.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two degenerate complementary pairs can approach zero at reciprocal free rates and make the resulting weighted normal matrix arbitrarily ill-conditioned.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_i(\mu)s_i(\mu)=\mu,\quad x_i(\mu),s_i(\mu)\to0,\quad \kappa_2(H(\mu))\to\infty.
review_flags: This is a positive complementarity and normal-matrix family; it is not asserted to be the central path of a specified fixed LP.
knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate Scaling and Ill-Conditioning Family

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise degeneracy relevant to late-iteration barrier scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a positive complementarity path satisfying \(x_i(\mu)s_i(\mu)=\mu\) and converging to \((x^*,s^*)\), index \(i\) is a degenerate limiting complementarity component when \[x_i^*=s_i^*=0.\] The product equation alone then does not determine the quotient \(x_i(\mu)/s_i(\mu)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A component is degenerate when both its limiting primal variable and matching slack vanish.
assumptions_latex: \(x_i(\mu)s_i(\mu)=\mu\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: i\text{ is degenerate}\iff x_i^*=s_i^*=0.
knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate Limiting Complementarity Component

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additional condition converting degenerate scaling freedom into normal-equation ill-conditioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W(\mu)=\operatorname{diag}(x_i(\mu)/s_i(\mu))\succ0\) and \(H(\mu)=AW(\mu)A^{\mathsf T}\succ0\). For any unit vectors \(u(\mu),v(\mu)\), \[\kappa_2(H(\mu))\ge \frac{u(\mu)^{\mathsf T}H(\mu)u(\mu)}{v(\mu)^{\mathsf T}H(\mu)v(\mu)}.\] Therefore degeneracy forces unbounded conditioning only when its scaling rates create diverging weighted-curvature ratios; degeneracy alone implies no universal condition-number rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Degeneracy yields unbounded conditioning only when its free scaling rates separate weighted curvature in different constraint directions.
assumptions_latex: \(W(\mu)\succ0\).
\(H(\mu)=AW(\mu)A^{\mathsf T}\succ0\).
\(u(\mu)\) and \(v(\mu)\) are unit vectors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \frac{u^{\mathsf T}Hu}{v^{\mathsf T}Hv}\to\infty\Rightarrow\kappa_2(H)\to\infty.
knowledge_statements.title: Directional-Curvature Conditioning Boundary
Degeneracy-Driven Ill-Conditioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of uniform Newton-system conditioning near a degenerate optimal face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(W(\mu)=X(\mu)S(\mu)^{-1}\) and \(H(\mu)=AW(\mu)A^{\mathsf T}\) along a central path. If the limiting solution is degenerate, some index may satisfy \(x_i^*=s_i^*=0\); complementarity \(x_i(\mu)s_i(\mu)=\mu\) then does not determine a uniform bound on \(x_i(\mu)/s_i(\mu)\). More generally, for unit vectors \(u,v\),
\[\kappa_2(H(\mu))\ge \frac{u^{\mathsf T}H(\mu)u}{v^{\mathsf T}H(\mu)v}\]
whenever the denominator is positive. Thus diverging weighted curvature in one constraint direction and vanishing curvature in another forces unbounded conditioning; strict feasibility alone does not prevent this late-iteration failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At degenerate limits, complementarity need not control primal-dual ratios; unequal weighted curvature can therefore make barrier normal equations arbitrarily ill-conditioned.
assumptions_latex: \(W(\mu)\succ0\) and \(H(\mu)\) is positive definite for each \(\mu>0\).
The central path approaches a degenerate optimal solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If a Rayleigh-quotient ratio for \(H(\mu)\) diverges, then \(\kappa_2(H(\mu))\to\infty\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional Rayleigh-quotient conclusion is correct and fits a failure-boundary container, but a general central-path locator does not specifically support the degeneracy-driven conditioning claim.

assumptions_latex: The stated diagonal elimination order and matrix-maximum scale are used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \pi_{\min}(I)=1\quad\text{but}\quad\pi_{\min}(\operatorname{diag}(\alpha,1))=\alpha.

notation.meaning: Smallest pivot magnitude divided by the largest matrix-entry magnitude.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counterexample to invariance of a matrix-scale-relative pivot diagnostic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the equivalent systems \[Iz=b,\qquad \operatorname{diag}(\alpha,1)z=\operatorname{diag}(\alpha,1)b,\qquad 0<\alpha<1.\] With diagonal elimination in the displayed order, the first system has pivots \(1,1\) and relative minimum pivot \(1\). The row-scaled system has pivots \(\alpha,1\), matrix scale \(1\), and relative minimum pivot \(\alpha\). Both systems have the same exact solution, yet the diagnostic can be made arbitrarily small as \(\alpha\downarrow0\). Thus any pivot threshold must be reported with its scaling and pivoting conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equivalent row scaling can make a relative minimum pivot arbitrarily small without changing the exact solution.
knowledge_statements.title: Small-Pivot Classification Is Scaling Dependent

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar-factorization-relative definition using the active-column scale controlled by the chosen elimination model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For scalar Gaussian or \(LDL^{\mathsf T}\) elimination at step \(k\), let \(p_k\ne0\) be the pivot and let \[s_k:=\max_i|a_{ik}^{(k)}|\] over entries in the active column eligible for elimination. Given a declared threshold \(0<\tau_{\mathrm{piv}}<1\), step \(k\) is in the small-pivot regime when \[|p_k|/s_k\le\tau_{\mathrm{piv}}.\] When this occurs, some elimination multiplier has magnitude at least \(1/\tau_{\mathrm{piv}}\). The classification is relative to the scaling, ordering, pivoting rule, arithmetic, and threshold, and does not prove exact singularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scalar pivot is operationally small when it is tiny relative to the active entries it must eliminate, thereby creating a large multiplier.
assumptions_latex: A declared scalar Gaussian or \(LDL^{\mathsf T}\) elimination model is used.
\(0<\tau_{\mathrm{piv}}<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |p_k|/s_k\le\tau_{\mathrm{piv}}\Rightarrow\max_i|a_{ik}^{(k)}/p_k|\ge1/\tau_{\mathrm{piv}}.

notation.meaning: Active-column elimination scale at step k.

review_flags: Block-pivot factorizations require the analogous local block-solve or inverse-pivot-block diagnostic.
knowledge_statements.title: Local-Scale Small-Pivot Regime

assumptions_latex: The computed Newton system is \(K\Delta z=r\), with nonsingular exact-arithmetic matrix \(K\in\mathbb{R}^{q\times q}\).
A floating-point factorization applies pivots \(p_1,\ldots,p_q\), with scale \(\sigma_K=\max_{i,j}|K_{ij}|>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\pi_{\min}\le \tau_{\mathrm{piv}}\), the solve is in the small-pivot regime and its step must not be accepted without a residual or backward-error check.

notation.meaning: Smallest pivot relative to the matrix scale.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational floating-point boundary for a late-iteration Newton factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the relative minimum pivot by \(\pi_{\min}:=\min_{1\le k\le q}|p_k|/\sigma_K\). For a prescribed reliability threshold \(\tau_{\mathrm{piv}}>0\), the factorization enters the small-pivot regime when
\[
\pi_{\min}\le \tau_{\mathrm{piv}}.
\]
This condition indicates that division by at least one pivot can strongly amplify rounding error relative to the scale of \(K\). It is a failure boundary, not a proof that the exact Newton system is singular: the computed step is classified as unreliable unless an independent scaled residual or backward-error test succeeds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A factorization enters the small-pivot regime when its smallest pivot, relative to the matrix scale, falls below a chosen reliability threshold.
knowledge_statements.title: Small-Pivot Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure boundary depends on the factorization, pivoting strategy, scaling, arithmetic model, and solver-specific threshold. No cited source supports the proposed metric or the mandatory acceptance rule.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonsingularity Does Not Prevent Algorithmic Breakdown
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal counterexample separating matrix nonsingularity from success of an unpivoted factorization attempt.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\begin{bmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{bmatrix}\). Since \(\det K=-1\), \(K\) is nonsingular, but elimination requiring \(K_{11}\) as its first scalar pivot breaks down because \(K_{11}=0\). A row interchange or an admissible \(2\times2\) symmetric-indefinite pivot permits factorization. Thus breakdown of a specified factorization attempt does not establish singularity of \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonsingular matrix can immediately break an unpivoted factorization, while suitable pivoting factors the same system.
assumptions_latex: Gaussian elimination is attempted without row or symmetric pivoting.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The nonsingular matrix \(K\) causes zero-pivot breakdown for the specified unpivoted method but is factorable with suitable pivoting.

notation.meaning: Nonsingular coefficient matrix with a zero leading diagonal entry.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonsingularity Does Not Prevent Algorithmic Breakdown

assumptions_latex: A floating-point solver attempts to factor the Newton matrix \(K\) using a specified pivoting and arithmetic model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Occurrence of any listed event classifies the attempted factorization as broken and triggers solve-failure recovery.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational breakdown predicate for direct Newton-system factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Factorization breakdown occurs if the attempted factorization of \(K\) cannot produce finite usable factors. Concretely, the predicate is true when at least one of the following occurs: a required pivot is zero or rejected by the pivoting rule; an arithmetic operation produces a nonfinite entry in \(\widehat L\), \(\widehat D\), or \(\widehat U\); the factorization routine reports structural or numerical singularity; or triangular solution with the computed factors cannot return a finite candidate step. Breakdown prevents certification of a Newton step from that factorization, irrespective of the termination measures of the outer barrier iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Factorization has broken down when rejected pivots, singularity reports, nonfinite factors, or failed triangular solves prevent production of a usable Newton step.
knowledge_statements.title: Factorization Breakdown

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The listed breakdown events are plausible, and failure_boundary fits the leaf, but their exact operational scope depends on the factorization interface and solver model. No source is supplied.

assumptions_latex: The intended linear system is \(K\Delta z=r\), and a finite candidate \(\widehat{\Delta z}\) has been computed.
The scaling denominator is nonzero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The step is unreliable whenever \(\eta_{\mathrm{lin}}>\tau_{\mathrm{lin}}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A posteriori reliability test for a computed barrier Newton step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a consistent subordinate norm, define
\[
\eta_{\mathrm{lin}}:=\frac{\|r-K\widehat{\Delta z}\|}{\|K\|\,\|\widehat{\Delta z}\|+\|r\|}.
\]
Given a prescribed tolerance \(\tau_{\mathrm{lin}}>0\), the computed step has an acceptable normwise residual certificate when \(\eta_{\mathrm{lin}}\le\tau_{\mathrm{lin}}\). It is classified as having an unreliable step residual when \(\eta_{\mathrm{lin}}>\tau_{\mathrm{lin}}\), or when the numerator or denominator evaluation is nonfinite. This certificate concerns the computed linear solve only; it does not by itself certify feasibility, positivity, or sufficient decrease of the outer primal-dual iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A computed Newton step is unreliable when its normwise scaled linear-system residual exceeds the prescribed tolerance or cannot be evaluated finitely.
knowledge_statements.title: Unreliable Step Residuals

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scaled residual is a standard normwise diagnostic and certificate is a defensible kind, but the precise reliability classification and treatment of nonfinite evaluations require an authoritative numerical-linear-algebra or solver source.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact residual dynamics explaining contraction and stagnation when refinement repeatedly uses unchanged factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For stationary refinement \(z_{j+1}=z_j+Mr_j\), where \(r_j=r-Kz_j\), the residuals satisfy \[r_{j+1}=(I-KM)r_j.\] Thus \(\|I-KM\|=q<1\) implies \(\|r_j\|\le q^j\|r_0\|\). Conversely, if \(I-KM\) has a real eigenpair \((\lambda,v)\) with \(|\lambda|\ge1\), then \(r_0=v\) gives \(r_j=\lambda^jv\), so the residual does not contract. Unchanged factors therefore cannot universally cure error when their correction operator has a noncontracting residual mode.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed-factor refinement repeatedly applies one residual-propagation matrix; contraction gives geometric improvement, while a mode of magnitude at least one stagnates or diverges.
assumptions_latex: The intended system is \(Kz=r\).
Each correction is \(c_j=Mr_j\) for a fixed linear operator \(M\).
The update is \(z_{j+1}=z_j+c_j\), and the displayed recurrence is interpreted in exact arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_{j+1}=(I-KM)r_j\); if \(\|I-KM\|<1\), residuals converge geometrically, while a real eigenmode with modulus at least one does not contract.

notation.meaning: Fixed correction-solve operator induced by retained factors.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual Propagation Under Fixed Refinement

assumptions_latex: Iterative refinement produces finite iterates \(\Delta z^{(0)},\Delta z^{(1)},\ldots\) for \(K\Delta z=r\).
Scaled residuals \(\eta_j\) are evaluated consistently after each correction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Refinement stagnates if \(\eta_j>\tau_{\mathrm{lin}}\) and \(\eta_{j+1}\ge\rho_{\min}\eta_j\) for \(m\) consecutive corrections.

notation.meaning: Scaled residual after refinement correction j.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational nonprogress boundary for residual-based iterative refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\eta_j\) be the scaled residual of the candidate after correction \(j\). Fix a target \(\tau_{\mathrm{lin}}>0\), a required contraction \(\rho_{\min}\in(0,1)\), and an integer window \(m\ge1\). Refinement is stagnating at index \(j\) if \(\eta_j>\tau_{\mathrm{lin}}\) and
\[
\eta_{k+1}\ge\rho_{\min}\eta_k
\]
for every \(k=j-m+1,\ldots,j\). It also stagnates immediately if a correction or residual becomes nonfinite. Once this predicate holds, further corrections using the unchanged factors are not accepted as a recovery mechanism; refactorization, changed regularization, or another representation is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Iterative refinement stagnates when residuals remain above tolerance and fail to contract sufficiently for a prescribed number of consecutive corrections.
knowledge_statements.title: Stagnating Refinement

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The windowed contraction predicate and prescribed recovery response are implementation choices rather than a universal refinement boundary. They require a source specifying the indexing, parameters, and recovery policy.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Regularized Solve Can Miss the Original Equation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar family showing that zero regularized residual does not control the original Newton residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K=[1]\), \(r=[1]\), and \(R=[M]\) with \(M>0\), the exact regularized solution is \(\widehat d=(1+M)^{-1}\). Its regularized residual is zero, but its original residual has magnitude \[|K\widehat d-r|=\frac{M}{1+M}\to1\quad\text{as }M\to\infty,\] while the intended solution is \(d=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even an exact solve of a strongly regularized scalar equation can have an original-equation residual approaching the full right-hand-side magnitude.
assumptions_latex: The candidate is accepted only provisionally from the regularized equation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((K+R)\widehat d-r=0\) while \(|K\widehat d-r|=M/(1+M)\to1\).
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Regularized Solve Can Miss the Original Equation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative regime in which additive stabilization remains a controlled perturbation of the intended Newton equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d=K^{-1}r\), \(\widehat d=(K+R)^{-1}r\), and \(q=\|K^{-1}R\|\) in a subordinate norm. If \(q<1\), then \(K+R\) is nonsingular and \[\|\widehat d-d\|\le\frac{q}{1-q}\|d\|.\] Thus regularization is a controlled perturbation when \(q\) is bounded away from one. Without such control, a small residual for the regularized equation alone gives no relative-error guarantee for the solution of \(Kd=r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If regularization is small relative to the inverse Newton operator, its solution stays close to the intended one; otherwise the regularized residual alone gives no such guarantee.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is nonsingular.
\(d=K^{-1}r\) and \(\widehat d=(K+R)^{-1}r\).
A subordinate norm satisfies \(q=\|K^{-1}R\|<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K+R\) is nonsingular and \(\|\widehat d-d\|\le q(1-q)^{-1}\|d\|\).
knowledge_statements.title: Perturbative Regularization Regime

assumptions_latex: The unregularized Newton equation is \(K\Delta z=r\), while the computed step solves \((K+R)\widehat{\Delta z}\approx r\).
The selected norm and dominance threshold \(\tau_{\mathrm{reg}}\in(0,1)\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Regularization dominates when \(\delta_{\mathrm{reg}}>\tau_{\mathrm{reg}}\), so a small regularized residual does not certify the original Newton equation.

notation.meaning: Regularization matrix added for numerical stabilization.
Relative perturbation contribution at the computed step.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary where stabilization perturbation overwhelms the intended Newton equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a finite computed step with positive denominator, define
\[
\delta_{\mathrm{reg}}:=\frac{\|R\widehat{\Delta z}\|}{\max\{\|r\|,\|K\widehat{\Delta z}\|\}}.
\]
Regularization is dominant when \(\delta_{\mathrm{reg}}>\tau_{\mathrm{reg}}\). Indeed, from \((K+R)\widehat{\Delta z}-r\) being small it does not follow that \(K\widehat{\Delta z}-r\) is small, because
\[
K\widehat{\Delta z}-r=((K+R)\widehat{\Delta z}-r)-R\widehat{\Delta z}.
\]
Thus a step in the dominance regime cannot be accepted solely on the regularized-system residual; the residual of the original Newton equation must be checked.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Regularization dominates when its contribution to the computed equation exceeds a chosen fraction of the original equation's scale.
knowledge_statements.title: Regularization Dominance

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The residual identity is correct, but the proposed normalization and dominance threshold are not canonical. A source is needed to establish this particular failure boundary and its acceptance consequence.

assumptions_latex: The current Newton solve has failed an accepted factorization, residual, refinement, or regularization test.
Each fallback candidate can be mapped to the same primal-dual step variables and independently residual-checked.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Return the first candidate satisfying \(\eta_{\mathrm{lin}}\le\tau_{\mathrm{lin}}\); otherwise return solve failure.

notation.meaning: Ordered collection of alternative system representations or solvers.
Scaled residual in the original Newton equation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic recovery algorithm after failure of the preferred Newton solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input the original Newton equation \(K\Delta z=r\), tolerance \(\tau_{\mathrm{lin}}>0\), and ordered fallbacks \(\mathcal{F}=(F_1,\ldots,F_m)\). For \(i=1,\ldots,m\), form the system representation required by \(F_i\), compute a finite candidate \(\widehat{\Delta z}_i\), map it back to the original step variables, and evaluate its scaled residual \(\eta_{\mathrm{lin},i}\) in \(K\Delta z=r\). Stop and output the first candidate satisfying \(\eta_{\mathrm{lin},i}\le\tau_{\mathrm{lin}}\). If factorization fails, the candidate is nonfinite, or the residual test fails, continue to \(F_{i+1}\). If no fallback passes, output solve failure and do not update the barrier iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Try alternative representations or solvers in order, accepting only a finite step that passes a residual test in the original Newton equation.
knowledge_statements.title: Representation or Solver Fallback

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm fits the recovery leaf, but the ordered first-passing fallback policy, representation-equivalence requirements, and residual-only acceptance rule need solver or algorithmic documentation.

children.top_down_role: Outer termination, accuracy interpretation, and solver-status separation for finite-precision LP barrier computations.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Interior-Point Termination Criterion; Problem and Solution Status

assumptions_latex: The primal linear program is \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\).
The residual scaling denominator is positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Primal feasibility to tolerance \(\varepsilon_p\) holds when \(\eta_p\le\varepsilon_p\) and \(v_p\le\varepsilon_p\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Norm-scaled primal feasibility measures for standard-form linear programming.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a candidate \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), define the scaled equality residual and nonnegativity violation by
\[
\eta_p:=\frac{\|Ax-b\|}{1+\|b\|},\qquad v_p:=\frac{\|(-x)_+\|}{1+\|x\|},
\]
where \(((-x)_+)_i=\max\{-x_i,0\}\). Given \(\varepsilon_p\ge0\), the candidate is primal feasible to tolerance when both \(\eta_p\le\varepsilon_p\) and \(v_p\le\varepsilon_p\). If the barrier method maintains \(x>0\) explicitly, then \(v_p=0\), and the equality residual alone determines this termination component.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal feasibility is measured by a scaled equality residual and a scaled violation of nonnegativity; both must lie below tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Feasibility Measures

assumptions_latex: The dual linear program is \(\max\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\ s\ge0\}\).
The residual scaling denominator is positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dual feasibility to tolerance \(\varepsilon_d\) holds when \(\eta_d\le\varepsilon_d\) and \(v_d\le\varepsilon_d\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Norm-scaled dual feasibility measures for standard-form linear programming.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a candidate \((y,s)\in\mathbb{R}^m\times\mathbb{R}^n\), define
\[
\eta_d:=\frac{\|A^{\mathsf T}y+s-c\|}{1+\|c\|},\qquad v_d:=\frac{\|(-s)_+\|}{1+\|s\|},
\]
where \(((-s)_+)_i=\max\{-s_i,0\}\). Given \(\varepsilon_d\ge0\), the candidate is dual feasible to tolerance when both \(\eta_d\le\varepsilon_d\) and \(v_d\le\varepsilon_d\). If the barrier method maintains \(s>0\) explicitly, then \(v_d=0\), leaving the dual equality residual as this termination component.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual feasibility is measured by a scaled stationarity residual and a scaled violation of slack nonnegativity; both must lie below tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Feasibility Measures

children.title: Componentwise Complementarity Measures
children.top_down_role: Per-component indicators used in barrier termination assessment.

assumptions_latex: The primal and dual variables satisfy \(x,s\in\mathbb{R}_+^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Componentwise complementarity to tolerance \(\varepsilon_c\) holds exactly when \(\|XSe\|_\infty\le\varepsilon_c\).

notation.meaning: Diagonal matrices formed from primal variables and dual slacks.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maximum-product complementarity measure for nonnegative primal variables and dual slacks.

source_refs.locator: Primal-Dual Methods: Development of the Fundamental Ideas p. 43

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X:=\operatorname{diag}(x)\), \(S:=\operatorname{diag}(s)\), and let \(e\) be the all-ones vector. The complementarity products are
\[
XSe=(x_1s_1,\ldots,x_ns_n)^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Define the componentwise measure \(\chi_\infty:=\|XSe\|_\infty=\max_i x_is_i\). For a tolerance \(\varepsilon_c\ge0\), componentwise complementarity holds to tolerance precisely when \(x_is_i\le\varepsilon_c\) for every \(i\), equivalently \(\chi_\infty\le\varepsilon_c\). At \(\varepsilon_c=0\), this reduces to the exact complementary-slackness equations \(x_is_i=0\) for all indices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Componentwise complementarity uses the largest primal-variable times dual-slack product and requires every such product to be below tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Componentwise Complementarity Measures

source_witnesses.locator: Primal-Dual Methods: Development of the Fundamental Ideas p. 43

children.title: Aggregate Complementarity Measures
children.top_down_role: Scalar summaries of complementarity across primal-dual components.

assumptions_latex: The primal and dual variables satisfy \(x,s\in\mathbb{R}_+^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The aggregate complementarity measure is \(\mu=x^{\mathsf T}s/n\), and \(\mu=0\) exactly when all complementarity products vanish.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sum and average of nonnegative primal-dual complementarity products.

source_refs.locator: Primal-Dual Methods: Development of the Fundamental Ideas p. 43

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x,s\in\mathbb{R}_+^n\), define the aggregate complementarity sum and its average by
\[
g_c:=x^{\mathsf T}s=\sum_{i=1}^n x_is_i,\qquad \mu:=\frac{x^{\mathsf T}s}{n}.
\]
Because every product \(x_is_i\) is nonnegative, \(g_c=0\), \(\mu=0\), and \(x_is_i=0\) for every \(i\) are equivalent. For \(\varepsilon_c\ge0\), the average-based termination condition is \(\mu\le\varepsilon_c\); equivalently, \(g_c\le n\varepsilon_c\). This aggregate test controls the sum but can conceal disparity among individual products when \(\varepsilon_c>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Aggregate complementarity is the sum or average of all nonnegative primal-variable times dual-slack products.
knowledge_statements.title: Aggregate Complementarity Measures

source_witnesses.locator: Primal-Dual Methods: Development of the Fundamental Ideas p. 43

children.title: Absolute Duality Gap
children.top_down_role: Unnormalized objective-gap assessment for finite-precision stopping.

assumptions_latex: The primal and dual objectives are \(c^{\mathsf T}x\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}y\), respectively.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The absolute duality gap is \(g_{\mathrm{abs}}=|c^{\mathsf T}x-b^{\mathsf T}y|\); under primal and dual feasibility it equals \(x^{\mathsf T}s\).

notation.meaning: Absolute difference between primal and dual objective values.
Dual slack satisfying the dual equality when feasible.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-gap measure and its feasible primal-dual complementarity identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For any candidate objective values, define
\[
g_{\mathrm{abs}}:=\left|c^{\mathsf T}x-b^{\mathsf T}y\right|.
\]
If \(Ax=b\), \(A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c\), and \(x,s\ge0\), then weak duality gives \(c^{\mathsf T}x-b^{\mathsf T}y\ge0\), and
\[
c^{\mathsf T}x-b^{\mathsf T}y=x^{\mathsf T}(c-A^{\mathsf T}y)=x^{\mathsf T}s.
\]
Consequently, for feasible primal-dual candidates, the absolute duality gap equals aggregate complementarity. Without feasibility, this identity need not hold, so an objective-gap termination test must be accompanied by primal- and dual-feasibility tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The absolute duality gap is the objective-value difference in magnitude; for feasible primal-dual points it equals total complementarity.
knowledge_statements.title: Absolute Duality Gap

children.title: Relative Duality Gap
children.top_down_role: Scale-aware objective-gap assessment for finite-precision stopping.

assumptions_latex: The primal and dual objective values \(p=c^{\mathsf T}x\) and \(d=b^{\mathsf T}y\) are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The relative gap is \(g_{\mathrm{rel}}=|p-d|/(1+|p|+|d|)\), and it lies in \([0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symmetrically scaled relative objective-gap convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(p:=c^{\mathsf T}x\) and \(d:=b^{\mathsf T}y\). Under the symmetric normalization convention, define
\[
g_{\mathrm{rel}}:=\frac{|p-d|}{1+|p|+|d|}.
\]
The denominator is strictly positive, and the triangle inequality implies \(0\le g_{\mathrm{rel}}<1\). For a tolerance \(\varepsilon_g\ge0\), the relative-gap termination condition is \(g_{\mathrm{rel}}\le\varepsilon_g\). This normalization is invariant under neither objective translation nor arbitrary rescaling, so the convention must be fixed when solver statuses are compared. Feasibility must be checked separately because a small relative objective difference alone does not certify near-optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The relative duality gap divides the absolute objective difference by one plus the magnitudes of both objectives; feasibility remains a separate requirement.
knowledge_statements.title: Relative Duality Gap

children.title: Measure Disagreement Regimes
children.top_down_role: Cases where complementarity and gap indicators support different stopping interpretations.

knowledge_statements.title: Measure Disagreement Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimension-dependent disagreement between nonnegative componentwise and aggregate complementarity tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\in\mathbb N\) with \(n\ge1\), and let \(x,s\in\mathbb R_+^n\). Define \(g_{\max}:=\max_{1\le i\le n}x_i s_i\) and \(g_{\Sigma}:=x^{\mathsf T}s\). Then \[g_{\max}\le g_{\Sigma}\le n g_{\max}.\] Consequently, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), \(g_{\Sigma}\le\varepsilon\) implies \(g_{\max}\le\varepsilon\), while \(g_{\max}\le\varepsilon\) implies \(g_{\Sigma}\le n\varepsilon\). Thus the two tests can return different decisions when they use the same numerical tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Aggregate acceptance implies componentwise acceptance at the same tolerance, while componentwise acceptance guarantees aggregate acceptance only at a tolerance larger by a factor of n.
assumptions_latex: \(n\in\mathbb N\) and \(n\ge1\).
\(x,s\in\mathbb R_+^n\).
A common tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\) is used when comparing the two tests.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_{\max}\le g_{\Sigma}\le n g_{\max}\), with the stated dimension-dependent tolerance implications.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal example showing that objective-gap acceptance without feasibility tests does not control complementarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the one-variable standard-form data \(A=[1]\), \(b=0\), and \(c=0\), take \(x=1\), \(y=0\), and \(s=1\). Then \[|c^{\mathsf T}x-b^{\mathsf T}y|=0,\qquad x^{\mathsf T}s=\max_i x_is_i=1,\] while \(r_p=Ax-b=1\) and \(r_d=A^{\mathsf T}y+s-c=1\). Thus absolute and ordinarily normalized relative objective-gap tests accept even though aggregate and componentwise complementarity tests reject and both feasibility residuals are nonzero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An infeasible candidate can have zero objective gap while its complementarity and feasibility residuals remain positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The objective gap is zero, whereas aggregate and componentwise complementarity equal one and both residuals are nonzero.

notation.meaning: primal and dual residuals in the example

knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Gap Infeasible Candidate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact residual correction characterizing disagreement between signed objective difference and aggregate complementarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For arbitrary candidates \((x,y,s)\), define \(r_p:=Ax-b\) and \(r_d:=A^{\mathsf T}y+s-c\). Then \[c^{\mathsf T}x-b^{\mathsf T}y=x^{\mathsf T}s+y^{\mathsf T}r_p-x^{\mathsf T}r_d.\] Hence the signed objective difference equals aggregate complementarity exactly when \(y^{\mathsf T}r_p=x^{\mathsf T}r_d\); primal and dual feasibility are sufficient but not necessary. For paired norms, \[\left|c^{\mathsf T}x-b^{\mathsf T}y-x^{\mathsf T}s\right|\le \|y\|_{p,*}\|r_p\|_p+\|x\|_{d,*}\|r_d\|_d.\] Thus small residual norms need not prevent substantial disagreement when the corresponding candidate norms are large.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The objective difference equals complementarity plus residual-weighted correction terms, so infeasibility or large candidate vectors can separate the diagnostics.
assumptions_latex: \(r_p:=Ax-b\) and \(r_d:=A^{\mathsf T}y+s-c\).
\(\|\cdot\|_{p,*}\) and \(\|\cdot\|_{d,*}\) are dual to the norms used for \(r_p\) and \(r_d\), respectively.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c^{\mathsf T}x-b^{\mathsf T}y=x^{\mathsf T}s+y^{\mathsf T}r_p-x^{\mathsf T}r_d\).
knowledge_statements.title: Residual Identity for Gap Disagreement
Absolute Accuracy Measures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unnormalized feasibility and objective-gap stopping test for standard-form linear programming.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\) define the primal problem \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\) and dual problem \(\max\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\ s\ge0\}\). Fix norms on \(\mathbb R^m\) and \(\mathbb R^n\), and let \((x,y,s)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb R^n\) and \(\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_d,\varepsilon_g\ge0\). The iterate meets these absolute accuracy tolerances when \[\|Ax-b\|\le\varepsilon_p,\qquad \|A^{\mathsf T}y+s-c\|\le\varepsilon_d,\qquad |c^{\mathsf T}x-b^{\mathsf T}y|\le\varepsilon_g.\] These unnormalized tests generally change when the equations or objective data are rescaled.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Absolute accuracy directly bounds the primal residual, dual residual, and objective gap using fixed norms and no data-dependent normalization.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\).
\((x,y,s)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb R^n\).
Norms on \(\mathbb R^m\) and \(\mathbb R^n\) are fixed by the interface.
\(\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_d,\varepsilon_g\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Absolute accuracy holds when \(\|r_p\|\le\varepsilon_p\), \(\|r_d\|\le\varepsilon_d\), and \(|g|\le\varepsilon_g\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unnormalized cone-violation components of absolute primal-dual accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a standard-form primal-dual candidate \((x,y,s)\), define \[v_x:=\|(-x)_+\|,\qquad v_s:=\|(-s)_+\|,\] where the positive part is componentwise and the norms are fixed by the interface. Absolute cone tolerances \(\varepsilon_x,\varepsilon_s\ge0\) are met when \(v_x\le\varepsilon_x\) and \(v_s\le\varepsilon_s\). Zero tolerances impose exact nonnegativity; positive tolerances permit the stated absolute violations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Absolute cone accuracy bounds the unnormalized negative parts of the primal variables and dual slacks.
assumptions_latex: \(x,s\in\mathbb R^n\).
A norm on \(\mathbb R^n\) is fixed by the interface.
\(\varepsilon_x,\varepsilon_s\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|(-x)_+\|\le\varepsilon_x\) and \(\|(-s)_+\|\le\varepsilon_s\) are the absolute primal and dual nonnegativity tests.
knowledge_statements.title: Absolute Nonnegativity-Violation Measures

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convention-independent definition of a relative stopping measure; particular data-derived denominators remain separate conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each nonnegative absolute diagnostic \(e_j\), choose a declared scale \(d_j>0\) having the same units and define \(\rho_j:=e_j/d_j\). Relative accuracy at tolerances \(\varepsilon_j\ge0\) means \(\rho_j\le\varepsilon_j\) for every diagnostic, equivalently \(e_j\le\varepsilon_jd_j\). Distinct choices of \(d_j\) define distinct relative measures and must be reported explicitly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relative diagnostic divides an absolute error by an explicitly declared positive scale; changing the scale changes the measure.
assumptions_latex: \(e_j\ge0\), \(d_j>0\), and \(\varepsilon_j\ge0\) for every diagnostic \(j\).
Each \(d_j\) has the same units as \(e_j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_j:=e_j/d_j\) and \(\rho_j\le\varepsilon_j\iff e_j\le\varepsilon_jd_j\).

notation.meaning: absolute residual, violation, or gap diagnostic

knowledge_statements.title: Declared-Scale Relative Accuracy

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limitation shared by all positive-denominator relative stopping measures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(e\ge0\), \(d>0\), and \(\rho=e/d\). Although \(\rho\le\varepsilon\) is equivalent to \(e\le\varepsilon d\), it supplies no upper bound on \(e\) depending only on \(\varepsilon\) unless \(d\) is itself bounded above. Thus relative acceptance does not imply a scale-free absolute-accuracy guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A large normalization scale can make a large absolute error pass a relative test.
assumptions_latex: \(e\ge0\), \(d>0\), and \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Without an upper bound on \(d\), \(e/d\le\varepsilon\) gives no bound on \(e\) depending only on \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.title: Scale Dependence of Relative Acceptance

assumptions_latex: The primal and dual residuals are computed for the same standard-form model.
Each denominator is protected by \(\max\{1,\cdot\}\) to remain positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Relative accuracy holds when \(\rho_p\le\varepsilon_p\), \(\rho_d\le\varepsilon_d\), and \(\rho_g\le\varepsilon_g\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One explicit denominator convention for relative primal, dual, and objective accuracy.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\) and its standard dual, define \[\rho_p:=\frac{\|Ax-b\|}{\max\{1,\|b\|\}},\quad \rho_d:=\frac{\|A^{\mathsf T}y+s-c\|}{\max\{1,\|c\|\}},\quad \rho_g:=\frac{|c^{\mathsf T}x-b^{\mathsf T}y|}{\max\{1,|c^{\mathsf T}x|,|b^{\mathsf T}y|\}}.\] The iterate has relative accuracy \((\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_d,\varepsilon_g)\) precisely when \(\rho_p\le\varepsilon_p\), \(\rho_d\le\varepsilon_d\), and \(\rho_g\le\varepsilon_g\). Other denominator conventions define different measures and must not be mixed silently.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relative accuracy divides each residual or gap by a declared positive scale, making stopping thresholds meaningful across different data magnitudes.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extreme equation scaling can hide a large original-coordinate residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the equation \(x=0\), take \(x=1\) and measure \(\eta=\alpha|x|\). For any \(\varepsilon>0\), choosing \(\alpha=\varepsilon/2\) gives \(\eta\le\varepsilon\), although the original residual is \(|x|=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An arbitrarily small equation scale can hide a unit original residual.
assumptions_latex: The scalar equation is \(x=0\).
The scaled residual is \(\eta=\alpha|x|\) with \(\alpha>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x=1,\ \alpha=\varepsilon/2\Longrightarrow\eta=\varepsilon/2\le\varepsilon\text{ while }|x|=1.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimensionally explicit diagonal equation-scaling variant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose fixed positive diagonal matrices \(R\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) and \(C\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\). For \(r_p=Ax-b\) and \(r_d=A^Ty+s-c\), define \(\eta_p^{\mathrm{diag}}=\|Rr_p\|\) and \(\eta_d^{\mathrm{diag}}=\|Cr_d\|\). These measures vanish exactly with their unscaled residuals, but their magnitudes depend on the chosen scales.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Diagonal data scaling applies fixed positive equation weights before residual norms are taken.

knowledge_statements.title: Approximate Optimality Status
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Verifiable approximate KKT certificate for a standard-form primal-dual pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\) define the original standard-form primal-dual pair. Fix norms on \(\mathbb R^m\) and \(\mathbb R^n\), and let \(\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_d,\varepsilon_x,\varepsilon_s,\varepsilon_g\ge0\). A triple \((\bar x,\bar y,\bar s)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb R^n\) is an approximate optimality certificate when \[\|A\bar x-b\|\le\varepsilon_p,\quad \|A^{\mathsf T}\bar y+\bar s-c\|\le\varepsilon_d,\quad \|(-\bar x)_+\|\le\varepsilon_x,\quad \|(-\bar s)_+\|\le\varepsilon_s,\] and \[|c^{\mathsf T}\bar x-b^{\mathsf T}\bar y|\le\varepsilon_g.\] Each quantity is recomputable from the original data. The resulting status is approximate unless all five tolerances are zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate optimality is certified in original coordinates by bounded primal and dual residuals, bounded nonnegativity violations, and a bounded objective gap under declared norms and tolerances.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact improving-ray handoff for primal unboundedness in standard form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\) define \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\). A handoff pair \((x^0,d)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^n\) certifies that the primal objective is unbounded below when \[Ax^0=b,\quad x^0\ge0,\quad Ad=0,\quad d\ge0,\quad c^{\mathsf T}d<0.\] A floating-point handoff supports an exact unboundedness status only after sound verification of the equalities, inequalities, and strict improvement margin.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A verified feasible point and a verified nonnegative null-space direction with negative objective slope certify primal unboundedness below.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Improving Ray Without a Feasible Base Point
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessity of including primal feasibility in an unboundedness-certificate handoff.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{-x:0x=1,\ x\ge0\}\). The direction \(d=1\) satisfies \(0d=0\), \(d\ge0\), and \((-1)d<0\), although the primal feasible set is empty. Thus an improving nonnegative null-space direction without a feasible base point does not certify primal unboundedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An infeasible LP can possess an improving nonnegative null-space direction, so the direction alone is not an unboundedness certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Ad=0\), \(d\ge0\), and \(c^{\mathsf T}d<0\), but \(\{x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.title: Improving Ray Without a Feasible Base Point

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent objective normalization of the handed-off improving direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D:=\{d\in\mathbb R^n:Ad=0,\ d\ge0\}\). Then \[\exists d\in D:\ c^{\mathsf T}d<0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\exists\widehat d\in D:\ c^{\mathsf T}\widehat d=-1.\] For any strict improving direction, the corresponding normalized direction is \(\widehat d=d/(-c^{\mathsf T}d)\). With a feasible base point, either form is a verifiable unboundedness handoff.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strict improving recession direction can be positively rescaled to objective slope minus one.

The returned object should retain the best available iterate, residual measures, and diagnostic reason. This status makes no mathematical assertion that the original problem is feasible, infeasible, bounded, or unbounded.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal sequence counterexample to the conclusiveness of finite-window stagnation detection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any \(w\ge1\), let \(M_0=\cdots=M_w=1\) and \(M_{w+1}=0\). A rule declaring stagnation from zero decrease over the preceding \(w\) transitions triggers at \(w\), although the next iterate improves strictly. Thus a finite-window plateau cannot, without additional assumptions, distinguish permanent failure from delayed progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A merit can remain flat throughout the observation window and then improve at the next iteration.
