assumptions_latex: Original data and iterate quantities have valid interval enclosures.
All interval operations are outward rounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M\in[L,U]\ \land\ U\le\tau\Longrightarrow M\le\tau.

notation.meaning: certified enclosure of the exact merit

review_flags: requires validated interval or directed-rounding implementation
knowledge_statements.title: Interval-Enclosure Floor Certification

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Rounded Accumulation Can Hide a Nonzero Residual
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Provides a floating-point cancellation example using representable stored inputs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In binary floating-point arithmetic with precision \(p\), let \(a=2^p\), \(b=1\), and \(c=-2^p\), all exactly representable. Round-to-nearest with ties to even gives \(\operatorname{fl}(a+b)=2^p\), hence sequential evaluation yields \(\operatorname{fl}(\operatorname{fl}(a+b)+c)=0\), while the exact sum \(a+b+c=1\). Thus a computed linear residual can vanish although its exact residual for the stored data is nonzero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rounding during dot-product accumulation can produce a zero residual even though the exact residual of the stored inputs is nonzero.
assumptions_latex: Binary round-to-nearest arithmetic with ties to even is used.
The addition is evaluated sequentially in the displayed order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat r=0\quad\text{while}\quad r=1.

notation.meaning: binary floating-point precision in significand bits

knowledge_statements.title: Rounded Accumulation Can Hide a Nonzero Residual

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a numerical floor from a validated merit-evaluation error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\ge0\) be an exact merit and \(\widehat M\) its computed value with \(|\widehat M-M|\le\Delta\). Then \(M\in[\max\{0,\widehat M-\Delta\},\widehat M+\Delta]\). If two computed merits with the same error bound differ by at most \(2\Delta\), their error intervals overlap, so their exact ordering is not certified by those bounds alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The local numerical floor is determined by a validated merit-evaluation error bound, not by unit roundoff alone.
assumptions_latex: A valid absolute error bound \(\Delta\ge0\) is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |\widehat M_1-\widehat M_2|\le2\Delta\Longrightarrow\text{the bounds alone do not certify their exact ordering}.
knowledge_statements.title: Error-Bound Detectability Floor

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Accuracy Claims Below the Validated Floor
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the status-reporting restriction induced by the error enclosure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If evaluation establishes only \(M\in[L,U]\) with \(U>\tau\), then \(M\le\tau\) is not certified even when the point estimate \(\widehat M\le\tau\). A tighter status requires a stronger enclosure, exact validation, or another justified correction establishing the requested predicate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A small point estimate cannot support an accuracy claim below the validated error enclosure.
assumptions_latex: The status requires the exact merit predicate \(M\le\tau\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: U>\tau\Longrightarrow[L,U]\text{ does not certify }M\le\tau.
knowledge_statements.title: Accuracy Claims Below the Validated Floor

assumptions_latex: Residual and gap evaluations are performed in finite precision.
A positive detectability threshold \(M_{\mathrm{floor}}\) is fixed for the chosen merit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Once \(M_k\le M_{\mathrm{floor}}\), further computed decrease cannot by itself support a more accurate status.

notation.meaning: computed termination merit at iteration k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-precision boundary below which merit improvement is not reliably distinguishable.

source_refs.locator: Beyond the Turing Machine Model p. 59
More on the Real-Number Model and Algebraic Complexity p. 60

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M_k\) be a computed residual-gap merit and let \(M_{\mathrm{floor}}>0\) be a bound, derived from the arithmetic error model or calibration, below which changes in \(M_k\) are not reliably distinguishable from evaluation error. The numerical-accuracy-floor regime is \[M_k\le M_{\mathrm{floor}}.\] In this regime, a smaller computed merit alone cannot justify a tighter accuracy claim. The floor depends on unit roundoff \(u\), conditioning, scaling, and residual evaluation; it is not a universal multiple of \(u\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Below an error-model-dependent merit floor, computed improvements are not reliably distinguishable from rounding and conditioning effects and cannot justify tighter accuracy claims.
knowledge_statements.title: Numerical Accuracy Floor

source_witnesses.locator: Beyond the Turing Machine Model p. 59
More on the Real-Number Model and Algebraic Complexity p. 60

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited complexity-model sections do not substantiate a finite-precision merit floor or the claimed reliability implication. A concrete rounding-error analysis or documented calibration method is needed.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Detection latency and overshoot for discretely polled resources.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a monotone counter is inspected only at polling points and \(U(p_{q-1})<B\le U(p_q)\), the first detected trigger is at \(p_q\), not necessarily when usage first reached \(B\). Consequently, \(U(p_q)-B\) may be positive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Discrete polling can detect a resource limit after it has been crossed, so positive overshoot is legitimate.
assumptions_latex: A resource is observed only at polling points \(p_0<p_1<\cdots\).
Its actual usage is monotone between polling points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: U(p_{q-1})<B\le U(p_q)\quad\text{permits}\quad U(p_q)-B>0.
knowledge_statements.title: Polling Overshoot Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Auditable payload for a detected resource-limit event.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At polling point \(p\), let \(J(p)\) contain every resource whose declared trigger comparison is satisfied. The termination payload records \(p\), each \(j\in J(p)\), its limit \(B_j\), observed usage \(U_j(p)\), and any independently verified mathematical status. Reporting only one member of a non-singleton \(J(p)\) loses diagnostic information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Report every resource triggered at the polling point, including its limit, observed usage, and separately verified status.
assumptions_latex: At polling point \(p\), finitely many counters \(U_j(p)\) and limits \(B_j\) are available.
A comparison predicate has been declared for each resource.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: J(p):=\{j:U_j(p)\text{ triggers }B_j\}\text{ is reported with }(B_j,U_j(p))_{j\in J(p)}.

notation.meaning: resource usage observed at polling point p

review_flags: Resource-specific comparisons are implementation policies and must be logged.
knowledge_statements.title: Resource-Exhaustion Diagnostic Payload

assumptions_latex: The iteration counter records completed iterations.
The check occurs immediately before each new iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_k\ge B_N\Longrightarrow\text{iteration }k+1\text{ is not started}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact semantics for an integer iteration counter checked before new work begins.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N_k=k\) count completed iterations and let \(B_N\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\). If the budget is checked immediately before starting an iteration, iteration \(k+1\) is not started when \(N_k\ge B_N\); hence at most \(B_N\) iterations complete and no polling overshoot occurs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pre-iteration integer-budget check prevents starting an iteration after the allowed number has completed.
knowledge_statements.title: Iteration-Budget Detection

assumptions_latex: \(U\) is monotone.
Polling points and the safe-interruption policy are declared before interpretation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: q=\min\{i:U(p_i)\ge B\}\Longrightarrow\text{no new interruptible work starts after }p_q.
review_flags: The polling schedule and indivisible-operation policy are implementation-defined and must be reported.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Wall-clock, memory, and evaluation counters observed at safe polling points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a monotone externally measured resource \(U(t)\) with budget \(B\), choose safe polling points \(p_0<p_1<\cdots\). Stop initiating new interruptible work at the first observed \(p_q\) satisfying \(U(p_q)\ge B\); any indivisible operation already in progress may finish according to the declared interruption policy. The payload records the observation point and overshoot.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sample external resources at declared safe points, stop new work at the first detected trigger, and report polling or operation overshoot.
knowledge_statements.title: Sampled External-Resource Detection

assumptions_latex: At least one finite budget \(B_j\) is declared before the run.
Usage counters \(U_j(k)\) are measured monotonically for iterations, time, memory, or other resources.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Termination occurs at the first \(k\) satisfying \(U_j(k)\ge B_j\) for some resource \(j\).

notation.meaning: usage of resource j through iteration k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Budget-exhaustion predicate separated from mathematical certificate statuses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For declared resource budgets \(B_j<\infty\) and monotone usage counters \(U_j(k)\), define \[k_*:=\inf\{k\ge0:\exists j,\ U_j(k)\ge B_j\}.\] If this set is nonempty, stop at \(k_*\), return the resource identifier and observed usage, and retain the best available iterate and diagnostics. A resource-limit termination does not imply optimality, infeasibility, or unboundedness; any such secondary status may be attached only when its independent verification predicate has passed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stop at the first declared budget exhaustion, report the exhausted resource, and do not infer a mathematical solution status without separate verification.
knowledge_statements.title: Resource-Limit Termination

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stopping index and reporting behavior are implementation-policy conventions. No source is supplied for the first-budget-hitting semantics or associated status behavior.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Provides an online scalar-merit variant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a scalar merit \(M_k\in\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) and a tie rule. After each iterate, replace the retained index \(k_*\) when \(M_k<M_{k_*}\), or when equality holds and the tie rule prefers \(k\). Assign \(+\infty\) to unavailable or invalid measurements. Once a finite candidate exists, the invariant is \(M_{k_*}=\min_{0\le j\le k}M_j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maintain the best scalar-merit iterate online, applying a declared tie rule and excluding invalid measurements.
assumptions_latex: The scalar merit and tie rule are fixed before iteration.
At least one generated iterate has finite valid merit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M_{k_*}=\min_{0\le j\le k}M_j.
knowledge_statements.title: Scalar-Merit Best-So-Far Retention

knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the storage and comparison overhead of scalar best-so-far retention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Excluding evaluation and storage of the declared diagnostics, scalar best-so-far retention needs one retained iterate record and one comparison per generated iterate. Thus its additional storage is \(O(1)\) iterate records and its additional update work is \(O(1)\) per iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scalar best-so-far retention adds constant retained-state storage and constant comparison work per iteration.
assumptions_latex: A scalar merit value and tie key are already available at each iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S_{\mathrm{extra}}=O(1),\qquad T_{\mathrm{update}}=O(1).
knowledge_statements.title: Online Retention Overhead

knowledge_statements.statement_title: The Last Iterate Need Not Be Best
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Demonstrates the need for retention when diagnostics are nonmonotone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimized merits \(M_0=1\), \(M_1=1/2\), and \(M_2=3/4\), termination at \(k=2\) leaves the last iterate worse than retained iterate \(k_*=1\). Last-iterate and best-iterate return coincide only under an additional monotonicity guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A diagnostic can worsen before termination, so the final iterate need not be the best generated iterate.
assumptions_latex: Smaller scalar merit is preferred.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M_1<M_2\Longrightarrow k_*=1\ne2.
knowledge_statements.title: The Last Iterate Need Not Be Best

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Best Iterate Relative to a Declared Preorder
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines bestness without imposing an implementation-specific diagnostic ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) be the generated iterate indices and \(\preceq\) a declared total preorder on their diagnostic records. An index \(k_*\in K\) is best when \(q_{k_*}\preceq q_k\) for every \(k\in K\). A deterministic interface must also declare a tie rule within the minimal equivalence class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A best iterate is meaningful only relative to a declared comparison rule and tie policy.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is finite and nonempty.
Every retained candidate has a comparable diagnostic record.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: k_*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{k\in K}^{\preceq}q_k.

notation.meaning: declared total preorder on diagnostic records

knowledge_statements.title: Best Iterate Relative to a Declared Preorder

assumptions_latex: \(K\) is the finite set of barrier iterates generated before termination.
Each iterate \(z^k=(x^k,y^k,s^k)\) has a computable lexicographic quality vector \(q_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z^{k_*}\), where \(k_*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{k\in K}q_k\), is retained for recovery.

notation.meaning: Barrier iterate containing primal, dual, and slack variables.
Lexicographic vector of infeasibility, complementarity, and objective diagnostics.
Index of the best generated iterate.

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports this termination-interface retention rule.
The ordering and tie-breaking convention require implementation-level source confirmation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic retention rule for a stagnating primal-dual barrier run.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every generated iterate \(z^k=(x^k,y^k,s^k)\), compute \(q_k=(\rho_p^k,\rho_d^k,\mu_k,|g_k|)\), where the entries are scaled primal infeasibility, scaled dual infeasibility, average complementarity, and relative duality gap. Order these vectors lexicographically, breaking ties by the larger iteration index, and set \[k_*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{k\in K}q_k.\] At any stagnation or resource-limit termination, return and retain \(z^{k_*}\), together with \(q_{k_*}\) and \(k_*\), rather than assuming that the final iterate is best.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Score every generated iterate by feasibility, complementarity, and gap; on abnormal termination, retain the lexicographically best iterate and its diagnostics.
knowledge_statements.title: Best-Iterate Retention

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithmic role fits Best-Iterate Retention, but the lexicographic diagnostic order, tie-breaking rule, and mandatory return behavior are implementation-specific and have no cited source. Their mathematical and operational authority cannot be established from the supplied evidence.

assumptions_latex: The linear program is \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\) with \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) of row rank \(m\).
A candidate primal-dual point \((x,y,s)\) and tolerances \(\tau_p,\tau_d,\tau_c,\tau_B>0\) are given.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A nonsingular candidate basis \(B\) satisfying the stated residual and sign tests is ready for basis identification.

notation.meaning: Complementary set of candidate nonbasic indices.
Primal, dual, complementarity, and basis tolerances.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Readiness predicate for extracting a standard-form basis from an interior iterate.

source_refs.locator: Moving to a Solution from an Interior Point p. 55

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Basis-identification readiness holds when there is an index set \(B\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) with \(|B|=m\) such that \(A_B\) is nonsingular, \(\sigma_{\min}(A_B)\ge\tau_B\), and, for \(N=\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus B\), \[\|Ax-b\|\le\tau_p,\qquad \|A^Ty+s-c\|\le\tau_d,\qquad \max_i x_i s_i\le\tau_c,\] while \(x_B\ge-\tau_p\) and \(s_N\ge-\tau_d\). The set \(B\) is then admissible for combinatorial basis recovery; readiness does not assert that the first admissible set is unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Basis identification is ready when residuals and complementarity are small and a well-conditioned, sign-consistent set of exactly m columns can be selected.
knowledge_statements.title: Basis-Identification Readiness

source_witnesses.locator: Moving to a Solution from an Interior Point p. 55

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits the readiness container, but the cited locator does not establish that this exact combination of residual, complementarity, sign, and absolute singular-value tests is a recognized readiness predicate. In particular, the scale-dependent bound on the smallest singular value and the tolerance coupling require direct source support.

assumptions_latex: The standard-form primal-dual pair has a finite optimum.
A barrier iterate \((x,y,s)\) and positive feasibility, complementarity, and conditioning tolerances are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iterate and a candidate basis form an admissible input to a finite crossover procedure.

notation.meaning: Candidate basic and nonbasic index sets.

review_flags: The precise neighborhood and conditioning tests vary among crossover implementations.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Handoff condition from an interior iterate to basis-producing crossover.

source_refs.locator: Moving to a Solution from an Interior Point p. 55

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Crossover readiness holds if \(x>0\), \(s>0\), the residual tests \(\|r_p\|\le\tau_p\) and \(\|r_d\|\le\tau_d\) hold, and \(\max_i x_i s_i\le\tau_c\). In addition, there must exist complementary index sets \(B,N\) with \(|B|=m\), \(A_B\) nonsingular, \(\sigma_{\min}(A_B)\ge\tau_B\), and magnitude or complementarity diagnostics sufficient to initialize nonbasic-fixing decisions. Under these tests, \((x,y,s,B,N)\) is an admissible crossover input; successful production of an optimal basis remains a separate algorithmic obligation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Crossover is ready when the interior point is accurate and centered enough, and a numerically stable candidate basis and nonbasic partition can be supplied.
knowledge_statements.title: Crossover Readiness

source_witnesses.locator: Moving to a Solution from an Interior Point p. 55

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind fits Crossover Readiness, but “magnitude or complementarity diagnostics sufficient to initialize” is not an explicit mathematical condition. The plain statement additionally says the point is centered enough, which is not expressed by a centrality-neighborhood test in the LaTeX statement. A source is needed to select and state the actual implementation-dependent crossover predicate.

assumptions_latex: The standard-form linear program is \(\min\{c^T x:Ax=b,\ x\ge 0\}\), where \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has row rank \(m\).
A recovered set \(B\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) has \(|B|=m\), the matrix \(A_B\) is nonsingular, and \(N=\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus B\).
The cleanup tolerances \(\tau_p,\tau_d>0\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recovered basis is ready for primal simplex cleanup when it is nearly primal feasible, and it is ready for dual simplex cleanup when it is nearly dual feasible, subject to accurate basis solves.

notation.meaning: Recovered basic and complementary nonbasic index sets.
Basic primal vector and associated nonbasic reduced costs.

review_flags: Cleanup acceptance thresholds and the choice of primal or dual simplex are implementation-dependent.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numerical handoff predicate for simplex correction after basis recovery.

source_refs.locator: Moving to a Solution from an Interior Point p. 55
5.2 The Simplex Method for Bounded Variables p. 220

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Set \(x_N^B=0\), \(x_B^B=A_B^{-1}b\), \(y^B=A_B^{-T}c_B\), and \(\bar c_N=c_N-A_N^Ty^B\). Simplex-cleanup readiness holds if the basis systems are numerically solvable and \[\|A_Bx_B^B-b\|\le\tau_p,\qquad \|A_B^Ty^B-c_B\|\le\tau_d.\] The condition \(\min_{i\in B}x_i^B\ge-\tau_p\) supports primal simplex cleanup, whereas \(\min_{i\in N}\bar c_i\ge-\tau_d\) supports dual simplex cleanup. If both sign tests fail substantially, the recovered basis is not cleanup-ready under these tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A recovered basis is cleanup-ready for primal simplex when its basis solves are accurate and it is nearly primal feasible, or for dual simplex when its basis solves are accurate and it is nearly dual feasible.
knowledge_statements.title: Simplex-Cleanup Readiness

assumptions_latex: The standard-form problem has \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) of row rank \(m\).
A recovered index set \(B\) has \(|B|=m\) and nonsingular \(A_B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^B\) is the basic solution represented by \(B\).

source_refs.locator: Moving to a Solution from an Interior Point p. 55

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(N=\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus B\), the primal basic-solution output associated with \(B\) is defined by \[x_N^B=0,\qquad x_B^B=A_B^{-1}b.\] It satisfies \(Ax^B=b\). It is a basic feasible solution exactly when \(x_B^B\ge0\); otherwise it is a basic but primal-infeasible recovery output. The output must include \(B\), because the same vector may admit more than one basis under degeneracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A recovered basis outputs the vector with nonbasic entries zero and basic entries obtained by solving the basis equations; nonnegativity makes it feasible.
knowledge_statements.title: Basic Solution Output

assumptions_latex: A basis \(B\) and associated basic primal-dual quantities have been computed.
Numerical status tolerances \(\tau_x,\tau_s>0\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The resulting per-variable labels constitute a tolerance-qualified basis-status output.

notation.meaning: Reduced-cost vector at the recovered basis.

review_flags: Status vocabularies differ for bounded-variable formulations.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(B\) and \(N=\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus B\), assign status \(\mathrm{basic}\) to every \(i\in B\) and status \(\mathrm{nonbasic\mbox{-}at\mbox{-}zero}\) to every \(i\in N\). Refine a basic label to \(\mathrm{degenerate\mbox{-}basic}\) when \(|x_i^B|\le\tau_x\), and flag a nonbasic dual ambiguity when \(|\bar c_i|\le\tau_s\). The output is the tuple of labels together with \(B\), \(N\), \(x^B\), \(y^B\), \(\bar c\), and the tolerances used; labels without their tolerances are not numerically reproducible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Basis-status output labels each variable basic or nonbasic at zero, flags degeneracy and dual ambiguity, and records the values and tolerances supporting those labels.
knowledge_statements.title: Basis-Status Output

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Tolerance Labels Are Not Exact Zero Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interpretive boundary for tolerance-qualified basis-status output.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(\tau>0\), a nonzero scalar can satisfy \(0<|z|\le\tau\). Thus labels based on \(|x_i^B|\le\tau_x\) or \(|\bar c_i|\le\tau_s\) express numerical indistinguishability from zero, not exact equality, unless exact arithmetic or certified error bounds establish that equality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A near-zero status at positive tolerance is not proof of exact degeneracy or an exactly zero reduced cost.
assumptions_latex: \(\tau>0\) is a numerical status tolerance.
No independent exact or certified zero test is supplied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|z|\le\tau\) does not imply \(z=0\).

notation.meaning: computed basic value or reduced cost

knowledge_statements.title: Tolerance Labels Are Not Exact Zero Certificates

assumptions_latex: The standard-form linear program is \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\), where \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has row rank \(m\).
An optimal basis \(B\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) has been recovered, \(|B|=m\), \(A_B\) is nonsingular, and \(N=\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus B\).
The basis status and the partition of perturbations \(\Delta c=(\Delta c_B,\Delta c_N)\) have been retained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recovered basis supports fixed-basis right-hand-side and objective-coefficient sensitivity analysis on the displayed feasibility regions.

notation.meaning: Basic primal solution and dual multiplier for the unperturbed problem.
Nonbasic reduced costs for the unperturbed problem.
Perturbations to the right-hand side and cost vector.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-basis sensitivity readiness for standard-form right-hand-side and cost perturbations.

source_refs.locator: Optimality Conditions, Duality, and Solution Sets p. 23

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Postoptimal-analysis readiness holds when \(x_B^B=A_B^{-1}b\ge0\) and \(\bar c_N=c_N-A_N^TA_B^{-T}c_B\ge0\). For a right-hand-side perturbation \(\Delta b\), the same basis remains primal feasible exactly when \[A_B^{-1}(b+\Delta b)\ge0.\] For a cost perturbation \(\Delta c\), it remains dual feasible exactly when \[(c_N+\Delta c_N)-A_N^TA_B^{-T}(c_B+\Delta c_B)\ge0.\] On the intersection of these regions, the same basis remains optimal and determines the perturbed basic solution, dual multiplier, reduced costs, and optimal objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An optimal nonsingular basis is ready for fixed-basis sensitivity analysis because explicit linear inequalities characterize the right-hand-side and cost perturbations for which it remains feasible and optimal.
knowledge_statements.title: Postoptimal-Analysis Readiness

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a positive primal vector \(x(\mu)\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\) and threshold \(\theta(\mu)>0\), define the small-variable index set by \[S_{\theta}(\mu)=\{i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}:x_i(\mu)<\theta(\mu)\}.\] Together with the sibling convention \(L_{\theta}(\mu)=\{i:x_i(\mu)\ge\theta(\mu)\}\), this assigns each index to exactly one magnitude class. In optimal-partition recovery, small indices are candidates for variables fixed at zero on the relevant optimal face. Without a separation result or complementary dual evidence, a small positive value does not certify an exact optimal zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A variable is classified as small when its barrier-iterate value is strictly below the threshold; exact activity still requires separation or complementary dual evidence.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose indices in the intended primal-positive class satisfy \(x_i(\mu)\ge\alpha\), while indices in the intended primal-zero class satisfy \(s_i(\mu)\ge1/\beta\). Since \(x_i(\mu)s_i(\mu)=\mu\), every primal-zero index then satisfies \(x_i(\mu)\le\beta\mu\). A threshold is separating whenever \[\beta\mu<\theta(\mu)<\alpha.\] Such a threshold classifies every intended primal-positive index as large and every intended primal-zero index as small. The interval must be nonempty, equivalently \(\beta\mu<\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose the threshold strictly between the upper scale of variables tending to zero and the lower scale of variables remaining positive; separation requires a nonempty gap.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal B=\{i:\exists x^*\text{ optimal with }x_i^*>0\}\) and \(\mathcal N=\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus\mathcal B\). If no known constants separate \(x_i(\mu)\) for \(i\in\mathcal B\) from those for \(i\in\mathcal N\), then a single finite-precision magnitude threshold need not recover this partition. In particular, degeneracy can make a legitimate basic variable arbitrarily small or zero at one optimal basic solution, while it remains in \(\mathcal B\). Such indices must be marked ambiguous and resolved through strict-complementarity information, dual slacks, or rank-preserving basis tests.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Zero Coordinates Can Belong to the Maximal Positive Partition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degenerate optimal-face example showing failure of classification from one selected optimum's magnitudes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{0:x_1+x_3=1,\ x_2+x_3=1,\ x\ge0\}\). Its optimal set is \(\{(1-t,1-t,t):0\le t\le1\}\), so \(\mathcal B=\{1,2,3\}\). At the optimal basic feasible solution \(\hat x=(0,0,1)\), the basis formed by columns 1 and 3 has the zero basic variable \(x_1\); analogously, columns 2 and 3 make \(x_2\) a zero basic variable. Thus coordinates belonging to \(\mathcal B\) can be zero at a selected degenerate optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A selected degenerate optimum can set coordinates to zero even though they are positive at other optima and belong to the maximal primal-positive partition.
assumptions_latex: \(A=\begin{bmatrix}1&0&1\\0&1&1\end{bmatrix}\), \(b=(1,1)^T\), and \(c=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\hat x_1=\hat x_2=0\) while \(1,2\in\mathcal B\), so the zero pattern of a selected degenerate optimum need not identify \(\mathcal B\).

Primal-Dual Partition Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency of the maximal optimal partition for a standard-form primal-dual pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the primal-dual pair \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\) and \(\max\{b^Ty:A^Ty+s=c,\ s\ge0\}\), with nonempty optimal sets. Define \(B=\{i:\exists x^*\text{ optimal with }x_i^*>0\}\) and \(N=\{i:\exists (y^*,s^*)\text{ optimal with }s_i^*>0\}\). Then \(B\cap N=\varnothing\). Moreover, strict complementarity yields an optimal triple \((\bar x,\bar y,\bar s)\) satisfying \(\bar x_i>0\) exactly for \(i\in B\) and \(\bar s_i>0\) exactly for \(i\in N\); consequently \(B\dot\cup N=\{1,\ldots,n\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The maximal primal-positive and dual-slack-positive index sets are disjoint, and a strictly complementary optimum realizes them as a complete partition.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\).
Both primal and dual attain finite optimal values.
The finite-dimensional strict-complementarity theorem applies.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B\cap N=\varnothing\) and \(B\dot\cup N=\{1,\ldots,n\}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Optimal-Face Identification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate representation of the primal optimal face using the maximal optimal partition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(z^*\) be the attained optimum of \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\), and let \((B,N)\) be its maximal optimal partition. The primal optimal face is
\[F_P^*=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b,\ x\ge0,\ c^Tx=z^*\}=\{x:Ax=b,\ x_B\ge0,\ x_N=0,\ c^Tx=z^*\}.\]
Its relative interior is
\[\operatorname{ri}F_P^*=\{x\in F_P^*:x_i>0\text{ for every }i\in B\}.\]
Thus an exact relative-interior optimal point identifies both the optimal face and every coordinate fixed to zero throughout that face.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The optimal face is obtained by fixing precisely the partition indices in N to zero; its relative-interior points are positive on every index in B.
assumptions_latex: The standard-form primal problem has a nonempty optimal set.
\((B,N)\) is the maximal optimal partition.

notation.meaning: relative interior of the primal optimal face

knowledge_statements.title: Partition Ambiguity Under Degeneracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of single-solution zero patterns to identify the maximal optimal partition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{0:x_1+x_2=1,\ x_1,x_2\ge0\}\), every feasible point is optimal and the maximal partition is \(B=\{1,2\}\), \(N=\varnothing\). Nevertheless, the optimal endpoint \((1,0)\) classifies index \(2\) as zero, while \((0,1)\) classifies index \(1\) as zero. Hence the support of an arbitrary optimal solution need not equal \(B\), and a degenerate optimal basic solution can have zero basic variables or admit multiple optimal bases. Partition recovery therefore requires a relative-interior or strictly complementary optimum, or equivalent global face information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Degenerate optimal solutions may have different zero patterns and bases, so one arbitrary optimum does not determine the maximal optimal partition.
assumptions_latex: Partition inference uses only the support of one optimal solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{supp}(x^*)\) need not equal \(B\).

knowledge_statements.title: Optimal-Partition-Based Identification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact basis recovery guided and checked by the maximal optimal partition, while allowing degenerate basic indices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and an exact maximal partition \((B,N)\), with \(\operatorname{rank}(A)=m\). Enumerate \(m\)-element sets \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) for which \(A_I\) is nonsingular, prioritizing sets containing independent columns from \(B\) but permitting indices from \(N\) as degenerate basic indices. For each set, define \(x_I=A_I^{-1}b\), \(x_{I^c}=0\), \(y=A_I^{-T}c_I\), and \(s=c-A^Ty\). Output the first \(I\) satisfying \(x_I\ge0\), \(s\ge0\), \(x_N=0\), and \(s_B=0\). The primal and dual feasibility tests together with \(c^Tx=b^Ty\) certify that the returned basis is optimal. If no set passes, report that the supplied partition or rank and sign decisions are inconsistent with the stated assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Search nonsingular candidate bases while prioritizing primal-positive partition columns but allowing zero-valued basic indices from N; return a basis only after primal, dual, and partition-consistency checks certify it.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\).
The standard-form primal and dual problems attain a common finite optimum.
\((B,N)\) is the exact maximal optimal partition.
\(A\) has full row rank \(m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A returned set \(I\) is an optimal primal basis consistent with \((B,N)\).

notation.meaning: basis matrix formed from columns indexed by I

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case candidate count for exhaustive partition-guided basis enumeration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An exhaustive implementation tests at most \(\binom{n}{m}\) distinct \(m\)-element index sets. Partition restrictions may reduce this count, but without additional structure the worst-case count remains \(\binom{n}{m}\), which is exponential when \(m=\Theta(n)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exhaustive partition-guided recovery is finite but may test a binomial number of candidate bases.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has row rank \(m\).
Candidates are distinct \(m\)-element column-index sets.

Basis-Tableau Identification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Candidate-basis identification using tableau primal-feasibility and reduced-cost tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the standard-form problem \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\), input \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and an \(m\)-element set \(I\subseteq\{1,,n\}\) with nonsingular \(A_I\). Form \(\bar b=A_I^{-1}b\), \(\bar A=A_I^{-1}A_{I^c}\), and \(\bar c_{I^c}=c_{I^c}-A_{I^c}^TA_I^{-T}c_I\). If \(\bar b\ge0\) and \(\bar c_{I^c}\ge0\), output \(I\), with \(x_I=\bar b\) and \(x_{I^c}=0\), as an optimal basis. Otherwise report that \(I\) is not certified by the tableau test; a separate Phase-I, simplex, dual-simplex, or criss-cross procedure with its own applicability conditions is required to construct another candidate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accept a candidate basis exactly when its tableau right-hand side and minimization reduced costs are nonnegative; otherwise report that this basis is not certified and leave basis repair to a separately specified method.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank \(m\).
The LP is in standard minimization form.
The inverse solves and sign tests use exact arithmetic or certified error bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The conditions \(\bar b\ge0\) and \(\bar c_{I^c}\ge0\) certify that \(I\) is an optimal basis.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complementarity-based candidate classification with independent certification of every returned basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a primal-dual feasible approximation \((x,y,s)\), tolerances \(\tau_x,\tau_s>0\), and full-row-rank \(A\), classify \(i\) as primal-active when \(x_i>\tau_x\) and \(s_i\le\tau_s\), and as dual-active when \(s_i>\tau_s\) and \(x_i\le\tau_x\); leave all conflicting coordinates undecided. Select a nonsingular \(m\)-column candidate using the primal-active indices and, when necessary, undecided indices. Return it only after certified basis solves establish \(A_I^{-1}b\ge0\) and \(c_{I^c}-A_{I^c}^TA_I^{-T}c_I\ge0\). Otherwise report inconclusive classification or reject the candidate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate complementarity proposes active indices, but only certified primal-feasibility and reduced-cost tests can accept the resulting basis.
assumptions_latex: \(Ax=b\), \(A^Ty+s=c\), and \(x,s\ge0\).
\(A\) has row rank \(m\).
Final nonsingularity, residual, and sign decisions are certified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every returned candidate is an optimal basis; failure to return one makes no claim that the LP lacks an optimal basis.
knowledge_statements.title: Certified Orthogonality-Guided Identification
Orthogonality-Based Identification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Candidate partition and basis selection from approximate complementarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a primal-dual feasible approximation \((x,y,s)\), tolerances \(\tau_x,\tau_s>0\), and full-row-rank \(A\). Classify \(i\) as primal-active when \(x_i>\tau_x\) and \(s_i\le\tau_s\), and as dual-active when \(s_i>\tau_s\) and \(x_i\le\tau_x\); leave conflicting indices undecided. From primal-active indices, select \(m\) linearly independent columns of \(A\). Compute the associated basic primal solution and reduced costs, and accept the basis only if both are nonnegative. Thus complementarity guides identification, while exact tableau tests certify the result; unresolved or failed tests require refinement rather than forced classification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate orthogonality proposes primal- and dual-active indices, but primal feasibility and reduced-cost tests must certify the selected basis.
assumptions_latex: \(Ax=b\), \(A^Ty+s=c\), and \(x,s\ge0\).
\(A\) has full row rank.
Threshold comparisons and final sign tests are numerically certified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An accepted candidate satisfies the exact optimal-basis conditions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The final tableau certification is sound, but the cited introductory primal-dual framework does not specifically support this threshold-based crossover identification algorithm. A direct locator is required before its classification rule can be relied upon.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numerically guarded selection of independent candidate columns followed by exact or certified LP basis tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Apply a rank-revealing column factorization, such as column-pivoted QR, to \(A_C\) and use its numerical-rank policy to propose \(m\) pivot columns \(I\). If fewer than \(m\) columns are judged independent, report insufficient numerical rank. Otherwise accept \(I\) only after certified tests establish that \(A_I\) is nonsingular, the basis residuals satisfy their bounds, \(A_I^{-1}b\ge0\), and the nonbasic reduced costs are nonnegative. A tolerance-based rank decision is provisional and must not be reported as exact rank without certification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rank-revealing factorization proposes independent columns; certified nonsingularity, residual, feasibility, and reduced-cost tests decide whether they form an optimal basis.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) has row rank \(m\).
\(C\) is a candidate column pool.
Numerical-rank and final certification tolerances are recorded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every returned set \(I\) is a certified optimal basis; an insufficient-rank report is tolerance-qualified unless exact rank was established.
knowledge_statements.title: Certified Rank-Revealing Basis Construction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact algebraic condition for a candidate pool to contain a column basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: There exists \(I\subseteq C\) with \(|I|=m\) and nonsingular \(A_I\) if and only if \(\operatorname{rank}(A_C)=m\). This condition alone implies neither \(A_I^{-1}b\ge0\) nor nonnegative reduced costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A candidate pool contains a basis exactly when its columns have full row rank, but rank alone does not certify feasibility or optimality.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has row rank \(m\).
\(C\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) is a candidate column pool.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C\) contains a basis exactly when \(\operatorname{rank}(A_C)=m\).
knowledge_statements.title: Candidate-Pool Basis Existence
Rank-Revealing Basis Construction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numerically guarded construction of a basis from candidate optimal columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), a candidate set \(C\), and rank tolerance \(\tau>0\). Compute a column-pivoted QR factorization \(A_C\Pi=QR\). Let \(r\) be the largest index for which \(|R_{rr}|>\tau|R_{11}|\). If \(r<m\), report insufficient numerical rank. Otherwise take the first \(m\) pivoted columns as \(I\), solve \(A_Ix_I=b\) and \(A_I^Ty=c_I\), and compute \(s=c-A^Ty\). Output \(I\) only when residual bounds, \(x_I\ge0\), and \(s\ge0\) are certified; otherwise enlarge or revise \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pivoted QR selects independent candidate columns, after which residual, primal-feasibility, and reduced-cost checks certify or reject the proposed basis.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) has full row rank \(m\).
\(C\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) is a candidate basis pool.
Linear solves and inequalities have specified numerical error bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A returned set \(I\) is nonsingular and satisfies certified optimal-basis tests.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Support Reduction and Terminal Extremality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-termination and terminal certificate for primal boundary pushes within an optimal face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^0\) be optimal and define \(D(x)=\{d:Ad=0,\ c^{\mathsf T}d=0,\ d_i=0\text{ whenever }x_i=0\}\). Then \(x\) is an extreme point of the primal optimal face if and only if \(D(x)=\{0\}\). If \(d\in D(x)\setminus\{0\}\), choose its sign with some \(d_i<0\) and set \(\alpha=\min_{d_i<0}x_i/(-d_i)\). The point \(x+\alpha d\) remains optimal and feasible and has strictly smaller support. Consequently repeated exact pushes terminate at an optimal extreme point after at most \(|\operatorname{supp}(x^0)|\) pushes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The absence of a support-preserving optimal-face direction exactly characterizes terminal extremality, and every maximal exact push removes at least one positive coordinate, giving finite termination.
assumptions_latex: \(x^0\in\{x:Ax=b,\ x\geq0,\ c^{\mathsf T}x=v^*\}\).
Directions and ratio-test steps are computed exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D(x^k)=\{0\}\text{ for some }k\leq |\operatorname{supp}(x^0)|,\text{ and }x^k\text{ is an optimal extreme point.}

notation.meaning: Two-sided feasible-direction space of the optimal face at the support of x.
Indices of positive coordinates of x.

review_flags: Complements rather than regenerates the immutable algorithm seed.
Exact-arithmetic result; tolerance-based pushes require separate numerical safeguards.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Support Reduction and Terminal Extremality
Primal-Push Crossover
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary-pushing recovery of an optimal primal extreme point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an optimal \(x\) of \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\). While the current point is not extreme in its optimal face, choose nonzero \(d\) satisfying \(Ad=0\), \(c^Td=0\), and \(d_i=0\) whenever \(x_i=0\). Select a sign having at least one negative component and set \(\alpha=\min_{d_i<0}x_i/(-d_i)\), then update \(x\leftarrow x+\alpha d\). Each update preserves feasibility and objective value and makes at least one positive coordinate zero. Stop when no such direction exists; the output is an extreme point of the primal optimal face and hence an optimal basic feasible solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Move along objective-neutral feasible directions to the nearest boundary until no face direction remains, producing an optimal basic feasible solution.
assumptions_latex: The primal optimal face is nonempty and contains the input point.
Directions are computed exactly or with feasibility-preserving certification.
Zero coordinates are fixed during each push.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The terminal \(x\) is an extreme point of the primal optimal face.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The boundary-push construction is mathematically plausible, but no inspectable source supports the algorithm, its finite termination, or the crossover interpretation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Dual Push to an Extreme Dual Optimum
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Support-monotone face walking in the dual optimal face under full row rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((y,s)\) be dual optimal for \(A^Ty+s=c\), \(s\ge0\), and suppose \(A\) has full row rank. Define \[\mathcal D_D(y,s)=\{(d_y,d_s):A^Td_y+d_s=0,\ b^Td_y=0,\ (d_s)_i=0\ \forall i\text{ with }s_i=0\}.\] If \(\mathcal D_D(y,s)=\{0\}\), stop. Otherwise choose a nonzero direction and its sign so that some currently positive slack decreases, set \[\alpha=\min_{(d_s)_i<0}\frac{s_i}{-(d_s)_i},\] and update \((y,s)\leftarrow(y,s)+\alpha(d_y,d_s)\). Dual feasibility and the objective value are preserved, each push creates at least one additional zero slack, and the process terminates after at most \(|\operatorname{supp}(s^0)|\le n\) pushes. The terminal pair is extreme in the dual optimal face.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximal objective-neutral dual-face steps successively eliminate positive slacks and reach an extreme dual optimum in finitely many pushes.
assumptions_latex: A dual optimum is available.
\(A\) has full row rank.
Directions and ratio tests are computed exactly or with certified signs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure terminates after at most \(|\operatorname{supp}(s^0)|\) pushes at a dual optimum satisfying \(\mathcal D_D(y,s)=\{0\}\), which certifies extremality in the dual optimal face.

notation.meaning: support-preserving direction space of the dual optimal face

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Dual Push to an Extreme Dual Optimum

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp rank-deficient obstruction to terminating a dual push at an extreme pair in (y,s)-space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume the primal equations \(Ax=b\) are feasible. If \(A\) lacks full row rank, choose \(0\ne h\in\ker(A^T)\). Then \(b^Th=0\), and for every dual feasible pair \((y,s)\), \((y+th,s)\) is dual feasible with the same objective value for every \(t\in\mathbb R\). Consequently every nonempty dual optimal face has lineality in \((y,s)\)-space and contains no extreme point; the direction \((h,0)\) also admits no finite slack-boundary step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank deficiency creates objective-neutral multiplier lineality with unchanged slacks, so a dual push cannot terminate at an extreme (y,s) pair.
assumptions_latex: The primal equation \(Ax=b\) is feasible.
\(\operatorname{rank}(A)<m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((h,0)\) is a nonzero lineality direction of every nonempty dual optimal face, so no extreme \((y,s)\) exists.

notation.meaning: nonzero vector in the null space of \(A^T\)

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Lineality Prevents Extreme-Point Crossover
Dual-Push Crossover
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary-pushing recovery of an extreme dual optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a dual optimum \((y,s)\) satisfying \(A^Ty+s=c\), \(s\ge0\). While it is not extreme in the dual optimal face, choose nonzero \((d_y,d_s)\) satisfying \(A^Td_y+d_s=0\), \(b^Td_y=0\), and \((d_s)_i=0\) whenever \(s_i=0\). Choose a sign with some \((d_s)_i<0\), set \(\alpha=\min_{(d_s)_i<0}s_i/(-(d_s)_i)\), and update \((y,s)\leftarrow(y,s)+\alpha(d_y,d_s)\). Each push preserves dual feasibility and objective value and creates a new zero slack. Stop when no admissible face direction remains.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Move within the dual optimal face until successive slacks reach zero and no feasible objective-neutral direction remains.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Coupled Push to an Extreme Optimal Pair
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Support-monotone face walking in the joint primal-dual optimal set under a rank condition excluding dual lineality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((x,y,s)\) be primal-dual feasible with \(c^Tx=b^Ty\), and suppose \(A\) has full row rank. At each iteration form the direction space \[\mathcal D(x,s)=\{(d_x,d_y,d_s):Ad_x=0,\ A^Td_y+d_s=0,\ c^Td_x=b^Td_y,\ (d_x)_i=0\ \forall i\text{ with }x_i=0,\ (d_s)_i=0\ \forall i\text{ with }s_i=0\}.\] If \(\mathcal D(x,s)=\{0\}\), stop. Otherwise choose a nonzero direction and its sign so that a currently positive component of \(x\) or \(s\) decreases, take the maximal \(\alpha>0\) satisfying \(x+\alpha d_x\ge0\) and \(s+\alpha d_s\ge0\), and update \((x,y,s)\). Every iterate remains primal-dual optimal, every push makes at least one additional primal variable or dual slack zero, and termination occurs after at most \(|\operatorname{supp}(x^0)|+|\operatorname{supp}(s^0)|\le n\) pushes. The terminal point is extreme in the joint primal-dual optimal set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated maximal support-preserving joint face steps reach an extreme primal-dual optimal pair in at most the initial number of positive complementary components.
assumptions_latex: The initial triple is primal-dual feasible with zero duality gap.
\(A\) has full row rank.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure terminates after at most \(|\operatorname{supp}(x^0)|+|\operatorname{supp}(s^0)|\le n\) pushes at a point satisfying \(\mathcal D(x,s)=\{0\}\), hence at an extreme joint optimal pair.

notation.meaning: support-preserving direction space of the joint primal-dual optimal face

knowledge_statements.title: Face-Restricted Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery by restricting the primal-dual pair to an identified optimal face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((B,N)\) be the exact maximal optimal partition. Optimal recovery may be restricted to
\[A_Bx_B=b,\qquad x_B\ge0,\qquad x_N=0,\]
and
\[A_B^Ty=c_B,\qquad A_N^Ty+s_N=c_N,\qquad s_N\ge0,\qquad s_B=0.\]
Every feasible pair for these restricted systems has zero duality gap and extends to an optimal primal-dual solution of the original problem. Conversely, every relative-interior optimal primal-dual solution satisfies these restrictions with \(x_B>0\) and \(s_N>0\). A basic optimum is recovered by selecting a nonsingular feasible basis from columns of \(A_B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixing N primal variables and B dual slacks to zero reduces recovery to the identified optimal faces without changing optimality.
assumptions_latex: The standard-form primal-dual pair has attained finite optimum.
\((B,N)\) is its exact maximal optimal partition.
\(A\) has full row rank when a basis is requested.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Restricted feasible pairs extend exactly to original primal-dual optima.

notation.meaning: column submatrices indexed by B and N

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degenerate boundary of basis extraction from an identified primal optimal face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The primal-positive block \(B=\{i:\exists x^*\text{ optimal with }x_i^*>0\}\) need not contain \(m\) linearly independent columns. For the standard-form LP
\[\min\{x_1:x_1=0,\ x_1\ge0\},\]
the unique optimum has \(B=\varnothing\), but \(\{1\}\) is a nonsingular degenerate optimal basis: \(A_{\{1\}}=[1]\), its basic value is zero, and its basic reduced cost is zero. Therefore face restriction identifies the optimal point or face but does not guarantee that an optimal basis can be selected entirely from primal-positive indices; zero-valued basic indices from the forced-zero block may be necessary.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basis recovery through vanishing fixed-matrix data perturbations followed by exact validation on the original LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\varepsilon_k\downarrow0\), solve
\[\min\{(c+\varepsilon_kq)^Tx:Ax=b+\varepsilon_kp,\ x\ge0\}\]
to a basic optimum with basis \(I_k\). On the original data compute
\[x_{I_k}=A_{I_k}^{-1}b,\qquad y=A_{I_k}^{-T}c_{I_k},\qquad s=c-A^Ty.\]
Return \(I_k\) exactly when \(x_{I_k}\ge0\) and \(s\ge0\); otherwise decrease the perturbation. Every basis that occurs for arbitrarily large \(k\) satisfies these original-data sign conditions. Since only finitely many bases exist, all sufficiently late \(I_k\) validate, so the procedure terminates finitely under the stated assumptions. This argument gives no polynomial bound on the number or cost of perturbed solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve successively smaller fixed-matrix perturbations and return a basis only after original-data primal and reduced-cost validation; if every perturbed problem has a basic optimum, sufficiently late bases pass that validation.

Controlled-Perturbation Crossover
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basis recovery through vanishing generic perturbations and exact validation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose fixed generic vectors \(p\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(q\in\mathbb R^n\), and a decreasing sequence \(\varepsilon_k\downarrow0\). For each \(k\), solve the perturbed problem \(\min\{(c+\varepsilon_k q)^Tx:Ax=b+\varepsilon_k p,\ x\ge0\}\) to a basic optimum with basis \(I_k\). Validate \(I_k\) on the original data by computing \(x_{I_k}=A_{I_k}^{-1}b\), \(y=A_{I_k}^{-T}c_{I_k}\), and \(s=c-A^Ty\). Stop and output \(I_k\) only if \(x_{I_k}\ge0\) and \(s\ge0\); otherwise reduce \(\varepsilon_k\). The validation makes every returned basis exactly optimal for the unperturbed problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve successively smaller generic perturbations, but return a basis only after exact primal and reduced-cost validation on the original LP.

knowledge_statements.title: Network-Structure Crossover
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tree-based crossover for a standard-form minimum-cost network-flow problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an interior estimate \(\widehat x\) for \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\geq0\}\), rank arcs using \(\widehat x\), reduced-cost estimates, and bound proximity. Construct a spanning tree \(T\) from preferred arcs, put each non-tree arc in \(N=E\setminus T\) at its selected bound, and solve \[x_T=A_T^{-1}(b-A_Nx_N).\] If primal feasibility or the reduced-cost signs fail, exchange a tree arc with a non-tree arc on its fundamental cycle. Stop at a primal-dual feasible tree basis, or pass the last basis to simplex cleanup.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank arcs from the interior solution, build a spanning-tree basis, solve its flows, and use cycle exchanges or simplex cleanup to restore feasibility and optimality.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is connected and \(A\) is its reduced node-arc incidence matrix.
\(Ax=b\) is consistent and the bounded network-flow LP has an optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A successful termination returns a spanning tree \(T\) whose columns form a feasible optimal basis; otherwise it returns a structured basis for cleanup.

Interior-point primal estimate used for ranking arcs.

knowledge_statements.title: Cycle-Space Basis Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fundamental-cycle representation induced by a chosen network spanning tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a spanning tree \(T\) and let \(N=E\setminus T\). For every \(e\in N\), define \(z^e\in\mathbb R^E\) by \(z^e_e=1\), \(z^e_f=0\) for \(f\in N\setminus\{e\}\), and \[z^e_T=-A_T^{-1}A_e.\] Then \(Az^e=0\), and the family \(\{z^e:e\in N\}\) is a basis of \(\ker A\). Consequently every feasible displacement has a unique expansion in these fundamental-cycle vectors, and exchanging \(e\) with a tree arc having nonzero coefficient in \(z^e_T\) preserves the basis cardinality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each non-tree arc creates one fundamental cycle, and these cycle vectors form a basis for all flow-conserving displacements.

\(T\) is a spanning tree.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ker A=\operatorname{span}\{z^e:e\in N\}\), with a unique coefficient for every non-tree arc.

notation.meaning: Fundamental-cycle vector generated by non-tree arc e.

children.title: Network Degeneracy Regimes
children.top_down_role: Ambiguity or instability arising from degenerate network bases.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes degeneration of a bounded-flow tree solution, an individual network pivot, and the dual tree state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a bounded minimum-cost flow basis consisting of a spanning tree \(T\) and bound statuses for \(E\setminus T\), the tree solution is primal degenerate when some basic tree flow satisfies \(x_e=\ell_e\) or \(x_e=u_e\). A particular fundamental-cycle pivot is degenerate only when its maximum feasible augmentation is zero. The tree state is dual degenerate when an eligible non-tree arc has zero signed reduced cost relative to its bound status. Primal degeneracy does not make every pivot degenerate, and a zero reduced cost produces an alternative optimal tree only when a feasible admissible exchange exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A basic arc at a bound, a zero-step pivot, and a zero signed reduced cost are distinct degeneracy notions; none alone guarantees every asserted alternative tree or zero-progress exchange.

Network Degeneracy Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal and dual degeneracy in tree-basis recovery and crossover.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a recovered tree basis \(T\), primal degeneracy occurs when some basic flow lies at a bound, in standard form when \(x_{T,i}=0\). Dual degeneracy occurs when some non-tree arc has zero reduced cost \(r_e=c_e-A_e^{\mathsf T}y=0\), where \(A_T^{\mathsf T}y=c_T\). In either regime, several spanning trees may represent the same primal or dual solution, a cycle exchange may have zero step length or zero objective change, and thresholding an interior estimate cannot uniquely identify a tree without a deterministic tie rule or perturbation.

knowledge_statements.title: Block-Structured Basis Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basis recovery by local elimination and a linking Schur complement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the equality matrix consists of local block rows coupled by linking rows. Select nonsingular local column sets \(B_i\), eliminate their local basic variables, and select additional linking columns so that the resulting Schur complement \(S\) is square and nonsingular. Assign all remaining variables to candidate bounds, solve the reduced linking system \(Sz=q\), and back-substitute independently through each \(B_i\). Accept the assembled basis only if its primal variables satisfy their bounds; otherwise exchange offending local or linking columns and repeat, or return the candidate to simplex cleanup.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Simplex Cleanup
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cleanup from a primal-feasible crossover basis for a minimization LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Start from a primal-feasible basis \(B\) for \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\geq0\}\). Compute \(B^{\mathsf T}y=c_B\) and \(r_N=c_N-A_N^{\mathsf T}y\). If \(r_N\geq0\), stop. Otherwise choose \(j\in N\) with \(r_j<0\), set \(d=B^{-1}A_j\), and choose a leaving index attaining \[\min_{i:d_i>0}\frac{x_{B,i}}{d_i}.\] Pivot and repeat. If no component of \(d\) is positive, report an improving unbounded ray. The method outputs an optimal basis once both primal feasibility and nonnegative reduced costs hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: From a primal-feasible crossover basis, pivot on negative reduced costs until dual feasibility proves optimality or an unbounded ray appears.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) has full row rank.
The initial basis \(B\) is nonsingular and \(x_B=B^{-1}b\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Termination with \(r_N\geq0\) certifies optimality; failure of the ratio-test denominator certifies primal unboundedness.

notation.meaning: Basic-variable direction generated by the entering column.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Simplex Cleanup
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cleanup from a dual-feasible crossover basis for a minimization LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Start from a basis \(B\) with reduced costs \(r_N=c_N-A_N^{\mathsf T}y\geq0\), where \(B^{\mathsf T}y=c_B\), but possibly \(x_B=B^{-1}b\not\geq0\). Choose a row \(i\) with \(x_{B,i}<0\), write \(\bar a_{ij}=(B^{-1}A_j)_i\), and select an entering index attaining \[\min_{j:\bar a_{ij}<0}\frac{r_j}{-\bar a_{ij}}.\] Pivot and repeat. If no \(j\) has \(\bar a_{ij}<0\), report primal infeasibility. When \(x_B\geq0\), the retained dual feasibility certifies optimality.

Define \(\gamma=\min\{\min_{i\in B}x_i^*,\min_{j\in N}s_j^*\}\). If an approximation obeys \[\|\widehat x-x^*\|_\infty<\gamma/2,\qquad \|\widehat s-s^*\|_\infty<\gamma/2,\] then thresholding at \(\gamma/2\) identifies \(B\) from \(\widehat x\) and \(N\) from \(\widehat s\).

Polynomial Basis-Identification Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional polynomial recovery for rational, separated linear programs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a rational standard-form LP of encoding length \(L\) with a unique strictly complementary nondegenerate optimal basis and separation \(\gamma\geq2^{-p(m,n,L)}\) for some polynomial \(p\). Solving the identified basis equations in exact rational arithmetic then returns an exactly checkable optimal basic solution in polynomial bit complexity.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact basis rounding from an approximately identified primal-dual partition.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Precision boundary for reliable basis identification and exact recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\gamma\) be the smallest positive optimal basic variable or nonbasic dual slack. knowledge_statements.title: Incorrect Active-Set Prediction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure criterion for crossover from an interior primal-dual iterate to a basic optimal solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the standard-form linear program 
\[\min\{c^\top x:Ax=b,\ x\ge 0\},\]
where \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has rank \(m\), and let \((x^*,y^*,s^*)\) be an optimal primal-dual solution. A predicted nonbasic set \(N\) is incorrect for this solution if either \(x_j^*>0\) for some \(j\in N\), or its complement \(B=\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus N\) has cardinality different from \(m\), or \(A_B\) is singular. In these cases, fixing \(x_N=0\) cannot recover \(x^*\) as the unique basic solution \(x_B=A_B^{-1}b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A predicted active set fails when it removes a positive optimal variable or leaves a complement that cannot define a nonsingular basis reproducing the chosen optimum.

\((x^*,y^*,s^*)\) is primal-dual optimal.

knowledge_statements.title: Singular Candidate Basis
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic failure of a crossover basis candidate in standard-form linear programming.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) with \(\operatorname{rank}(A)=m\), let \(B\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) contain \(m\) indices. The candidate basis is singular precisely when
\[\det(A_B)=0,\quad\text{equivalently}\quad \operatorname{rank}(A_B)<m.\]
Then \(A_Bx_B=b\) either has no solution or has more than one solution. Consequently, the assignment \(x_N=0\), where \(N=B^c\), does not determine a unique basic solution and cannot complete basis recovery without replacing at least one index of \(B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A candidate basis is singular when its selected columns are dependent; the associated basis equations then cannot determine a unique basic solution.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has row rank \(m\).
\(B\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and \(|B|=m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}(A_B)<m\) implies that \(x_N=0\) does not yield a unique basic solution.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The square candidate matrix \(A_B\) is singular if and only if there exists \(z\in\mathbb R^m\setminus\{0\}\) satisfying \(A_Bz=0\). Any such vector is an exact certificate of singularity and explicitly records a nontrivial dependence among the selected columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonzero null vector of the selected square column matrix exactly certifies that the candidate basis is singular.

For the perturbation bound, \(b\ne0\), \(\delta_A=\|\Delta A_B\|/\|A_B\|\), \(\delta_b=\|\Delta b\|/\|b\|\), and \(\kappa(A_B)\delta_A<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\kappa(A_B)>\tau\) marks threshold instability; in the spectral norm, \(\kappa_2(A_B)=\sigma_{\max}(A_B)/\sigma_{\min}(A_B)\) and \(1/\kappa_2(A_B)\) is the relative distance to singularity.

notation.meaning: normwise condition number of the selected basis matrix

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-precision sensitivity of solves using a fixed nonsingular recovered basis matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\kappa(A_B)=\|A_B\|\,\|A_B^{-1}\|\). Call the basis numerically unstable at threshold \(\tau\) when \(\kappa(A_B)>\tau\). If \((A_B+\Delta A_B)(x_B+\Delta x_B)=b+\Delta b\) and \(\kappa(A_B)\delta_A<1\), then the standard normwise bound is
\[\frac{\|\Delta x_B\|}{\|x_B\|}\le \frac{\kappa(A_B)}{1-\kappa(A_B)\delta_A}(\delta_A+\delta_b).\]
For the spectral norm,
\[\kappa_2(A_B)=\frac{\sigma_{\max}(A_B)}{\sigma_{\min}(A_B)},\qquad \frac{1}{\kappa_2(A_B)}=\frac{\inf\{\|E\|_2:A_B+E\text{ is singular}\}}{\|A_B\|_2}.\]
Thus singular-value estimates or certified bounds on their ratio diagnose this failure. The family \(A_B(\eta)=\operatorname{diag}(1,\eta)\), \(b=(1,1)^T\), has \(\kappa_2(A_B(\eta))=1/\eta\) and \(x_B=(1,1/\eta)^T\), so nonsingular bases can become arbitrarily sensitive as \(\eta\downarrow0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonsingular basis is numerically unstable at a chosen threshold when its condition number is too large; the condition number controls normwise error amplification and, in the spectral norm, measures relative proximity to singularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conditioning Boundary for a Nonsingular Basis
knowledge_statements.title: Conditioning Boundary for a Nonsingular Basis
Numerically Unstable Basis
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Condition-number criterion for rejecting a formally nonsingular recovered basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B\) be a candidate basis with nonsingular \(A_B\), and fix a subordinate matrix norm and a permitted amplification threshold \(\tau\ge1\). The basis is numerically unstable at threshold \(\tau\) when
\[\kappa(A_B)=\|A_B\|\,\|A_B^{-1}\|>\tau.\]
Indeed, for perturbations satisfying \((A_B+\Delta A_B)(x_B+\Delta x_B)=b+\Delta b\), first-order relative errors in \(x_B\) may be amplified by a factor proportional to \(\kappa(A_B)\). Thus nonsingularity alone does not make the recovered basic solution reliable in finite precision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonsingular candidate basis is declared unstable when its condition number exceeds the prescribed amplification threshold, making recovered basic variables sensitive to numerical error.
assumptions_latex: \(A_B\) is square and nonsingular.
\(\|\cdot\|\) is a fixed subordinate matrix norm and \(\tau\ge1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\kappa(A_B)>\tau\) classifies \(B\) as numerically unstable at threshold \(\tau\).

knowledge_statements.title: Degeneracy-Induced Ambiguity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonuniqueness of basis labels at a degenerate basic feasible solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\) with \(\operatorname{rank}(A)=m\), let \(x\) be a basic feasible solution represented by a basis \(B\). If \(x\) is degenerate, meaning
\[|\{j:x_j>0\}|<m,\]
then the positive support does not supply all \(m\) basis indices. Additional zero-valued columns must be selected to complete a basis. Whenever two distinct such completions \(B_1\ne B_2\) are nonsingular, both represent the same point \(x\); hence primal values alone do not identify a unique recovered basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a degenerate vertex, positive variables do not fill a basis, so different nonsingular selections of zero-valued variables may label the same solution.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has rank \(m\).
\(x\) is a degenerate basic feasible solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If distinct nonsingular completions exist, the same \(x\) has more than one basis representation.

If two distinct bases \(B_1\ne B_2\) represent the same \(x\), then \(x\) is degenerate. Equivalently, every nondegenerate basic feasible solution has a unique representing column basis.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiple Optimal Bases
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Criterion for multiple basis representations attaining the same optimal objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(\min\{c^\top x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\), with \(A\) of row rank \(m\). There are multiple optimal bases if distinct sets \(B_1,B_2\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\), each of cardinality \(m\), satisfy
\[A_{B_k}\text{ nonsingular},\qquad x^{(k)}_{B_k}=A_{B_k}^{-1}b\ge0,\qquad x^{(k)}_{B_k^c}=0,\qquad c^\top x^{(k)}=v^*,\]
for \(k\in\{1,2\}\). The represented optimal solutions may be distinct, or they may coincide when the common solution is degenerate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two distinct nonsingular column sets are optimal bases when their basic feasible solutions both attain the optimal value; degeneracy may make those solutions identical.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent certificate for multiple optimal bases that does not require prior knowledge of the optimal value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\min\{c^\top x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\), let \(B_1\ne B_2\) be nonsingular column bases. For \(k=1,2\), define
\[x^{(k)}_{B_k}=A_{B_k}^{-1}b,\quad x^{(k)}_{B_k^c}=0,\quad y^{(k)}=A_{B_k}^{-\top}c_{B_k},\quad \bar c^{(k)}_{B_k^c}=c_{B_k^c}-A_{B_k^c}^{\top}y^{(k)}.\]
If \(x^{(k)}_{B_k}\ge0\) and \(\bar c^{(k)}_{B_k^c}\ge0\) for both \(k\), then both bases are optimal. Conversely, every optimal basis satisfies these two sign conditions. Thus two distinct bases satisfying them certify multiple optimal bases without separately knowing \(v^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two distinct nonsingular bases certify multiple optimal bases exactly when each has a nonnegative basic solution and nonnegative nonbasic reduced costs.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal B^*\) is finite, nonempty, and every member has already passed the required basis and optimality checks.
\(g(B)\) is evaluated consistently on all candidates, and \(\prec\) is a strict total order.

deterministic strict total order used for equal scores

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic structural preference among already certified admissible optimal crossover bases.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a finite nonempty certified family \(\mathcal B^*\), assign each basis a declared secondary score \(g(B)\), such as an estimated conditioning, factor-storage, or predicted-cleanup score, and select
\[B^{\mathrm{out}}=\min_{\prec}\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\mathcal B^*}g(B),\]
where \(\prec\) is a fixed strict total order resolving equal scores. This preserves admissibility because scoring is applied only after certification; the score itself supplies no feasibility or optimality certificate and need not predict realized cleanup cost exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A crossover implementation may prefer the certified candidate with the best declared structural score and use a fixed total order for equal scores; scoring does not replace candidate certification.
knowledge_statements.title: Score-Based Basis Tie-Breaking
Basis Tie-Breaking Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic selection among several admissible optimal crossover bases.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input a finite nonempty family \(\mathcal B^*\) of admissible optimal bases and a strict total order \(\prec\) on index sets. Initialize \(\widehat B\) to any member of \(\mathcal B^*\). For each \(B\in\mathcal B^*\), replace \(\widehat B\) by \(B\) whenever \(B\prec\widehat B\). Stop after all candidates have been examined and output
\[B^{\mathrm{out}}=\min_{\prec}\mathcal B^*.\]
For example, \(\prec\) may be lexicographic order on sorted index tuples. Strict totality makes the output unique and repeatable, although it does not alter the optimality of the represented basic feasible solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Order all admissible optimal bases by a fixed strict total order and return the least one; this resolves ambiguity deterministically without changing optimality.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal B^*\) is finite and nonempty.
\(\prec\) is a strict total order on candidate bases.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B^{\mathrm{out}}\) is the unique \(\prec\)-minimal admissible optimal basis.
