\(S\) is a fixed nonsingular data-scaling operator and \(\|\cdot\|\) is a fixed norm.
\(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal R(d)\) is \(\varepsilon\)-stable exactly when \(\rho_{\mathcal R,S}(d)>\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: deterministic basis-recovery map, including tie handling
fixed scaling operator on perturbations of the LP data
scaled distance to a change in recovered-basis identity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rule-relative robustness of recovered-basis identity under explicitly scaled admissible data perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For LP data \(d\in\mathcal D\), define
\[\rho_{\mathcal R,S}(d)=\inf\{\|S^{-1}\Delta d\|:d+\Delta d\in\mathcal D,\ \mathcal R(d+\Delta d)\ne\mathcal R(d)\},\]
with the infimum of the empty set equal to \(+\infty\). The recovered basis is \(\varepsilon\)-unstable when \(\rho_{\mathcal R,S}(d)\le\varepsilon\), and \(\varepsilon\)-stable when \(\rho_{\mathcal R,S}(d)>\varepsilon\). Equivalently, stability means that the fixed recovery map is constant on the admissible open scaled ball of radius \(\varepsilon\) about \(d\). This classification concerns basis identity and is not a condition-number statement about the selected basis matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a fixed deterministic recovery rule and fixed data scaling, the stability radius is the smallest admissible scaled perturbation that changes the returned basis.
knowledge_statements.title: Scaled Recovery-Map Stability Radius
Unstable Basis Classification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perturbation-based classification of ambiguity near a basis boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(d=(A,b,c)\) be linear-program data, let \(\mathcal R(d)\) be a deterministic basis-recovery map, and fix a data norm. A recovered basis \(B=
\mathcal R(d)\) is \(\varepsilon\)-unstable if
\[\inf\{\|\Delta d\|:\mathcal R(d+\Delta d)\ne B\}\le\varepsilon.\]
It is \(\varepsilon\)-stable if the infimum is greater than \(\varepsilon\). This classification concerns the identity of the recovered basis, not necessarily the optimal value or solution point: near degeneracy, arbitrarily small perturbations can change the selected basis while leaving those quantities nearly unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A recovered basis is unstable at scale epsilon when a data perturbation of at most that size can make the fixed recovery rule select another basis.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal R\) is a deterministic basis-recovery map.
A norm and perturbation radius \(\varepsilon\ge0\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed distance to a change of basis classifies \(B\) as \(\varepsilon\)-unstable or \(\varepsilon\)-stable.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed distance-to-classification-change condition is plausible, but its exact perturbation model and interpretation depend on the recovery map, norm, admissible perturbed data, and scaling. A supporting source is required.

children.title: Cleanup Implications of Ambiguity
children.top_down_role: Simplex-cleanup consequences of uncertain or nonunique basis recovery.

assumptions_latex: \(B_1\ne B_2\) are admissible recovered bases for the same LP optimum or optimal face.
Cleanup computations use basis-indexed solves, factorizations, reduced costs, or pivot choices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: B_1\ne B_2\text{ may yield different cleanup diagnostics, paths, and work even when both accepted outputs satisfy the same LP quality requirements.}
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numerical and computational consequences of sending different admissible bases into cleanup.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Distinct admissible bases \(B_1\ne B_2\) may represent the same degenerate optimum or different points on one optimal face, while their matrices \(A_{B_1}\) and \(A_{B_2}\), factorization behavior, reduced-cost data, and eligible pivots differ. Consequently, cleanup diagnostics, pivot paths, and work need not be invariant under the chosen basis. This numerical noninvariance does not relax the requirement that every accepted cleanup output pass the declared feasibility and objective-quality checks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Different admissible recovered bases can lead to different factorizations, pivot paths, and cleanup costs even though every accepted result must satisfy the same solution-quality requirements.
knowledge_statements.title: Basis-Dependent Cleanup Behavior
Cleanup Implications of Ambiguity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity requirement for post-crossover cleanup under nonunique optimal bases.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal B^*\) be the set of candidate bases produced at an ambiguous optimal solution. A cleanup procedure is basis-safe if, for every \(B\in\mathcal B^*\), its accepted output \(\widehat x(B)\) satisfies
\[A\widehat x(B)=b,\qquad \widehat x(B)\ge0,\qquad c^\top\widehat x(B)\le v^*+\eta,\]
for a prescribed objective tolerance \(\eta\ge0\). Therefore cleanup may use a tie-breaking policy to choose one basis, but it must validate feasibility and objective quality after that choice; equality of basis labels across admissible executions is not a valid requirement under degeneracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When several optimal bases are admissible, cleanup should certify feasibility and objective quality for the selected basis instead of requiring a unique basis label.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal B^*\) is a nonempty family of candidate optimal bases.
\(v^*\) and an objective tolerance \(\eta\ge0\) are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Basis-safe cleanup validates the displayed residual, bound, and objective conditions for every accepted output.

notation.meaning: cleanup output obtained from candidate basis B

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle is reasonable, but the universal basis-safety requirement and exact feasibility checks are uncited implementation policy; only the objective condition includes a tolerance.

children.title: Crossover Progress Stalling
children.top_down_role: Regimes where crossover ceases to produce useful basis progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Crossover Progress Stalling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational stopping condition for a crossover sequence that ceases to improve its merit measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(z^0,z^1,\ldots\) be crossover states and let \(M(z)\ge0\) be a merit measure, such as a maximum of primal infeasibility, dual infeasibility, and complementarity residuals. Given a window \(w\in\mathbb N\), decrease tolerance \(\delta>0\), and acceptance tolerance \(\epsilon\ge0\), crossover stalls at iteration \(k\ge w\) when
\[M(z^{k-w})-M(z^k)<\delta\quad\text{and}\quad M(z^k)>\epsilon.\]
Thus insufficient progress over the prescribed window is distinguished from successful termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Crossover stalls when its merit measure improves by less than the required amount over a fixed window while remaining above the acceptance tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(M(z^k)\ge0\) is evaluated consistently at every iteration.
\(w\ge1\), \(\delta>0\), and \(\epsilon\ge0\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two displayed inequalities declare iteration \(k\) stalled rather than converged.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The windowed merit-decrease rule is a coherent operational condition, but the cited simplex degeneracy and stalling section does not establish this specific crossover residual criterion or its parameters.

children.title: Basis Assembly Bottlenecks
children.top_down_role: Computational concentration in candidate-basis construction or validation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense arithmetic and factor-storage cost when candidate bases are independently factorized.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(q\) dense \(m\times m\) candidate bases are independently factorized and candidate \(i\) is used for \(r_i\) triangular solves, classical dense arithmetic requires \(\Theta(qm^3+m^2\sum_{i=1}^q r_i)\) operations. Sequential processing requires \(\Theta(m^2)\) peak factor storage, excluding storage for the original LP data.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without factor reuse, each dense candidate costs cubic factorization work and each solve costs quadratic work.
assumptions_latex: Each candidate basis is dense and \(m\times m\).
Candidates are factorized independently using classical dense arithmetic.
Candidates are processed sequentially for the stated peak factor storage.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Work is \(\Theta(qm^3+m^2\sum_i r_i)\), with \(\Theta(m^2)\) peak factor storage.
knowledge_statements.title: Dense Independent-Factorization Cost

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Candidate-count bottleneck before rank, factorization, solve, or cleanup costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A pool of \(k\) candidate columns contains \(\binom{k}{m}\) unordered \(m\)-column assemblies. Exhaustive assembly without pruning may therefore require that many rank or factorization attempts. For \(k=2m\), \(\binom{2m}{m}=\Theta(4^m/\sqrt m)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A candidate pool can contain exponentially many possible basis assemblies.
assumptions_latex: Distinct unordered \(m\)-element subsets are considered.
No structural pruning rule is assumed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The candidate count is \(\binom{k}{m}\), exponential for \(k=2m\).
knowledge_statements.title: Combinatorial Basis-Assembly Growth
Basis Assembly Bottlenecks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense-arithmetic lower accounting for testing and factorizing crossover basis candidates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose crossover tests \(q\) candidate bases \(B_1,\ldots,B_q\), each represented by a dense \(m\times m\) matrix, by fresh factorization and triangular solution. In the classical dense-arithmetic model, one factorization costs \(\Theta(m^3)\) operations and stores \(\Theta(m^2)\) scalars, while each subsequent right-hand-side solve costs \(\Theta(m^2)\). Consequently, with \(r_i\) solves for candidate \(i\), basis assembly and validation require
\[\Theta\!\left(qm^3+m^2\sum_{i=1}^q r_i\right)\]
operations if no factors are reused, with \(\Theta(m^2)\) peak factor storage per sequential candidate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without factor reuse, testing q dense candidate bases costs cubic work per factorization plus quadratic work per solve, and needs quadratic factor storage.
assumptions_latex: Every candidate basis matrix is dense and \(m\times m\).
Each candidate is factorized independently using classical dense arithmetic.
Candidates are processed sequentially for the stated peak storage.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The work and storage bounds are respectively \(\Theta(qm^3+m^2\sum_i r_i)\) and \(\Theta(m^2)\).

notation.meaning: number of triangular solves using candidate i
number of equality constraints and basis dimension

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The dense, independent-factorization accounting is mathematically standard and the complexity_bound kind fits, but the record supplies no source for the stated operation and storage bounds.

children.title: Degeneracy-Driven Slowdown
children.top_down_role: Crossover delays caused by repeated ambiguous or dependent basis choices.

knowledge_statements.title: Degeneracy-Driven Slowdown
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Slowdown mechanism caused by degenerate pivots during simplex-style crossover.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
In a primal simplex-style crossover, let \(x_B=A_B^{-1}b\ge0\), let entering direction satisfy \(d_B=A_B^{-1}A_j\), and choose
\[\theta=\min\{x_{B_i}/(d_B)_i:(d_B)_i>0\}.\]
If a minimizing row has \(x_{B_i}=0\), then \(\theta=0\). The pivot changes the basis but leaves the primal point and objective value unchanged. A sequence containing many such degenerate pivots can therefore increase crossover work without commensurate primal or objective progress; without an anti-cycling rule, repeated bases may even occur.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A degenerate zero-length pivot changes the basis without moving the solution or objective, so many such pivots slow crossover and may permit cycling.
assumptions_latex: \(A_B\) is nonsingular and \(x_B=A_B^{-1}b\ge0\).
The entering column admits at least one positive ratio denominator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A zero basic variable attaining the ratio minimum yields \(\theta=0\) and no primal or objective progress.

notation.meaning: basic component of the simplex entering direction

children.title: Cleanup-Dominated Runtime
children.top_down_role: Cases where post-crossover simplex work dominates total recovery cost.

assumptions_latex: \(T=C+U>0\) with \(C,U\ge 0\).
Acceleration replaces \(U\) by \(U/s\), with \(s\ge 1\), without changing cleanup work or cleanup cost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S_s=\frac{1}{f+(1-f)/s}\le \frac{1}{f}\quad\text{for }f>0,\qquad \lim_{s\to\infty}S_s=\frac{1}{f}.

notation.meaning: acceleration factor applied to noncleanup work

knowledge_statements.scope_note: End-to-end runtime consequence when cleanup is the unaccelerated portion of crossover recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T=C+U>0\) and \(f=C/T\). If only noncleanup work is accelerated by a factor \(s\ge1\), then \(T_s=C+U/s\) and
\[S_s=\frac{T}{T_s}=\frac{1}{f+(1-f)/s}.\]
Thus, for \(f>0\), acceleration confined to noncleanup phases cannot produce speedup exceeding \(1/f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If cleanup is unchanged, its original runtime fraction imposes an Amdahl-type ceiling on acceleration of all other crossover phases.
knowledge_statements.title: Cleanup Speedup Ceiling
Cleanup-Dominated Runtime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Runtime regime in which post-recovery correction exceeds all preceding crossover work.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Decompose the crossover runtime as
\[T_{\mathrm{total}}=T_{\mathrm{predict}}+T_{\mathrm{assemble}}+T_{\mathrm{pivot}}+T_{\mathrm{cleanup}},\]
where every term is nonnegative. For a dominance factor \(\rho\ge1\), the run is cleanup-dominated when
\[T_{\mathrm{cleanup}}\ge \rho\bigl(T_{\mathrm{predict}}+T_{\mathrm{assemble}}+T_{\mathrm{pivot}}\bigr).\]
Equivalently, cleanup consumes at least the fraction \(\rho/(1+\rho)\) of total crossover time. The definition requires mutually exclusive timing categories and includes feasibility restoration, residual correction, or basis repair only in the cleanup term.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cleanup dominates runtime when its measured time is at least rho times the combined prediction, basis-assembly, and pivot time.
assumptions_latex: The four timing categories are exhaustive and mutually exclusive.
All measured times are nonnegative and \(\rho\ge1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The dominance inequality is equivalent to \(T_{\mathrm{cleanup}}/T_{\mathrm{total}}\ge\rho/(1+\rho)\).

notation.meaning: time spent on post-recovery correction and repair

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algebraic equivalence is correct and the condition kind fits, but the runtime decomposition, dominance threshold, and category boundaries are uncited implementation-dependent definitions.

children.title: Memory Bottlenecks
children.top_down_role: Storage pressure arising during crossover or basis factorization.

assumptions_latex: Every charged allocation, including numerical values, sparse indices, metadata, temporary workspace, and allocator overhead, is included in \(s(q)\).
The execution schedule, representation, and object lifetimes are fixed.
\(M\) is usable capacity in the same units, and the allocation model has no uncharged fragmentation or separate capacity constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S_{\mathrm{peak}}\le M\text{ is necessary and sufficient for capacity feasibility under the fixed in-memory execution model.}

notation.meaning: objects simultaneously live at time t

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact capacity boundary for a fixed crossover execution schedule and storage representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each instant \(t\) of a fixed crossover execution, let \(\mathcal L(t)\) be its simultaneously live stored objects and let \(s(q)\) be the total charged storage of object \(q\). Define
\[S_{\mathrm{peak}}=\max_t\sum_{q\in\mathcal L(t)}s(q).\]
Under the stated allocation model, the execution fits usable memory \(M\) exactly when \(S_{\mathrm{peak}}\le M\). If this inequality fails, completion requires a different representation or live-object schedule, external storage, or additional usable memory.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed crossover execution fits in memory exactly when its peak simultaneous charged storage does not exceed usable capacity; objects that are never live together must not be summed.
knowledge_statements.title: Peak-Live-Storage Boundary
Memory Bottlenecks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Storage failure during crossover from an interior solution to a basic solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an LP with constraint matrix \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), a crossover implementation that materializes every candidate basis matrix, its factorization, and dense primal-dual work arrays can require \(\Omega(mn+m^2)\) words. Consequently, when the available memory is \(M<mn+m^2\), this implementation may fail even though sparse storage of \(A\) requires only \(O(\operatorname{nnz}(A))\) words. Streaming candidate columns or maintaining one sparse basis factorization avoids this particular dense-storage requirement but does not guarantee bounded fill-in.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dense candidate-basis arrays can exhaust memory despite a sparse original matrix; sparse or streamed assembly reduces storage but may still suffer factorization fill-in.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\).
The implementation explicitly stores dense candidate or factorization arrays.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M<mn+m^2\) can prevent crossover completion independently of mathematical solvability.

notation.meaning: available memory measured in machine words
number of stored nonzeros of the constraint matrix

review_flags: implementation-specific storage model needs an authoritative crossover reference

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role and dense-versus-sparse distinction fit the node, but the claimed lower bound depends on an underspecified implementation and storage model. In particular, “every candidate basis matrix” does not identify how many matrices coexist, and the threshold M<mn+m^2 suppresses constants implicit in the asymptotic bound. An authoritative crossover implementation or complexity source is required.

children.title: Barrier Postsolve Validation Interface
children.top_down_role: Reconstruction and validation of barrier, certificate, and basis outputs in the original unscaled model.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Presolve and postsolve; Accessing the solution

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Implementation of Interior Point Methods for Large Scale Linear Programming
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Implementation of Interior Point Methods for Large Scale Linear Programming

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the acceptance predicate for a reconstructed bounded-form primal vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Ax=b\), \(l\le x\le u\), a reconstructed vector \(\widehat x\) is exactly primal feasible if and only if \(A\widehat x=b\) and every finite original bound is satisfied. A tolerance-based interface must instead evaluate its declared equation residual and maximum bound violation in original, unscaled coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accept a reconstructed primal vector only after checking every original equation and finite original bound.
assumptions_latex: All checks use original, unscaled model coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A\widehat x=b\ \land\ l\le\widehat x\le u\Longleftrightarrow\widehat x\in X.
knowledge_statements.title: Original-Coordinate Primal Acceptance Test

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Incomplete Recovery Data Do Not Define a Primal Postsolve Map
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates reconstruction failure from ordinary primal infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If an eliminated variable has neither a stored value nor a defining relation evaluable from already reconstructed variables, the recovery log does not define a total map from reduced vectors to original vectors. An arbitrary completion must not be reported as the reconstructed solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A missing defining record for an eliminated variable makes primal postsolve underdetermined even when the reduced point is feasible.
assumptions_latex: The eliminated coordinate is required in the original-model output.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R\text{ not total on }Z\Longrightarrow\text{primal reconstruction failure}.

notation.meaning: partial reconstruction map induced by the log

knowledge_statements.title: Incomplete Recovery Data Do Not Define a Primal Postsolve Map

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Feasibility Preservation by an Exact Reconstruction Map
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the guarantee supplied by an exact affine postsolve map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z\) and \(X\) be the reduced and original feasible sets. If the recorded affine map \(R(z)=Pz+q\) satisfies \(R(Z)\subseteq X\), then every \(\widehat z\in Z\) reconstructs a feasible original point \(R(\widehat z)\). If \(R(Z)=X\), the map represents all original feasible points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact recovery map preserves feasibility when its image of the reduced feasible set lies in the original feasible set.
assumptions_latex: The reconstruction data \(P,q\) are exact.
\(Z\) and \(X\) use consistent reduced and original conventions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat z\in Z\Longrightarrow P\widehat z+q\in X.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility Preservation by an Exact Reconstruction Map

assumptions_latex: Every elementary recovery record is affine.
The maps have compatible input and output dimensions and are ordered so that the displayed composition is defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R_1\circ\cdots\circ R_t(z)=P_1\cdots P_tz+\sum_{i=1}^t(P_1\cdots P_{i-1})q_i.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural representation generated by a compatible dependency-ordered sequence of affine recovery records.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If successive recovery records are affine maps \(R_i(v)=P_iv+q_i\) with compatible dimensions, then their dependency-ordered composition \(R_1\circ\cdots\circ R_t\) is affine. In particular, \(R(z)=Pz+q\), where \(P=P_1\cdots P_t\) and \(q=q_1+P_1q_2+\cdots+P_1\cdots P_{t-1}q_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compatible sequence of affine variable-recovery records composes into one affine original-variable map.
knowledge_statements.title: Composition of Affine Recovery Records

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Criterion for formula-by-formula evaluation of stored single-valued recovery records.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Construct a directed graph on eliminated coordinates, with an edge \(i\to j\) when the stored formula for \(x_j\) requires \(x_i\). Assume every formula is single-valued and otherwise uses only reduced coordinates and its recorded predecessors. A formula-by-formula topological replay order exists if and only if this graph is acyclic. For an acyclic graph, every topological ordering evaluates each coordinate once and produces the same reconstructed vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complete single-valued formulas can be replayed sequentially exactly when their dependency graph has a topological ordering.
assumptions_latex: Each eliminated coordinate has one single-valued recovery formula.
Every dependency is explicitly recorded.
The interface uses formula-by-formula replay rather than an undeclared joint solve.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{A topological formula-replay order exists}\iff\text{the dependency graph is acyclic}.

notation.meaning: coordinate i is required to evaluate coordinate j

review_flags: The criterion concerns sequential replay, not general solvability of a cyclic joint system.
knowledge_statements.title: Acyclic Recovery-Dependency Criterion

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cyclic Recovery Log Without a Joint Solve
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational failure boundary for formula-by-formula replay.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If stored recovery formulas contain a directed cycle and the log supplies neither resolved equivalent formulas nor a declared nonsingular joint system for the cyclic coordinates, formula-by-formula replay is undefined. An arbitrary evaluation order cannot serve as a reconstruction rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unresolved dependency cycle prevents deterministic sequential replay.
assumptions_latex: The recovery interface evaluates stored formulas and supplies no joint system for the cyclic coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{unresolved dependency cycle}\Longrightarrow\text{formula-replay failure}.
knowledge_statements.title: Cyclic Recovery Log Without a Joint Solve

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact replay rules for fixed coordinates, affine scaling or shifting, and stored affine substitutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A primal recovery log may use the following single-valued records: (i) a fixed coordinate restores \(x_j=f\); (ii) if \(z_j=(x_j-d)/a\) with \(a\ne0\), restore \(x_j=az_j+d\); (iii) if an eliminated coordinate has the stored relation \(x_j=d+p^{\mathsf T}v\), restore it after every coordinate in \(v\) is available. Replaying \(L\) complete records in dependency-compatible order evaluates the induced affine map \(x=Pz+q\) in \(O(L+M)\) arithmetic operations, where \(M\) is the total number of referenced coefficients in the stored formulas.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed values, inverse affine coordinate changes, and stored affine substitutions are replayed in dependency order to reconstruct original variables in time linear in the recovery-log representation.
assumptions_latex: Every eliminated coordinate has one complete, single-valued recovery record.
All referenced predecessor coordinates have already been reconstructed.
Every inverse scaling coefficient is nonzero.
Scalar arithmetic and stored-coefficient access have unit cost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat x=R(\widehat z)=P\widehat z+q\text{ is uniquely evaluated in }O(L+M)\text{ operations before original-coordinate feasibility validation}.

notation.meaning: recorded predecessor coordinates used by a substitution
number of recovery records and total referenced coefficients

review_flags: Assumes exact stored transformations and does not assert that every solver presolve uses only these forms.
knowledge_statements.title: Elementary Primal Recovery Records
Primal-Solution Reconstruction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reverses a logged affine presolve map to recover original primal variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the original variables and reduced variables satisfy the logged affine relation \(x=Pz+q\), where fixed, substituted, scaled, and aggregated variables are represented in \(P\) and \(q\). Given a reduced solution \(\widehat z\), compute \(\widehat x=P\widehat z+q\) by applying the logged transformations in reverse order. Restore exact fixed values and evaluate eliminated variables from their recorded defining equations. Output \(\widehat x\) only after checking the original bounds and equations; otherwise report reconstruction failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply recorded presolve transformations backward, restore eliminated variables, and accept the reconstructed primal vector only after original-model feasibility checks.
assumptions_latex: \(x=Pz+q\) exactly represents the logged primal presolve transformations.
Every eliminated variable has a recorded inverse or defining equation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm returns \(\widehat x=P\widehat z+q\) or reports reconstruction failure.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits primal-solution reconstruction and is mathematically plausible, but no source is supplied for the claimed affine representation of all listed presolve operations or for their reverse-order reconstruction and failure protocol.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Redundant Rows Make Reconstructed Multipliers Nonunique
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies the nonuniqueness boundary for original equality multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the equality system \(x=0\), \(2x=0\) with objective \(c=0\) and no finite variable bounds, stationarity is \(y_1+2y_2=0\). Hence every \((y_1,y_2)=(-2t,t)\), \(t\in\mathbb R\), is stationary. Restoring a removed redundant row therefore need not produce a unique original multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Redundant original rows can admit infinitely many valid lifted dual multipliers.
assumptions_latex: Equality multipliers are unrestricted in sign.
The original constraint matrix contains redundant rows.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{y:y_1+2y_2=0\}\text{ is not a singleton.}

notation.meaning: multipliers of the two original equality rows

knowledge_statements.title: Redundant Rows Make Reconstructed Multipliers Nonunique

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes whether fixed reconstructed bound multipliers admit an original equality multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ l\le x\le u\}\) with proposed \(s^L,s^U\ge0\), a multiplier \(y\) satisfying \(c-A^{\mathsf T}y-s^L+s^U=0\) exists if and only if \(c-s^L+s^U\in\operatorname{range}(A^{\mathsf T})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recovered bound multipliers admit an equality multiplier exactly when the remaining stationarity vector lies in the transpose range.
assumptions_latex: The stationarity convention is \(c-A^{\mathsf T}y-s^L+s^U=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists y:\ A^{\mathsf T}y=c-s^L+s^U\iff c-s^L+s^U\in\operatorname{range}(A^{\mathsf T}).
knowledge_statements.title: Existence of Original Equality Multipliers

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Gauge Freedom of Restored Row Multipliers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Describes all equality multipliers compatible with a fixed stationarity vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(y_0\) satisfies \(A^{\mathsf T}y_0=c-s^L+s^U\), then every solution is in \(y_0+\ker(A^{\mathsf T})\). Thus the restored equality multiplier is unique exactly when \(A\) has full row rank; nonuniqueness alone does not invalidate stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Redundant rows create null-space freedom in reconstructed equality multipliers without invalidating stationarity.
assumptions_latex: At least one stationary multiplier \(y_0\) exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{y:A^{\mathsf T}y=c-s^L+s^U\}=y_0+\ker(A^{\mathsf T}).
knowledge_statements.title: Gauge Freedom of Restored Row Multipliers

assumptions_latex: \(D\) is nonsingular.
The scaled equality is exactly \(DAx=Db\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: y=D^{\mathsf T}\bar y,\quad A^{\mathsf T}y=A^{\mathsf T}D^{\mathsf T}\bar y,\quad b^{\mathsf T}y=(Db)^{\mathsf T}\bar y.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact adjoint reconstruction rule for equality-row scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the original equality be \(Ax=b\), and replace it by \(DAx=Db\) for a nonsingular diagonal \(D\). If \(\bar y\) is the multiplier in the scaled stationarity term \(A^{\mathsf T}D^{\mathsf T}\bar y\), then the corresponding original equality multiplier is \(y=D^{\mathsf T}\bar y\). This transport preserves both \(A^{\mathsf T}y\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Undo equality-row scaling by multiplying the scaled multiplier by the transpose of the row-scaling matrix.
knowledge_statements.title: Equality-Multiplier Transport Through Row Scaling

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical representative when redundant original rows make stationary equality multipliers nonunique.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r=c-s^L+s^U\in\operatorname{range}(A^{\mathsf T})\). Among all \(y\) satisfying \(A^{\mathsf T}y=r\), the unique minimum-Euclidean-norm representative is \(y_\star=(A^{\mathsf T})^\dagger r\). Every other solution is \(y_\star+v\), where \(v\in\ker(A^{\mathsf T})\), and \(y_\star\perp\ker(A^{\mathsf T})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The pseudoinverse selects a unique minimum-norm multiplier from the affine family caused by redundant rows.
assumptions_latex: \(r=c-s^L+s^U\in\operatorname{range}(A^{\mathsf T})\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: y_\star=(A^{\mathsf T})^\dagger r=\operatorname*{argmin}_{A^{\mathsf T}y=r}\|y\|_2.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bound-Multiplier Restoration for a Fixed Variable
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact dual postsolve rule when a variable fixed at equal finite bounds was removed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(x_j=f\) with \(l_j=u_j=f\) was eliminated and an equality multiplier \(y\) has already been reconstructed. Let \(r_j=c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}y\). Setting \(s_j^L=\max\{r_j,0\}\) and \(s_j^U=\max\{-r_j,0\}\) gives \(r_j-s_j^L+s_j^U=0\) with nonnegative bound multipliers. More generally, every nonnegative pair with \(s_j^L-s_j^U=r_j\) is valid; hence the pair is generally nonunique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a removed fixed variable, split its residual stationarity coefficient into nonnegative lower- and upper-bound multipliers.
assumptions_latex: The stationarity convention is \(c-A^{\mathsf T}y-s^L+s^U=0\).
The eliminated variable has equal finite bounds \(l_j=u_j=f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: s_j^L,s_j^U\ge0,\qquad c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}y-s_j^L+s_j^U=0.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual Transport Through Positive Diagonal Variable Rescaling and Translation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact multiplier transport for a coordinatewise affine transformation of bounded variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x=Dz+p\), where \(D=\operatorname{Diag}(d)\) with \(d_j>0\). Transform the objective, equality, and bounds to \((D^{\mathsf T}c)^{\mathsf T}z\), \((AD)z=b-Ap\), and \(D^{-1}(l-p)\le z\le D^{-1}(u-p)\). If \((y,\bar s^L,\bar s^U)\) satisfies transformed stationarity, then \(s^L=D^{-\mathsf T}\bar s^L\) and \(s^U=D^{-\mathsf T}\bar s^U\) are nonnegative and satisfy \(c-A^{\mathsf T}y-s^L+s^U=0\). Conversely, \(\bar s^L=D^{\mathsf T}s^L\) and \(\bar s^U=D^{\mathsf T}s^U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Retain equality multipliers and undo positive variable scaling on lower- and upper-bound multipliers.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is diagonal with strictly positive entries.
Objective, equations, and bounds are transformed exactly through \(x=Dz+p\).
The stationarity convention is \(c-A^{\mathsf T}y-s^L+s^U=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: s^L=D^{-\mathsf T}\bar s^L,\quad s^U=D^{-\mathsf T}\bar s^U,\quad c-A^{\mathsf T}y-s^L+s^U=0.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restores bound multipliers coordinatewise after fixing an original primal point and equality multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a reconstructed primal point \(x\) and equality multiplier \(y\), let \(r_j=c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}y\). Require \(r_j-s_j^L+s_j^U=0\), \(s_j^L,s_j^U\ge0\), \(s_j^L(x_j-l_j)=0\), and \(s_j^U(u_j-x_j)=0\), omitting multipliers for infinite bounds. If \(x_j\) is strictly between its available bounds, restoration exists exactly when \(r_j=0\), yielding \(s_j^L=s_j^U=0\). At only a lower bound it exists exactly when \(r_j\ge0\), yielding \((s_j^L,s_j^U)=(r_j,0)\); at only an upper bound it exists exactly when \(r_j\le0\), yielding \((0,-r_j)\). If \(l_j=u_j=x_j\), every nonnegative pair satisfying \(s_j^L-s_j^U=r_j\) is valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The primal activity pattern and equality multiplier determine complementary bound multipliers, except for the expected freedom at fixed variables.
assumptions_latex: The original problem is \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ l\le x\le u\}\).
The primal point \(x\) and equality multiplier \(y\) are fixed.
Stationarity is \(c-A^{\mathsf T}y-s^L+s^U=0\).

Given reduced multipliers, apply each recorded presolve transformation in reverse using its adjoint multiplier-lifting rule; restore multipliers for eliminated rows and bounds. Output \((\widehat y,\widehat s^L,\widehat s^U)\) only if original-model stationarity and sign conditions hold; otherwise report reconstruction failure.

Every presolve operation records a valid adjoint multiplier-lifting rule.

knowledge_statements.title: Solver-Status Reconstruction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Assigns an original-model status only from reconstructed and validated objects.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The reduced-model status is not transferred by name alone. Declare the original model optimal only when reconstructed primal and dual vectors satisfy primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and zero duality gap. Declare it infeasible only when a reconstructed Farkas vector satisfies the original equations and strict separating inequality. Declare it unbounded only when a reconstructed feasible point and improving recession direction satisfy the original constraints. If the corresponding predicate fails, return an indeterminate reconstruction status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An original solver status is accepted only when its reconstructed solution or certificate passes the defining original-model predicate.
assumptions_latex: The original LP data and the complete presolve transformation log are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each reported status is supported by a valid original-model witness; otherwise the status is indeterminate.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Reduced-Space Infeasibility Alone Is Not an Original Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the logical boundary requiring an equivalence-preserving reduction and valid certificate transport.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A certificate for a reduced system proves infeasibility of the original system only when the reduction is equivalence-preserving and the certificate is transported by a valid adjoint map. Without those premises, reduced infeasibility has no original-model force.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reduced infeasibility certificate proves nothing about the original model unless the reduction and certificate lift are valid.
assumptions_latex: The claimed conclusion concerns the original rather than merely the reduced model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{reduced certificate}+\neg\text{valid lift}\centernot\Longrightarrow\text{original infeasibility}.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) be nonsingular and replace \(Ax=b\) by \(TAx=Tb\). If \(\bar y\) is an equality multiplier for the transformed system, then \(y=T^{\mathsf T}\bar y\) preserves \(A^{\mathsf T}y\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}y\) relative to the transformed expressions. Consequently, every Farkas identity and strict margin involving these quantities is preserved.

A tuple \((y,\alpha,\beta)\), with \(y\) free, \(\alpha_j\ge0\) for \(j\in L\), and \(\beta_j\ge0\) for \(j\in U\), is an original-model infeasibility certificate when omitted components are zero and \[A^{\mathsf T}y-\alpha+\beta=0,\qquad l_L^{\mathsf T}\alpha_L-u_U^{\mathsf T}\beta_U-b^{\mathsf T}y>0.\] These conditions imply \(X=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite-bound sign conditions, exact stationarity, and a strict positive original-data margin form a bounded-form Farkas certificate.
assumptions_latex: The original feasibility system is \(Ax=b\), \(l\le x\le u\).
Multipliers for infinite bounds are absent or zero.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normalization invariance of an original-space certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \((y,\alpha,\beta)\) satisfies the bounded-form Farkas predicate with margin \(\delta=l_L^{\mathsf T}\alpha_L-u_U^{\mathsf T}\beta_U-b^{\mathsf T}y>0\), then \((y,\alpha,\beta)/\delta\) satisfies the same sign and stationarity conditions and has unit margin. Multiplication by any positive scalar preserves validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strict reconstructed Farkas witness can be normalized to unit margin by positive scaling.
assumptions_latex: \(\delta=l_L^{\mathsf T}\alpha_L-u_U^{\mathsf T}\beta_U-b^{\mathsf T}y>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \delta^{-1}(y,\alpha,\beta)\text{ is a unit-margin certificate}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact certificate lift when a variable fixed at equal finite bounds is removed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(x_j=f\), with \(l_j=u_j=f\), is removed, so the reduced equality right-hand side is \(b-a_jf\). Let a reduced Farkas witness have equality multiplier \(y\) and valid multipliers for all remaining bounds. Set \(q=a_j^{\mathsf T}y\), \(\alpha_j=\max\{q,0\}\), and \(\beta_j=\max\{-q,0\}\). Then \(q-\alpha_j+\beta_j=0\), and the original strict margin equals the reduced margin because \(f\alpha_j-f\beta_j-b^{\mathsf T}y=-(b-a_jf)^{\mathsf T}y\), apart from unchanged remaining-bound terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restore a removed fixed coordinate's Farkas multipliers by splitting its equality coefficient into nonnegative lower- and upper-bound parts; the strict margin is preserved.
assumptions_latex: The eliminated coordinate has equal finite bounds \(l_j=u_j=f\).
The reduced witness satisfies its reduced stationarity and strict-margin conditions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A^{\mathsf T}y-\alpha+\beta=0\text{ and }\delta_{\mathrm{original}}=\delta_{\mathrm{reduced}}>0.

Then \(A^{\mathsf T}y-\alpha+\beta=0\), signs and finite-bound supports are preserved, and \[l^{\mathsf T}\alpha-u^{\mathsf T}\beta-b^{\mathsf T}y=\bar l^{\mathsf T}\bar\alpha-\bar u^{\mathsf T}\bar\beta-(b-Ap)^{\mathsf T}y.\] Hence the strict certificate margin is unchanged.

knowledge_statements.title: Unboundedness-Certificate Reconstruction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Original-space improving recession ray with a feasible base point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ l\le x\le u\}\), reconstruct a base point \(x^0\) and nonzero direction \(d\). The pair certifies unboundedness when \(Ax^0=b\), \(l\le x^0\le u\), \(Ad=0\), and \(c^{\mathsf T}d<0\). Additionally, \(d_i\ge0\) whenever \(l_i\) is finite and \(d_i\le0\) whenever \(u_i\) is finite. Then \(x^0+td\) is feasible for every \(t\ge0\) and its objective tends to \(-\infty\).

assumptions_latex: The original problem is a minimization LP with equality constraints and componentwise bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^0+td\) remains feasible for all \(t\ge0\), and \(c^{\mathsf T}(x^0+td)\to-\infty\).

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Validation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validates termination witnesses directly against original, unscaled LP data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a reported status and reconstructed witness, select its original-model predicate. For optimality, check primal feasibility, dual feasibility, stationarity, complementarity, and objective agreement. For infeasibility, check multiplier signs, the homogeneous adjoint equation, and the strict Farkas inequality. For unboundedness, check a feasible base point, a bound-compatible null-space direction, and strict objective improvement. Accept the status only if every applicable check passes under declared tolerances; otherwise return certificate invalid.

Sensitivity-Analysis Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-basis local sensitivity information recovered from a postsolved optimal basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the LP \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge 0\}\) and an optimal basis \(\mathcal B\), with \(B=A_{:\mathcal B}\) nonsingular and nonbasic matrix \(N=A_{:\mathcal N}\). For perturbations \((\Delta b,\Delta c)\), the fixed-basis sensitivity interface returns
\[
x_{\mathcal B}(\Delta b)=B^{-1}(b+\Delta b),\quad x_{\mathcal N}=0,\quad y(\Delta c)=B^{-\mathsf T}(c_{\mathcal B}+\Delta c_{\mathcal B}),
\]
\[
r_{\mathcal N}(\Delta c)=c_{\mathcal N}+\Delta c_{\mathcal N}-N^{\mathsf T}y(\Delta c).
\]
The reported basis remains optimal exactly throughout the region \(x_{\mathcal B}(\Delta b)\ge0\) and \(r_{\mathcal N}(\Delta c)\ge0\). At zero perturbation, the interface reports the local value sensitivities \(D_bv=y\) and \(D_cv=x\) whenever the optimal value function is differentiable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The interface reports fixed-basis primal values, dual prices, reduced costs, admissible perturbations preserving optimality, and local derivatives of the optimal value when they exist.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\).
\(B=A_{:\mathcal B}\) is nonsingular and defines a primal-dual optimal basic solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{(\Delta b,\Delta c):B^{-1}(b+\Delta b)\ge0,\ c_{\mathcal N}+\Delta c_{\mathcal N}-N^{\mathsf T}B^{-\mathsf T}(c_{\mathcal B}+\Delta c_{\mathcal B})\ge0\}\) is the fixed-basis optimality region.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basis-independent value sensitivity for a finite attained standard-form LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v(b,c)=\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\). At data for which the primal and dual optima are finite and attained, the optimal dual-solution set equals the subdifferential of the convex function \(v(\cdot,c)\): \[\partial_b v(b,c)=Y^*(b,c).\] Likewise, the optimal primal-solution set equals the superdifferential of the concave function \(v(b,\cdot)\): \[\partial_c^+v(b,c)=X^*(b,c).\] Hence differentiability with respect to \(b\) or \(c\) requires the corresponding sensitivity set to be a singleton; otherwise the interface must report a set or directional range rather than a unique gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimal dual solutions are right-hand-side subgradients, and optimal primal solutions are cost supergradients. Multiple optima make sensitivity set-valued, so a unique gradient must not be asserted.

The standard-form minimization sign convention is used.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility requirements for transferring a previous postsolved artifact to a perturbed LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the old LP has dimensions \((n,m)\) and the perturbed LP has dimensions \((\widetilde n,\widetilde m)\). Reuse of a previous primal-dual artifact requires explicit mappings for retained rows and variables, initialization rules for new components, and reversal or reconciliation of the old and new presolve and scaling transformations. Every mapped component must be finite and must satisfy the receiving algorithm's bound, sign, and indexing requirements. Equal dimensions permit direct indexing only when row and variable identities are unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A prior solution can initialize a perturbed LP only after explicit row, variable, presolve, and scaling mappings are applied and the mapped components are validated. Equal dimensions alone are insufficient.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Performance limitation of transferring an old solution without stability hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An iterate that is central or optimal for the old LP need not be feasible, interior, or well centered for the perturbed LP. Without quantitative perturbation, admissibility, and neighborhood assumptions, transferring the old artifact guarantees neither fewer iterations nor less linear-algebra work than constructing a fresh initialization. A transferred artifact that violates the receiving interface must be repaired or rejected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An old optimal solution can be infeasible or poorly centered for the perturbed LP, so transfer alone gives no general iteration or work reduction and may require repair or rejection.
assumptions_latex: No quantitative stability or central-neighborhood hypothesis relates the old and perturbed LPs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Warm-start transfer alone implies no general reduction in iteration count or linear-algebra work.}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Warm-started infeasible primal-dual barrier workflow for a compatible perturbed LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Map the previous postsolved primal-dual artifact into the perturbed model's current presolved and scaled coordinates. Reject unmappable components and initialize new components by declared rules. Repair mapped primal variables and dual slacks to strict positivity, for example by a positive floor \(\delta\), while allowing nonzero primal and dual residuals. Starting from this repaired state, apply the selected infeasible-start primal-dual barrier method to \((\widetilde A,\widetilde b,\widetilde c)\): form its perturbed Newton equations, use fraction-to-boundary or stricter steps to retain \(x>0\) and \(s>0\), and stop only when the declared primal-residual, dual-residual, sign-violation, and duality-gap tests pass. Reverse the current scaling and presolve transformations and validate the reconstructed candidate against the perturbed original model before release. Mapping failure, Newton-solve failure, a validation failure, or an iteration limit produces a non-success status rather than a certified solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Map and validate the old artifact, repair it to a strictly positive infeasible-start state, solve the perturbed primal-dual barrier equations with positivity-preserving steps, and release a result only after stopping tests and original-coordinate postsolve validation pass.

Reoptimization Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Warm-started infeasible primal-dual barrier reoptimization after changes to LP data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given perturbed data \((\widetilde A,\widetilde b,\widetilde c)\), a previous postsolved triple \((\widehat x,\widehat y,\widehat s)\), and \(\delta>0\), initialize \(x^0_i=\max\{\widehat x_i,\delta\}\), \(s^0_i=\max\{\widehat s_i,\delta\}\), and \(y^0=\widehat y\). At iteration \(k\), set \(\mu_k=(x^k)^{\mathsf T}s^k/n\) and solve
\[
\widetilde A\Delta x=\widetilde b-\widetilde A x^k,\quad \widetilde A^{\mathsf T}\Delta y+\Delta s=\widetilde c-\widetilde A^{\mathsf T}y^k-s^k,
\]
\[
S^k\Delta x+X^k\Delta s=\sigma_k\mu_k\mathbf1-X^ks^k.
\]
Choose the largest damped step preserving \(x^{k+1}>0\) and \(s^{k+1}>0\). Stop when prescribed primal-residual, dual-residual, and duality-gap tolerances hold; otherwise report the iteration limit. Map the final candidate through postsolve before release.

knowledge_statements.title: Solver-Status Reporting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate-bearing terminal statuses for the postsolved original-form linear program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\), a terminal status is certified only by objects expressed in the original model. An optimal status requires \(Ax=b\), \(A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c\), \(x\ge0\), \(s\ge0\), and \(c^{\mathsf T}x-b^{\mathsf T}y=0\). A primal-infeasible status requires a vector \(y\) satisfying \(A^{\mathsf T}y\ge0\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}y<0\). An unbounded-primal status requires a feasible point \(x^0\) satisfying \(Ax^0=b\) and \(x^0\ge0\), together with a ray \(d\) satisfying \(Ad=0\), \(d\ge0\), and \(c^{\mathsf T}d<0\). With finite tolerances, the report must instead identify the status as approximate and include scaled residuals, sign violations, and the duality gap. If no applicable certificate passes validation, the status is indeterminate rather than certified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solver statuses are backed by postsolved optimality, infeasibility, or unboundedness certificates. An unboundedness certificate includes both a feasible point and an improving recession direction. Tolerance-based outcomes disclose residuals, while failed validation yields an indeterminate status.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\).
All reported vectors have been mapped back to the original, unscaled model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A reported exact terminal status is independently checkable by the displayed equalities and inequalities; otherwise only an approximate or indeterminate status is justified.
